article_content: By James Tozer. PUBLISHED: 10:31 EST, 21 June 2012. | UPDATED: 04:38 EST, 22 June 2012. When keen vegetable grower Brian Caswell won the lottery, there was one thing money couldn’t buy: the perfect carrot crop. His £24.9 million EuroMillions fortune brought him a luxury farmhouse, a Range Rover in the garage, and new homes for his daughters. Yet, despite all this, his beloved allotment in Bolton, Greater Manchester, remained his true sanctuary. The 77-year-old grandfather won the jackpot three years ago and admitted at the time that his inability to grow successful carrots was one of his few regrets. 'I’ve been trying to grow carrots ever since I started on that plot—and I’ve never had any success,' he said. 'I’ve followed every instruction in the book, but never had a single harvest.' He vowed then that his newfound wealth wouldn’t make him abandon his plot. And he kept his word. With more time to devote to his hobby, he finally cracked the code: growing carrots in pots filled with fresh compost. 'I could never grow them before the win,' Caswell explained. 'Then I was given a tip: plant them in pots. You’re using fresh compost every time—and they always come up. That’s what I’m doing now, and it works.' His win has allowed other upgrades too: night vision cameras to observe wildlife on the allotment, and a helper to assist with maintenance. But he remains grounded. Caswell, formerly chairman of the Harpers Lane Allotment Society, traded his modest semi-detached home for a £1.25 million five-bedroom farmhouse three miles away. He also bought homes for his daughters, Helen, 51, and Angela, 47—each with land and stables. He grows plums, damsons, tomatoes, onions—and, of course, carrots. 'I don’t plant anything unless it gives me something back,' he says. 'I still have damson jam from last year.' Though his wealth has eased some burdens, it hasn’t changed his character. 'Long before the win, we always took a family trip once a year—with all ten of us. We still do,' he noted. 'If I’d been 40 when I won, maybe it would’ve changed me more—you’ve got a long life ahead. But at my age, I don’t have that privilege.' And yes—he still plays the lottery. 'As someone told me recently, I have as much chance as anybody else.'

La seva fortuna de 24,9 milions de lliures esterlines a l'EuroMillions li va portar una granja de luxe, un Range Rover al garatge i cases noves per a les seves filles. Tot i això, la seva adorada allotment a Bolton, Gran Manchester, va continuar sent el seu refugi verdader. L'avi de 77 anys va guanyar el premi màxim fa tres anys i va reconèixer que la seva incapacitat per créixer pastanagues amb èxit era un dels seus pocs regrets. 'He intentat créixer pastanagues des de que vaig començar en aquesta parcel·la, i mai he tingut cap èxit,' va dir. 'He seguit cada instrucció del llibre, però mai he tret ni una sola collita.' Va prometre llavors que la seva riquesa no el faria abandonar la seva parcel·la. I va mantenir la seva paraula. Amb més temps per dedicar-hi al seu passatemps, finalment va trobar la solució: créixer-les en macetes amb compost fresc. 'No podia créixer-les abans de guanyar,' va explicar Caswell. 'Després em van donar un consell: plantar-les en macetes. Estàs posant compost fresc cada vegada—i sempre surten. Això és el que faig ara, i funciona.' La seva sortida li ha permès altres millores també: càmeres de visió nocturna per observar la vida salvatge a l'lotment, i un ajudant per ajudar amb el manteniment. Però segueix sent humil. Caswell, ex president de la Societat d'Allotments Harpers Lane, va canviar la seva casa semidemolida per una granja de cinc habitacions de 1,25 milions de lliures situada a tres milles de distància. També va comprar cases per a les seves filles, Helen, de 51 anys, i Angela, de 47, cadascuna amb terra i estables. Cultiva prunes, damascos, tomàquets, cebes—i, per descomptat, pastanagues. 'No planto res que no em doni alguna cosa a canvi,' diu. 'Encara tinc marmalada de damascos de l'any passat.' Tot i que la seva riquesa ha facilitat algunes tasques, no ha canviat el seu caràcter. 'Abans de guanyar, sempre feiem un viatge familiar una vegada a l'any—with all ten of us. We still do,' va observar. 'Si hagués tingut 40 anys quan vaig guanyar, potser m'hauria canviat més—tens una vida llarga per davant. Però a la meva edat, no tinc aquest privilegi.' I sí—encara juga a la loteria. 'Com algú em va dir recentment, tinc tantes possibilitats com qualsevol altre.'

article_content: Taco Bell has unveiled its latest indulgent hybrid: the Quesarito — a meat-stuffed burrito wrapped in a cheesy quesadilla. The Mexican-inspired chain describes it as filled with seasoned beef, premium Latin rice, Chipotle sauce, and reduced-fat sour cream, all enclosed in a grilled quesadilla loaded with melted cheese. Starting June 9, the Quesarito will be permanently available at Taco Bell locations across the U.S., priced at $1.99 for seasoned beef, $2.79 for shredded chicken, and $2.99 for steak. According to Taco Bell’s Chief Marketing Officer, Chris Brandt, the Quesarito — which contains 620 calories (chicken), 640 (steak), and 650 (seasoned beef) — underwent extensive testing in Oklahoma and received strong consumer feedback. It has become the brand’s best-selling test item since the iconic Doritos Locos Tacos, which have sold over 825 million units since their March 2012 debut. Last month, Taco Bell publicly disclosed the composition of its seasoned beef, clarifying that while it contains USDA-inspected beef, the remaining 12% consists of water, oats, yeast, citric acid, Mexican spices, and other ingredients to maintain texture and flavor consistency. This transparency initiative follows the successful rollout of Taco Bell’s breakfast menu in March — the largest expansion in its 50-year history — featuring the Waffle Taco, a breakfast favorite with eggs, bacon, and syrup wrapped in a waffle. To further diversify its offerings, Taco Bell is preparing to launch U.S. Taco Co., a fast-casual restaurant in Huntington Beach, California. The concept features elevated tacos, fries, and shakes alongside alcoholic beverages, targeting food-savvy millennials seeking a more refined dining experience. Jeff Jenkins, Taco Bell’s Senior Brand Manager, described U.S. Taco Co. as a fusion of American-inspired flavors designed for the emerging 'edgy foodie' demographic. The restaurant is expected to open later this year, while the Quesarito hits menus nationwide this Monday.

Per diversificar encara més la seva oferta, Taco Bell prepara el llançament de U.S. Taco Co., un restaurant de servei ràpid i casual a Huntington Beach, Califòrnia. El concepte ofereix tacos, patates fregides i batuts de qualitat superior, acompanyats de begudes alcohòliques, dirigint-se a millennials amb gust per la cuina innovadora que busquen una experiència gastronòmica única. El restaurant s'espera que obri més endavant aquest any, mentre que el Quesarito arribarà als menús de tot el país aquest dilluns.

article_content: Hank Sheinkopf, a seasoned political strategist and former media advisor to President Bill Clinton, is questioning whether Caroline Kennedy is the right person to fill New York’s upcoming U.S. Senate seat. While media buzz and public fascination with the Kennedy name suggest she’s already been chosen, Sheinkopf argues that fame alone doesn’t qualify someone for public office. Kennedy, he notes, has never held elected office, hasn’t campaigned for the position, and has largely avoided commenting on major national crises — from the financial collapse and auto industry bailout to ongoing conflicts abroad. Sheinkopf points out that Governor David Paterson, who must appoint a replacement after Hillary Clinton steps down to join the Biden administration, is under pressure to pick someone who can win votes in 2010. With state revenues plummeting after Wall Street’s crash and public services at risk, voters need a representative who understands real economic pain — not just one who smiles for cameras at school events. Sheinkopf draws a stark contrast: in 1964, Robert Kennedy didn’t rely on his family name to win — he ran a vigorous, issue-driven campaign against incumbent Kenneth Keating. Caroline Kennedy, by contrast, has not even entered the race. Sheinkopf insists that if she truly wants the seat, she should step forward, declare her candidacy, and earn support through debate and policy — not through legacy. He warns that appointing her over qualified, experienced candidates risks alienating voters who believe in fairness and earned opportunity — especially working-class communities outside Manhattan’s glittering skyline.

Mentre que els mitjans i la fascinació pública amb el nom Kennedy suggerixen que ja ha estat nomenada, Sheinkopf argumenta que la fama sola no qualifica ningú per a un càrrec públic. Kennedy, assenyala ell, mai ha ocupat un càrrec electiu, no ha fet campanya per a la posició i ha evitat gairebé completament comentar les grans crisis nacionals — des de la caiguda financera i el rescat de l’indústria automobilística fins als conflictes en curs a l’estranger. article_content: A controversial plan that would have required unemployed individuals to apply for at least 40 jobs per month to receive the Newstart Allowance has been scrapped. The reversal on a key element of the Federal Government’s welfare reform came after sustained negative feedback. Prime Minister Tony Abbott defended the government’s decision, insisting he is 'fair dinkum' about listening to feedback. 'The only fair dinkum consultations are those that can and do result in some refinements—and where necessary, some changes,' he said. 'Consultation that can’t lead to any changes is meaningless.' The proposed doubling of job application requirements—from 20 to 40 per month—was widely criticized as punitive for job seekers and an administrative burden for employers. The government has now confirmed the original target of 20 applications per month will remain. Employment Minister Eric Abetz acknowledged the policy would have placed undue pressure on businesses and potentially devalued job applications. However, he maintained that seeking employment should be the full-time job of the unemployed and argued that applying for two jobs daily—morning and afternoon—was 'not too hard.' Greens Leader Christine Milne welcomed the reversal but urged the government to abandon its plan to require people under 30 to wait six months before claiming unemployment benefits—a policy scheduled to take effect in January 2015. St Vincent de Paul Society CEO Dr John Falzon criticized the government’s approach, saying, 'What we had hoped for was a jobs plan; what we have got instead is a bashing-the-young-unemployed plan.' He emphasized that structural issues in the labor market—not individual effort—are the root cause of unemployment. The government also plans to expand the Work for the Dole program: those under 30 will be required to complete 25 hours per week, while job seekers aged 30 to 50 must complete 15 hours per week. Dr Falzon added: 'You don’t help young people into work by forcing them to live below the poverty line—and you certainly don’t help them find a job by forcing them to rely on charity to survive.'

article_content: Many don’t realize that 'The Lorax' — Dr. Seuss’s environmental allegory — sparked strong backlash from the logging industry, leading them to commission a counter-narrative called 'The Truax.' In 2004, Seuss’s widow, Audrey Geisel, accepted his star on the Hollywood Walk of Fame. Originally, 'The Lorax' included a line referencing pollution in Lake Erie. Fourteen years after publication, the Ohio Sea Grant Program wrote to Theodore Geisel, sharing progress in cleaning the lake and urging him to remove the line. He agreed, and future editions omitted it. Seuss’s beloved phrases have often been appropriated for political causes. For example, 'A person's a person, no matter how small' from 'Horton Hears a Who!' became a slogan for anti-abortion groups. Though it’s unclear if Seuss intended this meaning, he personally threatened to sue any group using his words on promotional materials. His estate’s attorney, Karl ZoBell, confirms that Audrey Geisel strongly opposes using Seuss’s characters to promote external agendas. 'If I Ran the Zoo,' published in 1950, contains the first known printed use of the word 'nerd.' 'The Cat in the Hat' was born from a challenge: Seuss believed the standard reading primers — like Dick and Jane — were dull and ineffective. To prove he could make reading fun, he later accepted a bet from his editor, Bennett Cerf, to write a book using only 50 words. The result? 'Green Eggs and Ham' — crafted with precisely 50 unique words: a, am, and, anywhere, are, be, boat, box, car, could, dark, do, eat, eggs, fox, goat, good, green, ham, here, house, I, if, in, let, like, may, me, mouse, not, on, or, rain, Sam, say, see, so, thank, that, the, them, there, they, train, tree, try, will, with, would, you. Though many believe 'Marvin K. Mooney Will You Please Go Now!' was aimed at President Nixon, the book was published in March 1972 — two months before the Watergate scandal broke publicly. Production timelines make direct inspiration implausible. Still, Seuss sent a personalized copy to journalist Art Buchwald, crossing out 'Marvin K. Mooney' and replacing it with 'Richard M. Nixon' — a cheeky nod that Buchwald later published. 'Yertle the Turtle' is widely understood as a critique of Hitler, with Yertle’s tyranny mirroring fascist domination. Seuss himself confirmed this interpretation. Even so, Random House hesitated over one detail: Mack the turtle’s burp — the first in children’s literature. They relented, and the burp stayed. 'The Butter Battle Book' — a satirical take on the Cold War arms race — was briefly pulled from some school libraries in the 1980s due to its political themes. It pits the Yooks (butter-up eaters) against the Zooks (butter-down eaters), escalating to absurd weaponry until both sides stand poised to destroy each other… with the ending left unresolved. 'Oh, The Places You’ll Go!' — Seuss’s final book, published in 1990 — remains a staple graduation gift, selling roughly 300,000 copies annually. In the classic animated adaptation of 'How the Grinch Stole Christmas!', Boris Karloff voiced the Grinch and narrated. Seuss worried Karloff’s deep voice might scare children, so audio engineers lowered the pitch, giving the Grinch his iconic gravelly tone. Meanwhile, Tony the Tiger — real name Thurl Ravenscroft — sang 'You’re a Mean One, Mr. Grinch' without credit. To ensure recognition, Seuss personally wrote letters to major U.S. newspapers naming Ravenscroft as the singer.

El 2004, la vídua de Seuss, Audrey Geisel, va acceptar la seva estrella al Passeig de la Fama de Hollywood. Originalment, 'El Lorax' incloïa una frase que feia referència a la contaminació del llac Erie. Quatorze anys després de la publicació, el programa Ohio Sea Grant va escriure a Theodore Geisel, compartint els progrés en la neteja del llac i demanant-li que eliminés la frase. Ell va acceptar, i les edicions posteriors van ometre-la. Les frases estimades de Seuss han estat sovint apropades per causes polítiques. Per exemple, 'Una persona és una persona, independentment de com de petita sigui' de 'Horton escolta un Who!' es va convertir en un lema per a grups antiabortistes. Tot i que no és clar si Seuss ho va intencionar així, ell va amençar personalment amb una demanda contra qualsevol grup que utilitzés les seves paraules en material promocional. L'advocat de la seva família, Karl ZoBell, confirma que Audrey Geisel s'oposa fermament a utilitzar els personatges de Seuss per promoure agendas externes. 'Si jo fes el zoològic', publicat el 1950, conté l'ús imprès conegut més antic de la paraula 'nerd'. 'El Gat en el Sombrer' va néixer d'un repte: Seuss creia que els llibres d'aprenentatge estàndard — com Dick i Jane — eren avorrits i ineficaços. Per demostrar que podia fer que llegir fos divertit, va acceptar una aposta del seu editor, Bennett Cerf, per escriure un llibre amb només 50 paraules. El resultat? 'Ufs, ous verds i embotit' — creat amb exactament 50 paraules úniques: a, am, and, anywhere, are, be, boat, box, car, could, dark, do, eat, eggs, fox, goat, good, green, ham, here, house, I, if, in, let, like, may, me, mouse, not, on, or, rain, Sam, say, see, so, thank, that, the, them, there, they, train, tree, try, will, with, would, you. Tot i que molts creuen que 'Marvin K. Mooney Will You Please Go Now!' era un atac a Nixon, el llibre es va publicar el març de 1972 — dos mesos abans que l'esclat de Watergate es fes públic. Els plazos de producció fan implausible una inspiració directa. Tot i això, Seuss va enviar una còpia personalitzada al periodista Art Buchwald, tapant 'Marvin K. Mooney' i substituint-ho per 'Richard M. Nixon' — una broma que Buchwald va publicar posteriorment. 'Yertle the Turtle' es considera àmpliament una crítica a Hitler, amb la tirania de Yertle que reflecteix la dominació fascista. El mateix Seuss va confirmar aquesta interpretació. Tot i això, Random House va dubtar sobre un detall: el rutx de Mack, la tortuga — el primer en la literatura infantil. Van cedir, i el rutx va quedar. 'El Llibre de la Batalla de la Mantega' — una presa de pissarra de la carrera armamentística de la Guerra Freda — va ser retirat temporalment de algunes biblioteques escolars als anys 80 per les seves temàtiques polítiques. Enfronta els Yooks (que mengen el pa amb la mantega cap a dalt) contra els Zooks (que mengen el pa amb la mantega cap a baix), escalant fins a armes absurdes fins que tots dos costats queden preparats per destruir-se mutuament... amb l'final deixat sense resoldre. 'Oh, The Places You’ll Go!' — l'últim llibre de Seuss, publicat el 1990 — continua sent un regal estàndard per a graduats, venent aproximadament 300.000 còpies anualment. En l'adaptació animada clàssica de 'Com el Grinch va robar la Nadal!', Boris Karloff va fer la veu del Grinch i va narrar. Seuss va temer que la veu profunda de Karloff esporregués els nens, així que els tècnics d'àudio van reduir la freqüència, donant al Grinch el seu toc característic i ronc. Mentrestant, Tony the Tiger — el seu nom real, Thurl Ravenscroft — va cantar 'You’re a Mean One, Mr. Grinch' sense crèdit. Per assegurar-ne el reconeixement, Seuss va escriure cartes personals a grans diaris dels EUA nombrant Ravenscroft com a cantant.

article_content: The IRS admitted it lost the emails of six other IRS officials tied to a scheme targeting conservative organizations—along with those of former IRS official Lois Lerner—and concealed the loss for months, the House Ways and Means Committee revealed on Tuesday. In response, the House Oversight and Government Reform Committee issued broad subpoenas for hard drives, thumb drives, and other backup systems potentially used by Lerner and other IRS personnel. Ways and Means Chairman Dave Camp and Subcommittee Chair Charles Boustany stated that the IRS had known since February that it could no longer access Lerner’s emails and those of other key figures involved in the tea party targeting scandal—but failed to inform Congress. 'It appears the American people were misled, and the IRS attempted to cover up the convenient disappearance of critical documents in this investigation,' Camp and Boustany said in a press release. 'The plotlines in Hollywood are more believable than what we’re being told by this White House and the IRS.' The IRS’s Exempt Organizations Division is at the center of a years-long controversy involving intrusive screening of conservative groups seeking tax-exempt status starting in 2009. Hundreds of these applications were delayed or denied, while politically aligned liberal groups received swift approvals. On Friday, the IRS informed the committee that 28 months of Lois Lerner’s emails—spanning January 2009 to April 2010—were lost due to a computer crash and could not be recovered because records were not backed up on servers, tapes, or external drives. IRS policy explicitly requires that federal email records not be stored solely on the email system and must be archived in a separate electronic recordkeeping system. Additionally, employees are required to print and file hard copies of all federally recordable communications—including transmission metadata. According to the IRS, none of these protocols were followed. Lerner’s emails from January 2009 to April 2010 remain missing. The IRS now reports that emails belonging to Nikole Flax, Chief of Staff to then-Deputy Commissioner Steve Miller, are also missing. Flax made over a dozen visits to the White House between July 2010 and April 2013, according to Politico. Camp and Boustany called Flax’s visits suspicious and pledged further investigation: 'Who was she meeting with at the White House? What were they discussing? Was she reporting on the targeting—or receiving instructions? These questions remain unanswered—because, unsurprisingly, a few computers crashed.' IRS Commissioner John Koskinen will testify before two House committees next week to explain how such losses occurred despite robust federal data retention standards. Lerner retired with a full government pension and has declined to testify about her role in the scandal. Camp and Boustany rejected the IRS’s claim that the emails are irrecoverable, demanding President Obama fulfill his pledge to work 'hand in hand' with Congress. They requested all communications between Lerner and personnel in the White House, Treasury, DOJ, EPA, FEC, and OSHA from January 2009 to May 2011. This request followed interviews with IRS IT staff, who reportedly confirmed that budget and space constraints limited access to archival systems. They also noted that other executive agencies maintain independent archives of records now lost at the IRS. Rep. Darrell Issa, chair of the House Oversight Committee, demanded Koskinen appear in a rare evening hearing on June 23—just a day before his scheduled testimony before Ways and Means—to explain the loss. Issa accused the IRS of obstruction, citing broken promises to produce subpoenaed documents. Koskinen previously assured Congress in March that locating Lerner’s emails would take 'years' due to privacy reviews, and claimed they were 'stored somewhere' across 90,000 employees’ systems. He did not disclose the computer crash until later. Conservative commentators mocked the explanation: 'The NSA has the original files,' joked Capitol Hill writer Amanda Carpenter. Senator Ted Cruz retorted: 'What would the IRS say if we told them we couldn’t file taxes because of a computer crash?' Actor Pat Sajak tweeted: 'Weird. Hundreds of emails to & from someone named Lerner just showed up in my spam. Must be British. Lots of tea talk.'

En resposta, el Comitè de Supervisió i Reforma del Govern de la Cambra va emetre subpòenes amples per a discos durs, unitats USB i altres sistemes de còpia de seguretat potencialment utilitzats per Lerner i altre personal de l'IRS. El president del Comitè de Vies i Mitjans, Dave Camp, i el president del subcomitè de supervisió, Charles Boustany, van afirmar que l'IRS sabia des de febrer que ja no podia accedir als correus electrònics de Lerner i d'altres figures clau implicades en l'esquema de vigilància del moviment Tea Party, però no va informar el Congrés. 'Sembla que el poble americà va ser enganyat i que l'IRS va intentar tapar la desaparició convenient de documents crítics en aquesta investigació,' van dir Camp i Boustany en un comunicat de premsa. 'Les trames de Hollywood són més creïbles que allò que ens estan dient aquesta Casa Blanca i l'IRS.' La Divisió d'Organitzacions Exemptes de l'IRS és el centre d'una controvèrsia de molts anys que involucra la inspecció intrusiva de grups conservadors que demanaven l'estatus d'exempció fiscal a partir de 2009. Centenars d'aquestes sol·licituds van ser retardades o denegades, mentre que els grups liberals políticament alineats van rebre aprovacions ràpides. El divendres, l'IRS va informar el comitè que 28 mesos de correus electrònics de Lois Lerner —que cobreixen gener de 2009 a abril de 2010— van ser perduts a causa d'un col·lapse informàtic i no es podien recuperar perquè els registres no van ser copiats en servidors, cintes ni discos externs. La política de l'IRS exigeix explícitament que els correus electrònics federals no es guardin únicament en el sistema de correu electrònic i que cal arxivar-los en un sistema electrònic de registre separadament. A més, els empleats han de imprimir i archivar còpies en paper de totes les comunicacions subjectes a lleis federals de registre —inclòs el metadada de transmissió. Segons l'IRS, cap d'aquests protocols s'ha seguit. Els correus electrònics de Lerner de gener de 2009 a abril de 2010 continuen desapareguts. L'IRS ara informa que també falten els correus electrònics de Nikole Flax, cap de gabinet de l'antic vicesecretari Steve Miller. Flax va fer més de dotze visites a la Casa Blanca entre juliol de 2010 i abril de 2013, segons Politico. Camp i Boustany van considerar les visites de Flax com a sospitoses i van prometre una investigació addicional: 'Amb qui es reunia a la Casa Blanca? De què parlaven? Estava informant sobre l'objectiu o rebent ordres? Aquestes preguntes romanen sense resposta —perquè, sorpresa, sorpresa, alguns ordinadors van col·lapsar.' El comissari de l'IRS, John Koskinen, testificarà davant dos comitès de la Cambra la setmana que ve per explicar com es van produir aquestes pèrdues malgrat els estrictes estàndards federals de conservació de dades. Lerner es va jubilar amb una pensió completa del govern i ha rebutjat testificar sobre el seu paper en l'esquema. Camp i Boustany van rebutjar la reclamació de l'IRS de que els correus són irrecoverables, exigit que el president Obama compleixi la seva promesa de treballar 'de la mà' amb el Congrés. Van sol·licitar totes les comunicacions entre Lerner i personal de la Casa Blanca, el Departament del Trésor, el Departament de Justícia, la EPA, la FEC i l'OSHA entre gener de 2009 i maig de 2011. Aquesta sol·licitud va seguir entrevistes amb personal de TI de l'IRS, que van confirmar que les limitacions pressupostàries i d'espai van restringir l'accés als sistemes d'arxiu. També van assenyalar que altres agències executives mantenen arxius independents dels registres ara perduts a l'IRS. El representant Darrell Issa, president del Comitè de Supervisió de la Cambra, va exigir que Koskinen comparegués en una audiència nocturna rara el 23 de juny —un dia abans de la seva testimoniança programada davant Vies i Mitjans— per explicar la pèrdua. Issa va acusar l'IRS d'obstrucció, citant promeses incumplides de produir documents subpoeñats. Koskinen va assegurar anteriorment al Congrés a març que localitzar els correus de Lerner trigarà 'anys' degut a revisió de privacitat, i va afirmar que estaven 'emmagatzemats en algun lloc' entre els sistemes de 90.000 empleats. No va revelar el col·lapse informàtic fins després. Comentaristes conservadors van ridiculitzar l'explicació: 'La NSA té els fitxers originals,' va bromejar l'escriptora de Capitol Hill Amanda Carpenter. El senador republicà de Texas Ted Cruz va respondre: 'Què diria l'IRS si li diguéssim que no podem presentar la nostra declaració d'impostos perquè un ordinador es va trencar?' L'actor Pat Sajak va tuitejar: 'Estrany. Centenars de correus electrònics a i des de qualcú anomenat Lerner acaben de sortir al meu correu brossa. Ha de ser britànic. Molta parla de te.'

article_content: Manchester United’s struggles after clinching their 20th league title continued with a narrow 1-0 loss to Chelsea, leaving the Blues firmly in control of the race for the final Champions League spot. Juan Mata struck the decisive blow in the 86th minute — a moment that triggered chaos as United’s Rafael da Silva was sent off for lashing out at David Luiz. Replays showed Luiz smiling on the ground afterward, fueling accusations of simulation. It was United’s first red card of the season, meaning Rafael will miss the remainder of the Premier League campaign due to an automatic three-match suspension. Manager Alex Ferguson wasn’t holding back, claiming the referee was misled by Luiz’s dramatic reaction. 'He got elbowed twice,' Ferguson said, 'but when someone retaliates, they’re always the villain. Luiz sold it.' The defeat followed a 1-1 stalemate against Arsenal, and Ferguson admitted the team lacked energy, acknowledging Chelsea were the superior side on the day. 'We’ve had a long season,' he added. 'The big push came last week — today, we just didn’t have it.' Meanwhile, Mata’s goal was his 11th in the league and 19th across all competitions, pushing Chelsea one point ahead of Arsenal and three clear of Tottenham. A win over Spurs in midweek would likely seal European qualification, given Tottenham’s inferior goal difference. 'It’s a final for fourth place,' said Chelsea boss Rafael Benitez. 'We’re close, and winning is critical — even more so for them.' He also hinted Eden Hazard might return from a calf injury. On the other side of town, Everton’s chances of European football next season took a hit after a 0-0 draw with Liverpool. Manager David Moyes fumed after Sylvain Distin’s header was wrongly disallowed, arguing that Liverpool keeper Pepe Reina had collided with his player. 'It was a goal,' Moyes insisted. 'He ran into us, not the other way around.' With the result, Everton now trail Tottenham by five points despite having played an extra game. Liverpool, missing suspended star Luis Suarez, remained in seventh place.

article_content: A Marine is under investigation for potential legal or administrative action after a video this week showed him engaging in a profanity-laced road rage incident against another motorist at Camp Pendleton, California, a Marine spokesman said Friday. The Marine, whose name, rank, and unit have not been disclosed, was cited for communicating a threat during the incident—but as of Friday, no formal charges had been filed, according to Sgt. Christopher Duncan, a spokesperson for Camp Pendleton. The viral video depicts a young man yelling outside a truck while aggressively striking its body with his hands and feet. The driver inside remains calm, windows rolled up. A female passenger records the event. The video’s caption claims the altercation began after an accident in which the Marine’s vehicle was struck—allegedly because he had slammed on his brakes multiple times. The truck contained a civilian driver and his passenger, described as 'a fellow Marine in a wheelchair.' According to CNN affiliate KGTV, the driver is the brother and caregiver of the female Marine, who is paralyzed from the waist down. The cited Marine was released into the custody of his unit. 'Any further legal proceedings regarding this incident will be determined by his unit, which is still gathering information,' Duncan stated. 'I have no timeline for when potential legal or administrative actions might occur,' Duncan added. 'This individual’s behavior does not meet the standards expected of Marines and has drawn the attention of senior base leadership.' The incident occurred on Monday at approximately 2 p.m., Duncan confirmed.

article_content: One of the most talked-about moments from last night’s final presidential debate was President Barack Obama’s sarcastic comparison of Mitt Romney’s foreign policy views to the era of 'horses and bayonets.' The quip quickly spread across social media, intended to depict Romney as disconnected from modern military realities. But the comment inadvertently drew attention to a surprising truth: both bayonets and horses remain part of today’s U.S. military arsenal. The exchange followed Romney’s criticism that the U.S. Navy had shrunk to its smallest size since 1917. Obama responded: 'We also have fewer horses and bayonets, because the nature of our military’s changed. We have these things called aircraft carriers, where planes land on them. We have these ships that go underwater — nuclear submarines. So the question isn’t a game of Battleship, where we’re just counting ships.' While the line became a viral meme among Obama supporters, it overlooked enduring military practices. The U.S. Marine Corps still issues the OKC-3S bayonet — a blade designed for the M16 rifle — and trains recruits in its use for close-quarters combat. The U.S. Army included bayonet training in basic drills until 2010. Horses, too, haven’t vanished from the battlefield. During the 2001 U.S.-led invasion of Afghanistan, special operations troops rode alongside Northern Alliance fighters through rugged terrain where vehicles couldn’t operate. Though unconventional, the tactic proved effective — even if one soldier had to ride with a broken back after his horse collapsed. Though modern warfare relies heavily on drones, missiles, and cyber tools, bayonets serve dual roles: as combat weapons and as practical multi-use knives in field deployments. In 2008, a British soldier earned the Military Cross after killing a Taliban fighter with his bayonet — citing its boost to troop morale. Neither horses nor bayonets dominate 21st-century combat as they did in WWI. But to claim they’ve been fully abandoned? That’s simply inaccurate.

Ni els cavalls ni les badies dominen la guerra del segle XXI com ho feien en la I Guerra Mundial. Però afirmar que han estat totalment abandonades? És simplement incorrecte.

article_content: On 7 February 2013, Jane Harding, a 52-year-old hairdresser and mother from Marden, Herefordshire, was killed when her car was struck by a passenger train at the Moreton-on-Lugg level crossing. The train, traveling at 61 mph, dragged the vehicle 150 yards along the tracks. The accident occurred after signalman Adrian Maund, 43, mistakenly raised the crossing barriers. He was distracted by a phone call from a local farmer requesting clearance to guide sheep across a nearby crossing. Believing the train had already passed, Maund lowered the barriers — only realizing his error moments later when he saw the train approaching at 80 mph around a bend. Maund frantically attempted to lower the barriers and alter the signal, but it was too late. The train collided with the Hardings’ Volkswagen Touareg and a second vehicle, a Vauxhall Astra. Mark Harding, Jane’s husband and the driver, survived with shoulder and pelvic injuries. Carol-Anne Thornewell and her 12-year-old daughter, occupants of the Astra, escaped unharmed. At Birmingham Crown Court, prosecutor Philip Mott QC argued that the tragedy could have been prevented. A £40,000 safety device known as an approach-locking system — capable of preventing signal changes while a train is approaching — had been proposed during 2009 upgrade works at the crossing but was rejected by Network Rail due to cost concerns. Mott emphasized that such systems have existed since the 1960s and questioned whether financial savings were prioritized over human life. Maund has pleaded not guilty to charges of failing to take reasonable care for the safety of railway users. Network Rail has also denied a separate charge of breaching its duty of care. Both face potential fines and, in Maund’s case, up to two years in prison. The trial, expected to last three weeks, continues.

article_content: Police in Massachusetts have arrested a 50-year-old French man, Edmund Alexandre of Paris, after he caused a disturbance aboard American Airlines Flight 62, en route from Miami to Paris. The flight was diverted to Boston’s Logan International Airport on Wednesday night after Alexandre became unruly. A federal air marshal subdued him mid-air, and state police took him into custody upon landing around 10 p.m. Alexandre has been charged with interfering with a flight crew. Due to a pre-existing medical condition, he was transported to Massachusetts General Hospital for observation and treatment. He will be arraigned at East Boston District Court once doctors determine he is medically fit. It remains unclear whether he has legal representation.

article_content: Egyptian President Mohamed Morsy met with Sudanese President Omar al-Bashir in Cairo on Sunday, defying international pressure to arrest the wanted leader. The International Criminal Court (ICC) has issued arrest warrants for al-Bashir on 10 counts of genocide and crimes against humanity, accusing him of orchestrating violence against African tribes in Darfur — including mass killings, rape, and forced displacement. Despite appeals from human rights group Amnesty International to detain al-Bashir during his visit, Egypt declined, citing its non-membership in the ICC and adherence to the African Union’s policy of non-cooperation with the tribunal. Morsy’s spokesperson, Yasser Ali, confirmed that discussions between the two leaders covered regional security, Nile River water rights, livestock imports, and industrial development. Amnesty International criticized Egypt’s decision, warning that hosting al-Bashir could turn the country into 'a safe haven for alleged perpetrators of genocide.' The group highlighted a contradiction between Morsy’s earlier pledge to uphold humanitarian values and his decision to meet with a leader accused of atrocities. The controversy echoes a similar situation in 2012, when Malawi withdrew from hosting an African Union summit after refusing to allow al-Bashir’s attendance due to its obligations under the Rome Statute. CNN’s Amir Ahmed contributed to this report.

El portaveu de Morsy, Yasser Ali, va confirmar que les discussions entre els dos líders van cobrir la seguretat regional, els drets a l'aigua del Nil, les importacions de bestiar i el desenvolupament industrial. article_content: Allison Baden-Clay’s spirit lives on through her three daughters — now 13, 10, and 7 — who are slowly rebuilding their lives with the unwavering support of their extended family. In her first interview since Gerard Baden-Clay was convicted of her murder, sister Vanessa Fowler shared how the girls are finding joy in everyday moments: excelling in ballet, stepping into leadership roles at school, and forming friendships. Though they still carry deep grief, counselors are helping them navigate their emotions, and the girls often speak about their mother with love. Vanessa emphasized that Allison would be proud of how they’re growing — kind, resilient, and full of life, just like she was. With their maternal grandparents, Geoff and Priscilla Dickie, as their primary caregivers, the girls are surrounded by stability and affection. The family acknowledges the pain won’t vanish overnight, but they’re committed to honoring Allison’s legacy by giving her daughters every opportunity to thrive — especially through education and emotional support. While Gerard Baden-Clay continues to deny responsibility, the court found overwhelming evidence of his infidelities and financial stress as motives, leading to a life sentence. For the family, justice has been served, but no verdict can replace the mother they lost.

article_content: This year’s Glorious Goodwood Magnolia Cup — a celebrity charity horse race — features an unexpected twist: jockey outfits designed by world-renowned fashion icons. Among them are Sarah Burton, famed for designing the Duchess of Cambridge’s wedding dress, and Vivienne Westwood, whose bold aesthetic has shaped modern fashion. Leading the pack is model Edie Campbell, last year’s Magnolia Cup winner and Ladies Day Ambassador. A close friend of Cara Delevingne, Edie is returning to defend her title, supported by a star-studded field including model Tricia Simonon, jeweler Philippa Holland, and Sunday Times writer Krissi Murison. The racing silks, crafted exclusively for the event, were created by a roster of elite designers: Bella Freud, Beulah, Jasmine Guinness, Frost French, and Kate Halfpenny. Sarah Burton’s design remains under wraps, adding anticipation to the grand unveiling. Sponsored by jewelry designer Theo Fennell, the race aims to raise funds for two vital charities: The Reading Agency and Best Beginnings. Fennell expressed pride in his role as Official Presenting Partner and in designing the race trophies. Edie Campbell, 24, rose to fame through a landmark Burberry campaign alongside Kate Moss and has since walked for Christian Dior, Marc Jacobs, Karl Lagerfeld, Lanvin, Alexander McQueen, and Louis Vuitton. She notably closed Chanel’s SS12 couture show as the bride — one of the most prestigious roles in fashion. Though her training hasn’t officially begun, Edie joked about her upcoming regimen: 'Lots of riding out-of-control racehorses at 7am, surrounded by tiny men on big horses.' Her enthusiasm underscores the blend of glamour, grit, and goodwill that defines this unique event.

article_content: Spanish police have uncovered and disrupted what officials describe as one of the most technically advanced terror plots in recent European history. The suspected cell, allegedly connected to al Qaeda, targeted multiple high-visibility locations — including a popular shopping center in Gibraltar and a joint U.S.-Spanish military base in Rota. Their method? Using small drones and motorized paragliders to drop explosives, a tactic previously seen in U.S. plots but never before attempted in Europe with this level of preparation. At the center of the operation was Cengiz Yalcin, a Turkish national living in Spain with his Moroccan wife. Working as an engineer in Gibraltar, Yalcin reportedly collected aerial imagery of the shopping mall and tested a 3-meter remote-controlled plane capable of carrying explosive packages. Surveillance footage captured him celebrating after successfully dropping two payloads mid-flight. Authorities also found paragliding equipment and a Russian-language manual in the suspects’ possession, suggesting they were training to use these devices for low-altitude attacks. The two suspected operatives, Eldar Magomedov and Muhammad Adamov, are former Russian special forces soldiers with extensive militant training in Afghanistan and Pakistan. Magomedov, a sniper and poison expert, allegedly spent years operating in Dagestan and Waziristan. Adamov was trained in bomb-making and may have been involved in a recent Moscow bombing. Both were arrested on a bus headed toward France, where French intelligence had been monitoring their communications — even intercepting a conversation in which they called Spain ‘easier’ for acquiring explosives. Though French authorities warned Spain months in advance, judicial delays meant police couldn’t immediately search Yalcin’s home. When they finally did, his wife greeted him with, 'Don’t worry, honey, I cleaned it all.' Investigators detected a heavy bleach odor — a likely attempt to destroy evidence. Dog teams later indicated more explosives had been hidden than were recovered. International cooperation was vital: Russian agencies confirmed identities, British intel tracked movements, and U.S. officials provided background. Experts warn this case underscores how terror networks adapt — using civilian tech like drones and hobbyist gear to bypass traditional security. With the Olympics looming, authorities fear the timing was intentional to maximize global shock value.

El seu mètode? Utilitzar drons petits i parapentes motoritzats per deixar caure explosius, una tècnica vista abans en atacs als EUA però mai abans intentada a Europa amb aquest nivell de preparació. Al centre de l'operació hi havia Cengiz Yalcin, un nacional turc que vivia a Espanya amb la seva dona marroquina. Els dos sospitosos, Eldar Magomedov i Muhammad Adamov, són exsoldats de les forces especials russes amb extensa formació militar a Afganistan i Pakistan. Ambdós van ser arrestats en un autobús que anava cap a França, on la intel·ligència francesa havia estat monitorant les seves comunicacions — fins i tot interceptant una conversa en què van qualificar Espanya com 'més fàcil' per obtenir explosius. Tot i que les autoritats franceses van advertir Espanya fa mesos, retards judicials van fer que la policia no pogués cercar immediatament la casa de Yalcin. Els experts avisen que aquest cas destaca com les xarxes terroristes s'adaptan — utilitzant tecnologia civil com drons i material de passatemps per evadir la seguretat tradicional. Amb els Jocs Olímpics a l'horitzó, les autoritats temen que el moment fos intencionat per maximitzar el xoc global.

article_content: Chelsea midfielder Nathaniel Chalobah is exploring a potential loan move to French club Bordeaux. He returned to Chelsea last week following a disappointing loan spell at Burnley, where he made only four appearances. Despite being highly regarded within the club, the 20-year-old has yet to make his first-team debut for Chelsea. Manager Jose Mourinho is keen for Chalobah to secure a temporary move to a club where he can play regular first-team football for the remainder of the season. Chalobah has previously gained Championship experience through loan stints at Middlesbrough, Nottingham Forest, and Watford over the past two seasons. He has earned 21 caps for the England Under-21 team, including appearances in friendlies against Portugal, and played in Premier League matches for West Brom during his loan in September. Meanwhile, Bordeaux president Jean-Louis Triaud is pushing for a swift decision from Arsenal regarding a potential loan for striker Yaya Sanogo. With interest from Crystal Palace, Aston Villa, Swansea, Stoke, and Everton, Sanogo remains a sought-after asset. However, Triaud insists Sanogo has expressed a clear preference for Bordeaux: 'He has told his manager Arsène Wenger he wants to come here. We are going all in on this target. We need an answer by Tuesday or Wednesday at the latest.' Sanogo, who celebrated a goal against Dortmund in the Champions League last November, is one of several young forwards Arsenal may look to loan out this January.

article_content: LONDON: More than 100 British citizens have been evacuated from Gaza through the Rafah crossing, with the UK government urging its immediate reopening to facilitate further departures, Deputy Prime Minister Oliver Dowden said on Sunday. The crossing, which opened for a limited three-day window earlier this week under a Qatari-brokered agreement, allowed foreign nationals, their dependents, and some injured Palestinians to exit the enclave. 'Over 100 UK nationals successfully crossed into Egypt via Rafah,' Dowden told the BBC. 'It is deeply disappointing that the crossing closed yesterday. We are in close contact with all parties and remain hopeful it will reopen today, enabling more Britons to leave.' While the UK has called for humanitarian pauses in Israel’s military operations in Gaza, it has not demanded a full ceasefire, affirming Israel’s right to defend itself after Hamas carried out the deadliest attack on Jews since the Holocaust on October 7. At least 12 Britons died in that assault, and Dowden confirmed three others remain unaccounted for — though he could not confirm if they had been taken hostage. Responding to comments by Home Secretary Suella Braverman labeling pro-Palestinian protests in London as 'hate marches,' Dowden acknowledged that some chants contained hateful rhetoric, particularly those denying Israel’s right to exist. 'Those attending these marches must ask themselves: are they standing beside those promoting hatred?' he said. He added he has 'grave concerns' about holding additional demonstrations next weekend, coinciding with Armistice Day commemorations marking the end of World War I.

El passatge, que es va obrir durant una finestra limitada de tres dies a l'inici d’aquesta setmana sota un acord mediador de Qatar, va permetre que nacionals estrangers, els seus familiars i alguns palestins ferits sortissin de l’enclavament. 'Més de 100 nacionals del Regne Unit van travessar amb èxit cap a Egipte mitjançant Rafah,' va dir Dowden a la BBC. 'És profundament decebedor que el passatge s’hagi tancat ahir. Estem en contacte estret amb totes les parts i esperem que es torni a obrir avui, permetent que més britànics surtin.' Mentre el Regne Unit ha demanat pauses humanitàries en les operacions militars d’Israel a Gaza, no ha exigit un alto el foc total, afirmando el dret d’Israel a defensar-se després que Hamas realitzés l’atac més mortífer contra jueus des de l’Holocaust el 7 d’octubre. Almenys 12 britànics van morir en aquest atac, i Dowden va confirmar que tres altres continuen sense localitzar — encara que no va poder confirmar si havien estat presos com a ostatges. En resposta als comentaris de la secretària d’Interior Suella Braverman, que van etiquetar les manifestacions pro-palestines a Londres com a 'marxes d’odi', Dowden va reconèixer que alguns crits contenien retòrica odiosa, especialment aquells que neguen el dret d’Israel a existir. 'Els que assisteixen a aquestes marxes han de preguntar-se: estan al costat de qui predica l’odi?', va dir. Va afegir que té 'grans preocupacions' sobre la conveniència de celebrar més manifestacions el proper cap de setmana, quan també es commemora el Dia de l’Armistici, l’aniversari de la fi de la Primera Guerra Mundial.

article_content: A 23-year-old woman from New Jersey died during a United Airlines flight from London Heathrow to Newark Liberty International Airport on Monday night. She was traveling alone when she was found unconscious mid-air. A passenger who was a physician attempted to resuscitate her, but she was pronounced dead at 1:30 a.m. GMT (8:30 p.m. EST). When Flight 115 landed at Newark at approximately 9:45 p.m. EST, police and a medical examiner were waiting. According to Port Authority spokesman Joe Pentangelo, the woman had pre-existing medical conditions, which were not contagious and posed no risk to other passengers. No quarantine measures were enacted on the aircraft or the body upon landing. Authorities believe she passed away from natural causes, though an autopsy is pending. United Airlines confirmed the incident in a statement, offering condolences to the family and citing privacy concerns as the reason for declining further comment. The woman’s identity has not been released, and the official cause of death remains under investigation.

article_content: A senior pediatric cardiac surgeon at Leeds Children’s Hospital has voluntarily ceased performing operations while concerns about aspects of his surgical practice are investigated. The hospital, already slated to shut down its pediatric cardiac unit as part of a nationwide NHS reorganization, has declined to identify the surgeon — one of only four in the department — citing employer obligations to protect staff privacy. The decision follows years of scrutiny. In 2008, the Care Quality Commission reported 20 excess deaths among pediatric heart patients at Leeds over an eight-year period. Last year, the Children’s Heart Federation raised alarms, alleging some infants were sent home to die, prompting calls for an independent inquiry. Hospital officials insist the current review is unrelated to overall mortality statistics or the broader debate over relocating services. However, they acknowledged the surgeon had previously been restricted from performing certain procedures. Leeds is one of three pediatric heart centers targeted for closure following the landmark Bristol heart scandal of the 1990s, in which 35 infants died and many others suffered brain damage. That tragedy transformed UK cardiac care protocols, leading to calls for centralized, high-volume centers to improve outcomes. Despite a recent High Court ruling finding flaws in the NHS’s public consultation process, the government remains committed to closing Leeds and consolidating services in Newcastle. Campaigners argue that emotional connections and local success stories justify maintaining the unit, while clinical experts warn that fragmented care puts children at risk. A former adviser to Health Secretary Andrew Lansley stated: 'Leeds ranked lowest in clinical outcomes during national evaluations. While families’ attachment to local care is understandable, the priority must be the best possible outcomes for every child — even if that means traveling farther.' Medical leaders point to Oxford’s 2010 response — halting all pediatric heart surgery amid safety concerns — as a model for decisive action. 'We cannot afford another Bristol,' warned one pediatric cardiologist. 'Safety must come before sentiment.'

article_content: England’s bold experiment of shifting Manu Tuilagi from center to wing appears unlikely to continue after a lackluster performance in Dunedin. A week after dominating midfield with explosive carries, Tuilagi looked out of place on the flank — missing the pace to finish breaks and struggling to cope with high kicks behind him. Though he helped set up Chris Ashton’s third try with a clever back-handed offload and made six tackles — three more than in the previous match — his overall impact was muted. He completed only 10 runs, down from 13 in the first Test, and hesitated whenever the ball was kicked into his space. One telling moment came just before halftime: Tuilagi broke free down the right wing but was easily caught from behind, highlighting his inability to outrun elite defenders. The All Blacks repeatedly targeted him defensively, forcing England’s fullback and wingers into panicked recoveries every time a kick landed behind him. Coach Stuart Lancaster acknowledged the mixed results, praising the team for scoring three tries against New Zealand but refusing to commit to repeating the experiment until a full review next Wednesday. Ultimately, while Tuilagi’s effort and work rate were commendable, the evidence suggests he remains a force best unleashed in the heart of the backline — not out wide.

article_content: As the 2014 Scottish independence referendum nears, a wave of high-profile voices is urging voters to keep Scotland within the United Kingdom — including none other than Kermit the Frog. In a playful yet pointed intervention, the beloved Muppet told The Big Issue that he fully supports staying united, citing deep cultural ties forged through decades of filming The Muppet Show in Britain. 'We love the UK,' Kermit said. 'You folks even get Fozzie’s jokes — and that’s saying something.' But there’s a twist: Kermit also revealed that his longtime partner, Miss Piggy, is ready to step into royal duties if Scotland chooses independence. 'She’s willing to serve as Queen,' he quipped. 'Better lock up your castles.' The remark, laced with humor, underscores the emotional and symbolic weight of the monarchy in the debate. This isn't the first celebrity intervention. David Bowie, via model Kate Moss at the Brit Awards, implored Scots to 'stay with us.' Rod Stewart and actor John Barrowman echoed similar sentiments, emphasizing unity. Even comedian Janette Tough, known as Jimmy Krankie, bluntly declared, 'Alex Salmond can sod off.' Meanwhile, the SNP faces internal tension. While official party policy holds that the monarchy would continue post-independence, ministers like Kenny MacAskill insist the people should decide whether Scotland becomes a republic. Many within the party, however, are openly republican. Adding a surreal twist, Danny Alexander — the UK Treasury’s Chief Secretary and a vocal opponent of independence — has long been likened to Beaker, the nervous Muppet sidekick. Alexander himself joked about the resemblance on Twitter, saying Beaker agrees with Kermit: 'Scotland is #BetterTogether.' Downing Street declined to comment on whether the UK government influenced these endorsements, deflecting questions with a cheeky: 'Are you suggesting someone’s pulling the strings?' But with stars, politicians, and Muppets all aligning against separation, the cultural tide appears firmly unionist.

article_content: Arnold Schwarzenegger has denied responsibility for exposing prisoners to Valley Fever, a debilitating fungal disease, during his time as California’s governor. He is among several officials named in lawsuits filed by dozens of current and former inmates who claim they contracted the illness while incarcerated at prisons in central California. Valley Fever, caused by inhaling spores from a soil-borne fungus endemic to arid regions like the Central Valley, can lead to severe complications including skin lesions, pneumonia, and even brain damage. Inmates allege that prison authorities were aware of the risks — including documented outbreaks — yet failed to take basic protective measures recommended by medical experts. In court filings, Schwarzenegger argues he is not personally liable, noting that prison operations and health policies fell under the jurisdiction of other state agencies. He points to a public press conference he held to address the issue as evidence of his awareness and engagement. The National Institute for Occupational Safety and Health (NIOSH) confirmed 103 illnesses and three deaths among prison staff between January 2009 and mid-2012 at Avenal and Pleasant Valley prisons. Infection rates among employees were far higher than in the surrounding communities — 511 cases per 100,000 at Avenal compared to 110 per 100,000 in Kings County. In response to the crisis, a federal judge ordered the transfer of nearly 2,600 inmates deemed especially vulnerable to the fungus. At the time of the study, Pleasant Valley housed over 3,300 inmates and 1,300 staff; Avenal held more than 4,500 inmates and 1,500 staff. Current California Governor Jerry Brown is also named in the lawsuit. The state requested the NIOSH investigation after nearly three dozen inmate deaths and hundreds of hospitalizations were linked to the fungus.

article_content: A groundbreaking clinical trial has shown that gradual exposure to peanut protein under the tongue may help people with severe peanut allergies build tolerance — though it’s not yet a cure. Researchers from the University of North Carolina and National Jewish Health tested this method, called sublingual immunotherapy, on 40 participants aged 12 to 37. Over nearly a year, those receiving daily doses of a peanut powder solution could safely consume up to nearly a gram of peanut protein by week 68 — a massive jump from their initial tolerance of just a few milligrams. In contrast, only 15% of those given a placebo showed similar improvement. While 70% of the treatment group became ‘responders,’ meaning they could handle at least ten times their original threshold, experts stress this therapy must only be administered in controlled medical settings. Though most doses caused no serious reactions, and 95% were symptom-free when minor mouth/throat sensations were ignored, the risks of self-experimentation remain extreme. Currently, avoiding peanuts and carrying an epinephrine pen are the only safeguards for the estimated 1 in 100 Americans and Brits with this allergy. The findings, published in the Journal of Allergy and Clinical Immunology, offer real hope — but not a do-it-yourself solution.

Investigadors de la Universitat de Carolina del Nord i el National Jewish Health van provar aquest mètode, anomenat immunoteràpia sublingual, en 40 participants entre 12 i 37 anys. Durant gairebé un any, aquells que rebien dosis diàries d'una solució amb pols de cacau podien consumir de forma segura fins a gairebé un gram de proteïna de cacau a la setmana 68 — un salt enormement significatiu des del seu nivell inicial de tolerància de només uns pocs mil·ligrams. En canvi, només el 15% dels que rebien un placebo van mostrar millora similar. Mentre que el 70% del grup de tractament es va convertir en 'responents', cosa que vol dir que podien suportar almenys deu vegades el seu llindar original, els experts subratllen que aquesta teràpia només s'ha de administrar en entorns mèdics controlats. Encara que la majoria de les dosis no van causar reaccions serioses, i el 95% van ser sense símptomes quan es van ignorar les sensacions lleus a la boca i la gola, els riscos de l'autotratament segueixen sent extrems. Actualment, evitar els cacaus i portar un plomall d'epinefrina són les úniques proteccions per a l'estimada 1 de cada 100 persones als EUA i el Regne Unit amb aquesta al·lèrgia. Els resultats, publicats al Journal of Allergy and Clinical Immunology, ofereixen esperança real — però no una solució feta a casa.

article_content: Actor-turned-director Deepak Tijori has accused filmmaker Mohit Suri of betraying him during Tijori’s transition into film direction. He alleges that Suri took an idea Tijori presented to producer Mahesh Bhatt—and to this day, has never acknowledged doing so. The film in question is Suri’s directorial debut, Zeher (2005). Tijori claims the concept was originally his, inspired by the 2003 Denzel Washington film Out of Time. In an interview with Bollywood Thikana, Tijori recounted: 'I wanted to work with Mahesh Bhatt. I went to narrate the film to him while he was on the treadmill. He listened for about 15–20 minutes and then said, 'I didn't enjoy it.' Forget it.' Tijori said he later met Suri outside Bhatt’s room and urged him to convince Bhatt to reconsider. Four days later, however, Anurag Basu contacted Tijori and revealed that Bhatt had liked Out of Time and decided to launch Suri with the same concept. Reacting to this, Tijori said: 'I felt so much anger—I thought of the Bhatts as family. This is my second career, my life. The first betrayal of my second career, and such a huge one. Since then, until today, he has never come to me and admitted he betrayed me this way.' He added: 'Zeher was his first film. It was my idea. But if he had just called me once, said, 'I used your idea,' what difference would it have made? I was working with Udita at Fox—I wanted to tell her, 'You’re having an affair with that guy.' But eventually, they got married and are happy. I’m happy for them. I just feel… this.' Mohit Suri is married to Udita Goswami, who starred in Zeher. The film, produced by Mahesh Bhatt, also features Emraan Hashmi and Shamita Shetty. It is loosely based on Out of Time.

article_content: Original Nazi Christmas decorations used by the SS have sparked widespread outrage after appearing on the Czech online auction site Aukro. The four glass baubles, described as 'fancy,' are red with a white circle and a centrally painted Nazi swastika. The seller, who identifies as 'Anti95,' claims they are authentic decorations used by SS units more than 70 years ago and are being offered at a starting price of £59. He states they are made of blown glass, undamaged, in original colors, and in good condition, calling them 'very precious pieces.' He adds that the sale is intended solely for collecting purposes. The decorations have provoked fury across the Czech Republic, a nation annexed by Nazi Germany in 1938 and not liberated until 1945. On the auction site’s Facebook page, Jana Bodinkova commented, 'It makes me sick. My granddad would cry if he saw this. It is incredible that we have something like this here now.' Vaclav Ceska, 59, from Prague, said, 'This is absolutely disgraceful. My grandparents fought in the resistance against the Nazis and remember the atrocities committed by the SS.' Jozsef Helmeczy posted: 'Are you kidding me? I would forbid it.' In response to criticism, the seller declared: 'I am not a member of any movement aimed at suppressing human rights and freedoms or any movement that supports national, racial, or class hatred toward other groups of people. I do not support movements like the SS.' Yet critics argue that preserving such items glorifies perpetrators who tortured and murdered millions while celebrating holidays.

Les decoracions han provocat una gran indignació a la República Txeca, una nació annexionada per la Alemanya nazi el 1938 i no lliurada fins al 1945. A la pàgina de Facebook del lloc d'intercanvi, Jana Bodinkova va comentar: 'Em fa malalda. El meu avi ploraria si ho veiés. És increïble que tinguem alguna cosa així ara.' Vaclav Ceska, de 59 anys, de Praga, va dir: 'És absolutament vergonyós. Els meus avis van lluitar a la resistència contra els nazis i recorden les atrocitats cometudes per les SS.' En resposta a les crítiques, el venedor va declarar: 'No soc membre de cap moviment orientat a suprimir els drets humans i les llibertats o cap moviment que suporti l'odi nacional, racial o de classe cap a altres grups de persones. article_content: Masoud Rasab, 38, is accused of orchestrating a network of sham marriages designed to help four Pakistani men obtain UK residency visas. In court, prosecutors revealed that brides were given 'crib sheets' listing fabricated personal details about their husbands—including height, weight, shoe size, how they supposedly met, and even the frequency of their intimate encounters. The alleged scheme, centered in Nottingham, Leicester, and Hertfordshire, involved British women being paid up to £7,000 each to marry men they had never met. Several brides lived more than 150 miles away from their spouses, claimed unemployment benefits as single women, and in one case, had to text her husband just to learn their shared address. When one woman tried to withdraw from the plan, she and her children received threatening messages. Another bride, Alisha Mahmood, was found with detailed notes about her husband Muhammad Ishaque’s home—down to the color of the walls and carpets—despite having married him only in June 2012. Prosecutor Christopher Smith told jurors the marriages were 'less about passion and more about profit.' He emphasized that UK immigration law allows foreign nationals to settle if they marry a British citizen—but this system was exploited for financial gain. The first marriage, in January 2010, linked Gul Khatab, a Pakistani student in Sheffield, with Tracey Caulstock, a 48-year-old security guard from Hertfordshire. Though legally listed as cohabiting, Khatab lived and worked in Sheffield, while Caulstock received £7,000. In another case, Sabrina Khan, 29, received nearly £2,000 from her husband Umair Hussain, whose student visa expired in 2011. Messages on her phone revealed she was in a romantic relationship with another man within months of the wedding and had to ask where her husband lived. Rasab allegedly ran this operation for nearly four years until July last year. Alisha Mahmood, 21, also acted as a recruiter, earning £250 for each bride she brought in—including Keeley Cox, who has already pleaded guilty. Tahir Siddique, 41, is accused of allowing his address to be used in the fraud. All six defendants on trial deny conspiring to breach immigration law. The trial continues at Sheffield Crown Court.

L'esquema presunt, centrat a Nottingham, Leicester i Hertfordshire, va implicar dones britàniques pagades fins a 7.000 lliures cada una per casar-se amb homes que mai havien vist. Algunes noves vivien a més de 240 quilòmetres dels seus marits, reclamaven prestacions per desocupació com a dones solteres i, en un cas, van haver d'escriure un missatge al seu marit només per saber la seva adreça compartida. El fiscal Christopher Smith va dir als jurats que els matrimonis eren 'menys sobre passió i més sobre beneficis.' Va enfatitzar que la llei d'immigració del Regne Unit permet als nacionals estrangers residir si es casen amb un ciutadà britànic, però aquest sistema va ser explotat per guanys financers. El primer matrimoni, el gener de 2010, va unir Gul Khatab, un estudiant pakistanès a Sheffield, amb Tracey Caulstock, una guarda de seguretat de 48 anys de Hertfordshire. El judici continua al Tribunal de la Corona de Sheffield.

article_content: On the morning of February 17, 2012, the body of six-year-old Laurence Mullany-Mills was recovered from a frozen pond in Holywell, Lincolnshire, following a harrowing overnight search. He had vanished the previous evening alongside his grandmother, Dawn Mullany, 71, after they went out to feed ducks and swans. Neither returned home, prompting a large-scale rescue effort involving local residents, police, and an RAF helicopter. Dawn’s car was found parked near the pond, and her body was located shortly after. Despite immediate attempts to revive her, she was pronounced dead at the scene. Laurence’s body was found just before 4 a.m. the next day by specialized police divers. Laurence, affectionately called Laurie, was a bright, outgoing child known for his curiosity and warmth. Neighbors recalled how he’d wave from the garden wall, strike up conversations with passersby, and proudly help his toddler sister, Nancy, take her first steps. He attended Ketton Church of England Primary School and dreamed of playing rugby and learning the violin. His mother, Asmina, and father, Vaughan, were too heartbroken to speak publicly. Dawn Mullany, a longtime resident of Castle Bytham, was remembered as a gentle, devoted grandmother who had weathered deep personal losses — including the death of her father during World War II and her husband in 1977. Friends described her as endlessly patient, generous, and trusted to care for anyone. One neighbor noted she was ‘the kind of woman who made you feel safe.’ The pond, lined with grass and a concrete feeding platform, is a quiet spot frequented by ducks and swans. Authorities confirmed no signs of foul play. Detective Chief Inspector David Wood stated the incident appeared to be a tragic accident, with no witnesses and likely no way to reconstruct the exact moment of the fall. The family had recently returned from a Christmas holiday in New Zealand. Community members expressed disbelief and sorrow, calling the double loss ‘beyond tragedy.’

El cos de Laurence va ser trobat just abans de les 4 del matí del dia següent per equips especialitzats de la polícia. Laurence, conegut com a Laurie, era un nen brillant i extrovertit, recordat per la seva curiositat i calidesa. Dawn Mullany, residenta de Castle Bytham des de fa molts anys, va ser recordada com una àvia gentil i dedicada que havia superat grans pèrdues personals —com la mort del seu pare durant la Segona Guerra Mundial i la del seu marit el 1977. Els amics la descriuen com a infatigablement pacient, generosa i de confiança absoluta per cuidar qualsevol persona. Un veí va dir que era ‘el tipus de dona que et feia sentir segura.’ L'estany, envoltat d'herba i una plataforma de formigó per alimentar els ocells, és un lloc tranquil molt freqüentat per patos i cignes. Les autoritats van confirmar que no hi ha cap indici de criminalitat. El detectiu inspector cap David Wood va afirmar que l'esdeveniment semblava un accident tràgic, sense testifics i probablement impossible de reconstruir exactament. While other children play, seven-year-old Long Dihao from Dazu, Chongqing, spends hours each day in intense training to become the world’s best backflipper. Long’s rigorous routine fuels a big appetite, which he satisfies with simple, healthy noodle soup. article_content: Fans of the 2011 film 'The Green Hornet' have a rare opportunity to own a piece of cinematic history: the legendary Black Beauty, the hero’s custom-built 1965 Chrysler Imperial. Up for auction next week by RR Auction in Massachusetts, this one-of-a-kind vehicle was designed by California-based special effects expert Dennis McCarthy and is among only two intact 'show cars' left from the movie’s production. Unlike typical movie props, this Black Beauty isn’t just for show—it’s fully functional. Under the hood lies its original 413 cubic-inch engine with just over 71,000 miles. Its most striking features? Two hood-mounted Browning .30 caliber machine guns that shoot real flames when connected to a propane tank, 12 Stinger missiles lining the bumpers, a front-grill flame-thrower, beanbag launchers, and shotgun barrels—all part of its over-the-top, comic-book-inspired arsenal. But it’s not all firepower. The car also boasts playful details: a license plate that flips to 'HORNET' with a click of a key fob, green-tinted headlights, the Green Hornet emblem on the trunk, and an interior console labeled in Chinese. Even the doors open like butterfly wings—a design challenge McCarthy admitted was tricky to execute. Inside, the original black leather seats remain untouched, and the sound system? A high-end Sony setup—the same company that produced the film. Jay Leno, car enthusiast and former Tonight Show host, got behind the wheel and called it a dream ride. 'Twenty-nine cars were built for the film,' says RR Auction’s Bobby Livingston, 'but most were wrecked or stripped down. This is the real deal.' The Green Hornet himself—played by Seth Rogen, who also co-wrote the script—first appeared in 1936 as a radio drama about a masked vigilante and his brilliant sidekick, Kato. Bruce Lee famously portrayed Kato in the 1960s TV series. Though the 2011 remake earned nearly $100 million globally, critics weren’t blown away. Still, for collectors and fans, this car is pure magic. Bidding opened at $10,000 on Friday and runs through June 26 on RR Auction’s website.

article_content: Michael Owen has praised Manchester United’s formidable attacking lineup but cautioned that the team’s strike force is aging. The former Liverpool and Real Madrid forward, who played for United between 2009 and 2012, believes the club must begin investing in younger talent to secure its future. 'It’s an exceptional attacking unit,' Owen told the Manchester Evening News. 'The only concern is that all the strikers are reaching the latter stages of their careers.' With Robin van Persie now 31, Wayne Rooney 29, and Radamel Falcao 28 — the latter dealing with recurring injuries — Owen argues that United cannot rely indefinitely on experienced players. 'In the coming years, you’d expect United to bring through or sign a promising young striker to carry the torch,' he said. Despite this, Owen remains confident in the team’s immediate prospects. 'The here and now is very exciting — for the next few years, United are well placed to compete for titles.' He added that Van Persie still has two or three prime years left and that Louis van Gaal’s priority will be winning silverware soon.

article_content: LONDON, England (CNN) — A new witness in the disappearance of British girl Madeleine McCann has told investigators he spoke with a woman resembling Victoria Beckham who may hold clues about the child’s fate, a family spokesman said Thursday. A police sketch has been released depicting the woman, described as being in her 30s, approximately 5 feet 2 inches tall, speaking with an Australian accent and fluent Spanish. Madeleine vanished from her family’s holiday villa in Praia da Luz, Portugal, in May 2007, when she was three years old. Her parents, Kate and Gerry McCann, were dining at a nearby restaurant at the time. According to family spokesman Clarence Mitchell, the witness encountered the woman outside a bar in Barcelona on May 7, 2007. Authorities have not disclosed details of the conversation but are actively seeking to locate the woman. Former detective inspector Dave Edgar, hired by the McCann family, called the new testimony a significant development in the case. He declined to explain why the witness came forward so late, citing personal reasons. Madeleine’s parents have received widespread international support, including appeals from celebrities and even Pope Benedict XVI. In 2008, Portuguese authorities briefly considered the McCanns and British resident Robert Murat as suspects. However, the Portuguese public prosecutor’s office confirmed in July 2008 that no evidence linked any of them to the disappearance, and the investigation into them was closed. The overall case remains open.

S'ha publicat un esbós policial que representa la dona, descrita com a d'uns 30 anys, aproximadament 1,57 m d'alçada, que parla amb un accent australià i un castellà fluent. Madeleine va desaparèixer de la seva vivenda de vacances a Praia da Luz, Portugal, el maig de 2007, quan tenia tres anys. Segons el portaveu de la família, Clarence Mitchell, el testimoni va trobar-se amb la dona fora d'un bar a Barcelona el 7 de maig de 2007. article_content: The son-in-law of Hélène Pastor, a 77-year-old billionaire heiress from Monaco, has acknowledged his involvement in her murder, according to prosecutors. Wojciech Janowski, 64, a former Polish Honorary Consul in Monaco, was arrested alongside his wife, Sylvia Pastor, on suspicion of masterminding the killing. Sylvia was later released without charge. Hélène Pastor and her chauffeur were fatally shot on May 6 outside L'Archet Hospital in Nice. Investigators have identified two suspects — two men aged 24 and 31 from the Comoros Islands, both with prior criminal records — using DNA evidence and CCTV footage. The footage shows them traveling by train from Marseille to Nice, checking into a hotel, and proceeding to the crime scene. One suspect allegedly left his face uncovered. Prosecutors have uncovered suspicious financial transactions into Janowski’s bank account, suggesting a possible motive tied to inheritance. Hélène Pastor’s children, already wealthy, stood to inherit billions upon her death. A separate lead involves an alleged blackmailer who had been contacting the Pastor family and is now undergoing psychiatric evaluation. In total, 23 people were arrested across Nice, Marseille, and Rennes; ten have since been released. French MP Eric Ciotti expressed 'extreme shock,' while Prince Albert II of Monaco offered 'deep support' to the Pastor family. Hélène Pastor’s grandfather, an Italian immigrant, helped develop much of Monaco’s infrastructure. The principality, known as a tax haven, has long been associated with financial secrecy and high-net-worth individuals — some linked to organized crime.
