article_content: Paris (CNN) — François Hollande defeated incumbent President Nicolas Sarkozy in France’s presidential runoff on Sunday, ushering in a new era of left-leaning leadership as the country and Europe grapple with economic hardship. In a heartfelt address to supporters in Tulle, Hollande called the victory 'a great day for our country and a new beginning for Europe.' He pledged to govern for all French citizens, saying, 'Many have waited for this moment for years. Others, younger, have never known it. I’m proud to bring hope back.' Hollande, set to become France’s first left-wing president since François Mitterrand left office in 1995, emphasized national unity: 'Tonight, there are not two Frances — only one France, one nation bound by the same destiny.' He also signaled a departure from austerity, declaring, 'Austerity can no longer be seen as inevitable.' Later, speaking to a roaring crowd at Paris’s Bastille, Hollande vowed to heal decades of division: 'I know the wounds, the ruptures — and together, we will repair, recover, and unite.' Sarkozy, conceding defeat early as official results poured in, accepted full responsibility: 'I carry the entire responsibility for this defeat. I fought for responsibility — and I don’t run from mine.' He added, 'I’m ready to be a French citizen among French citizens, with love for my country deep in my heart.' With nearly all votes counted, Hollande led 51.6% to 48.4%, according to France’s Interior Ministry. Exit polls from France 2 TV put his margin slightly higher at 51.9%. Turnout exceeded 80%, underscoring intense public engagement. Celebrations erupted across France — car horns blared along the Champs-Élysées, crowds cheered at campaign headquarters, and youth activists hailed the result. 'It’s a great night, full of joy for so many young people,' said Thierry Marchal-Beck of the Movement of Young Socialists. U.S. President Barack Obama called Hollande immediately after the results to offer congratulations and extend an invitation to the White House. Sarkozy, president since 2007, defended his record amid high unemployment (~10%) and sluggish growth, arguing that Europe’s debt crisis could have been far worse. His loss marks the latest in a string of European leaders ousted during the eurozone crisis — including those in Greece and Italy. The election coincided with Greece’s parliamentary vote, where exit polls showed major gains for anti-austerity parties. In the sole televised debate, the two candidates exchanged sharp attacks: Sarkozy called Hollande a 'liar' and 'little slanderer'; Hollande accused Sarkozy of neglecting duty, cronyism, and favoring the wealthy. Centrist François Bayrou, who won 9% in the first round, bolstered Hollande’s campaign by endorsing him and urging his supporters to vote 'according to conscience.'

article_content: A fire on a packed commuter bus in Xiamen, southeastern China, killed 47 people and injured around 30. Authorities have attributed the tragedy to Chen Shuizong, a 60-year-old man who allegedly set the bus ablaze with petrol. State media reported that a suicide note was found at Chen’s home following the incident, which occurred during Friday evening rush hour on an elevated roadway. Forensic evidence confirmed his involvement; he died in the fire. Witnesses described smelling petrol and hearing explosions about 10 minutes after the fire began. Thick black smoke engulfed the bus, leaving it reduced to a charred shell. Images shared on social media showed severely burned passengers and widespread chaos. The Bus Rapid Transit (BRT) system—operational since 2008, covering over 80 kilometers and serving more than 250,000 daily riders—was temporarily suspended. It has since reopened. Chinese officials are investigating how petrol was introduced onto the bus, though the vehicle’s fuel tank remained intact. This incident echoes previous tragedies: in 2009, an unemployed man set fire to a bus in Chengdu, killing 27; in 2011, a high-speed train derailment near Wenzhou claimed 40 lives, and a subway collision in Shanghai injured hundreds. While China’s public transit network has expanded rapidly over the past decade, concerns persist that safety standards are being compromised in the push for modernization.

article_content: Luis Suárez’s bite on Italy’s Giorgio Chiellini during Uruguay’s 1-0 World Cup victory has sparked global headlines. It marks the third time the Liverpool striker has bitten an opponent, prompting FIFA to consider a disciplinary response — potentially a ban of up to two years. But how has the story been received in Uruguay, Italy, and Spain? In Uruguay, the incident was completely absent from front pages. Media outlets like La República, El Telégrafo, La Diaria, and El Observador focused solely on their team’s historic qualification to the last 16. Headlines celebrated Diego Godin’s decisive header and the nation’s upcoming clash against Colombia at the Maracanã. In Italy, Suárez’s bite was a minor footnote. While Tuttosport led with 'Godin and the referee send Uruguay through as Suárez bites Chiellini,' major papers like La Gazzetta dello Sport and Corriere dello Sport centered on Italy’s shocking group-stage exit. Attention turned to Claudio Marchisio’s red card and the immediate resignations of coach Cesare Prandelli and Italian FA president Giancarlo Abete. Spain’s AS, however, ran a fierce campaign against Suárez. Their front page screamed 'Suárez Bites for the Third Time,' featuring images of Chiellini showing his injured shoulder. The paper explicitly connected Suárez to Real Madrid and Barcelona, labeling him a 'cannibal' and revisiting his prior bites on PSV’s Otman Bakkal (2010) and Chelsea’s Branislav Ivanović (2013). The narrative framed Suárez not just as a troublemaker, but as a toxic figure for Spain’s elite clubs.

article_content: Iran has reportedly activated a heavy-water production plant at Arak, raising concerns it could produce plutonium for nuclear weapons. For the past 18 months, inspectors from the International Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA) have been barred from accessing the heavily guarded site. Recent satellite images, released yesterday, show steam plumes emanating from the facility—located about 150 miles southwest of Tehran—suggesting active operations. These developments coincide with the resumption of nuclear talks in Almaty, Kazakhstan, between Iran and the P5+1 nations (the United States, United Kingdom, France, Russia, China, and Germany)—the first such negotiations in eight months. Western diplomats described the first day of the two-day talks as 'useful,' but noted Iran did not immediately agree to shut down the underground Fordow enrichment facility near Qom, a key point of contention. Fordow, buried deep within a mountain, has long alarmed Western powers due to its capacity to enrich uranium up to 20% purity—well above the 3.5% needed for civilian reactors, though below weapons-grade 90%. Iran maintains this enrichment is solely for producing medical isotopes for a research reactor in Tehran. Although Iran currently lacks the technology to reprocess plutonium into weapons material, analysts warn it may seek expertise from North Korea, which has successfully developed such capabilities. Meanwhile, Iran denies reports of a recent explosion at Fordow, labeling them as Israeli propaganda aimed at influencing ongoing negotiations. In late 2011, Fordow began producing 20% enriched uranium—a move that triggered global concern. The UN Security Council has repeatedly demanded Iran halt all uranium enrichment. Despite offers of limited sanctions relief in exchange for freezing sensitive nuclear activities, Iran responded only with a promise to submit a proposal of 'equal scale.' No concrete agreement was reached by the end of the talks. Iran plans to begin operating the Arak reactor in early 2014—a timeline many fear could provoke a preemptive military strike by Israel. While Tehran insists its program is entirely peaceful, international skepticism remains high due to years of noncompliance and lack of transparency.

Diplomàtics occidentals van descriure el primer dia de les converses de dos dies com 'útil', però van assenyalar que Irà no va acceptar immediatament tancar la instal·lació d'enriquiment subterrània de Fordow, propera a Qom, un punt clau de controvèrsia. article_content: Former President Donald Trump has never admitted to being wrong — so when he repeatedly confuses the names of President Joe Biden, former President Barack Obama, George W. Bush, and Jeb Bush, he offers a peculiar explanation: it’s all intentional. On Truth Social, Trump claimed that swapping Obama’s name for Biden’s is a sarcastic signal that Obama still wields influence over the administration. He accused critics — including Florida Governor Ron DeSantis and the Democratic Party — of exploiting these moments to falsely label him cognitively impaired. Trump added that he recently passed a cognitive test with a perfect score during a physical exam — the same result he reportedly achieved while in office. He then challenged Biden to take a similar test, implying that Biden’s policy positions — from open borders to electric vehicles — reflect poor judgment. During a radio interview with Brian Kilmeade, Trump doubled down, asserting that Obama — not Biden — is truly in control, particularly regarding Iran policy. When Kilmeade corrected him, Trump replied, 'Obama is Biden’s boss,' suggesting a hidden power structure. The claim, presented with absolute certainty, resembles more a rehearsed conspiracy theory than a coherent political analysis. While Trump cites passing cognitive tests, neither assessment was independently verified or publicly released in full. Multiple credible reports confirm his pattern of misidentifying leaders, which remains unexplained by anything other than error or rhetorical flourish.

article_content: Washington (CNN) — Lawmakers have scheduled a hearing for Thursday to investigate the recall of popular pediatric medicines by drugmaker McNeil Consumer Healthcare, which has initiated four product recalls in the past seven months. Among those set to testify is Colleen Goggins, worldwide chair of Johnson & Johnson, under which McNeil operates as a division. The House Committee on Oversight and Government Reform also invited Johnson & Johnson CEO William Weldon, but he declined to attend due to health reasons. A panel of Food and Drug Administration (FDA) officials will also appear at the hearing. The recalls include widely used over-the-counter medications such as Tylenol, Motrin, and Benadryl. On May 1, fifty children’s versions of these nonprescription drugs were recalled due to quality and safety concerns. McNeil maintains that the pediatric recalls were not prompted by adverse medical events but were taken as a precautionary measure. According to the FDA, adverse events refer to consumer-reported serious side effects — such as death, hospitalization, or disability — linked to product use. Following the pediatric recall, Johnson & Johnson suspended production at McNeil’s Fort Washington, Pennsylvania facility, which manufactured the affected children’s products. On Tuesday, the company outlined steps to address serious quality and safety deficiencies at Fort Washington and its other manufacturing sites. 'McNeil is taking steps to restore its operations to the level of quality that Johnson & Johnson demands, that the public rightly expects, and that we demand of ourselves,' the company stated. To improve quality and manufacturing systems, McNeil has hired an independent pharmaceutical consulting firm to recommend corrective actions. The company has not disclosed when production will resume. It also pledged to conduct in-depth quality assessments for every product to ensure it meets specifications throughout its shelf life. McNeil will provide monthly updates to the FDA on its progress and involve an independent firm in product decisions during the first six months of resumed operations. Previous recalls by McNeil in the past seven months include: In November 2009, five lots of Tylenol Arthritis Pain (100-count, EZ-open cap) were recalled due to an unusual odor linked to nausea, stomach pain, vomiting, and diarrhea. In December 2009, the recall expanded to include all lots of that product. In January 2010, additional recalls were issued for unspecified quantities of Tylenol, Motrin, and other OTC drugs following consumer complaints of illness related to odors.

article_content: E. Lynn Harris, the acclaimed author who brought the hidden lives of Black gay men into the literary mainstream, was remembered by friends as both courageous and deeply generous. He passed away at age 54 on Thursday night during a business trip to Los Angeles, according to his publicist, Laura Gilmore. Through novels like 'Invisible Life,' 'A Love of My Own,' and his bestselling memoir 'What Becomes of the Brokenhearted,' Harris created a new literary space — centering Black, affluent, masculine gay men whose inner lives were often invisible in mainstream fiction. His stories resonated powerfully, especially among Black women, whose copies of his books became common sights in beauty salons, bookstores, and subway cars from New York to Washington, D.C. An unlikely literary star, Harris began his career in 1991 selling self-published books from the trunk of his car to Black-owned salons and bookshops. He rose to become one of America’s most widely read authors, with an estimated four million copies in print. Author Tina McElroy Ansa recalled meeting Harris when both were struggling financially — they bought each other’s first books. Ansa was moved to tears after reading just twenty pages of 'Invisible Life,' struck by a tender scene of two Black men playing in the snow — a depiction of same-sex affection she’d never encountered before. 'It was playful, loving, and it wasn’t hidden,' she said. As his fame grew, Harris remained grounded. He hosted dinners for aspiring writers, hugged fans at signings, answered up to 200 emails daily, and even flew unknown authors to events at his own expense. 'He had a spirit of joy,' said Tananarive Due, who recalled Harris remembering a fan’s name years after their first meeting. Yet his journey wasn’t without pain. Born in Flint, Michigan, and raised in Little Rock, Arkansas, Harris endured abuse by his stepfather and attempted suicide in 1990. In his memoir, he described his 20s and early 30s as years spent hiding his identity — until writing 'Invisible Life' helped him find peace. Though celebrated by many, Harris also faced criticism. Some questioned his literary skill, calling him formulaic. Others within the Black community accused him of either misrepresenting gay Black men or revealing too much. 'I’m not James Baldwin,' Harris once said, defending his mission to write accessible, relatable stories for everyday readers. Despite being labeled an advocate, Harris resisted the role. 'It’s such a small part of who I am,' he told the Detroit Free Press in 2003. 'Most of my friends are straight. I tend to have a regular life.' Yet his legacy is undeniable. As Due put it, 'He helped let the air in. He helped us all breathe a little better.'

article_content: Adrianne Haslet-Davis’s life as a dancer was shattered in the 2013 Boston Marathon bombing. She and her husband Adam — recently returned from a tour in Afghanistan with the Air Force — were just steps away from the second explosion. 'I felt the direct impact,' she recalls. 'It immediately blew off part of my left foot.' Before she could even look down, Adam’s reaction confirmed her worst fears. 'I remember him picking up my foot and screaming — a sound you never want to hear from someone you love.' Adam, who suffered shrapnel wounds to both legs, knew Adrianne’s injury was life-threatening. He used his belt as a tourniquet. 'It was ironic,' he said. 'For 4½ months in Afghanistan, I wore a tourniquet daily. When did I need it? Back at home.' Minutes later, first responders rushed her to Boston Medical Center. Surgeons had no choice but to amputate. When Adrianne woke up the next day, she believed her foot had been saved. Her mother delivered the devastating truth: 'Adrianne, you don’t have a foot. Your foot is gone.' 'I just lost it,' she says. 'It was really hard to hear.' As an award-winning ballroom dancer, losing her foot meant losing her identity. 'Dancing is the one thing I do where I don’t feel like I should be doing anything else. I feel so free,' she says. Adam adds: 'When she dances, I see her glow. To have that taken in a split second — it’s devastating.' In the weeks after the attack, Adrianne struggled with PTSD and crippling anxiety. 'I thought everybody had a bomb,' she admits. One night, fireworks outside her apartment triggered a panic attack — she hit the floor, screamed, and called 911. The physical road to recovery was equally brutal. 'I didn’t know a prosthetic could be this painful,' she says. Months of grueling therapy followed. Her muscle memory remained, but standard prosthetics couldn’t replicate the complex motions of ballroom dance. Then she met Dr. Hugh Herr — a leading biomechatronics expert at MIT and a double amputee himself. Moved by her determination, he pledged to build the world’s first bionic leg designed for dancing. His team mapped her favorite dance moves using ultra-sensitive sensors and embedded AI into the limb to learn movement patterns. After months of testing and feedback, Adrianne stood before CNN’s Anderson Cooper — eight months after their first meeting — and danced. 'I had no doubt she’d do it,' Cooper said. 'She was kind enough to teach me. I need a lot more work.' Today, Adrianne is not just dancing again — she’s advocating for amputee rights and better prosthetics. 'What disables me isn’t missing a foot — it’s that my tech isn’t advanced enough to let me do what others with two feet can do.' And she refuses to be called a victim. 'A victim means I belong to someone who hurt me. I’m not suffering. I’m thriving. I am a survivor.'

Una nit, un espectacle de focs artificials fora del seu apartament va desencadenar un atac de pànic — va caure al terra, va cridar i va trucar al 911. La seva memòria muscular encara hi era, però les pròtesis normals no podien replicar els moviments complexos del ball de saló. Impressionat per la seva determinació, va prometre construir la primera pròtesi biónica del món dissenyada específicament per ballar. El seu equip va mapejar els seus moviments favorits de ball amb sensors ultrassensibles i va integrar intel·ligència artificial a la pròtesi per aprendre patrons de moviment. Després de mesos de proves i retroalimentació, Adrianne es va presentar davant d'Anderson Cooper de la CNN —vuit mesos després de la seva primera reunió— i va ballar. 'No vaig tenir cap dubte que ho aconseguiria,' va dir Cooper. 'Va ser suficientment amable per ensenyar-me. Jo necessito molta més feina.' Avui, Adrianne no només balla de nou — també defensa els drets dels amputats i millors pròtesis. 'El que em discapacita no és no tenir dos peus — és que la meva tecnologia no és prou avançada per fer el mateix que algú amb dos peus pot fer.' I es refusa a ser anomenada víctima. 'Una víctima vol dir que pertanyes a algú que et va fer mal. Jo no sofro. Jo prospero. Sóc una supervivient.'

article_content: A freelance cameraman covering Egypt’s constitutional referendum for The Associated Press has been released on bail, the news agency said Friday. Hassan Abdullah Hassan was producing video coverage outside a Cairo polling station when police detained him and his driver, according to an AP report. His driver, Mohammed Salah Mohammed, was released on Thursday. 'We are pleased that Mr. Hassan has been released on bail, and we hope any remaining legal questions can be resolved quickly,' said John Daniszewski, AP’s senior managing editor for international news. Hassan told AP by phone that he was arrested after police saw his footage being broadcast live on Al Jazeera Television’s Egyptian affiliate and mistakenly concluded he was an Al Jazeera employee. CNN first learned of Hassan’s detention through Twitter, after Cairo-based AP journalist Jon Gambrell posted about it. Last month, Egyptian authorities detained four Al Jazeera employees. Cameraman Mohamed Fawzy was released on December 31, but Peter Greste, Mohamed Fadel Fahmy, and Baher Mohamed from Al Jazeera English remain in custody. Authorities accuse them of holding illegal meetings with the Muslim Brotherhood, which Egypt designated a terrorist organization last month. Al Jazeera has called the arrests arbitrary, stating the network has faced sustained harassment by Egyptian security forces—including confiscation of equipment and raids on its offices—despite not being banned from operating in Egypt. Nearly 40 correspondents and editors from 29 international media organizations signed a letter to Egyptian authorities on Monday, demanding the immediate release of the detained journalists and condemning what they described as arbitrary detentions. They also called for the release of other journalists imprisoned in Egypt, some of whom have been held for over five months. 'The arrest of these journalists has cast a shadow over press and media freedom in Egypt,' the letter states. CNN’s Catherine E. Shoichet and Marie-Louise Gumuchian contributed to this report.

article_content: A dishevelled Paul Gascoigne was found wandering the streets of Poole, Dorset, clutching a four-pack of lager and a bottle of gin. Looking dazed and occasionally in tears, he was escorted to an ambulance after bystanders called 999 at approximately 2:30 p.m. on Thursday. The former World Cup hero, now 47, was admitted to Poole Hospital, where he awoke the following day after another devastating relapse into alcoholism. Witnesses reported smelling alcohol on him and described him as physically frail, barely able to stand. He was still wearing the same T-shirt and had on a pair of blue slippers—footwear he wore while purchasing alcohol and cigarettes from a local off-licence. His hair was unkempt, his skin blotchy, and his body visibly malnourished. Gascoigne, once renowned for his athletic build, now appears a shadow of his former self. His legs are painfully thin, with a small wound visible on his left shin. His arms, once powerful enough to power past defenders, are now emaciated. He is expected to be evicted from his £3 million rented penthouse in Sandbanks by September 13, as the landlord has decided not to renew the lease. Neighbors have filed multiple complaints about noise from the property, where Gascoigne lives alone. His sister, Lindsay, posted on Facebook: 'This illness is so tragic, and there is no cure. It has shown its ugly head again. Please leave us alone to grieve and pull together as a family to help save a great man.' Gascoigne’s struggles date back to 1998, when then-Middlesbrough manager Bryan Robson sent him to rehab after he was found unconscious following a binge of 32 shots of whisky. Since then, he has battled alcoholism, drug use, OCD, ADHD, Tourette’s syndrome, and eating disorders. He has lived in Poole for the past four years and has been a patient at The Providence Project rehabilitation center. Yet, between stays, his condition has deteriorated significantly. Friends and former teammates—including Gary Lineker, Chris Evans, and Ronnie Irani—have previously funded treatment in Arizona. Lineker stated at the Edinburgh TV Festival: 'We've supported him over the years. But ultimately, the responsibility for recovery has to come from Paul.' According to Hunter Davies, co-author of Gascoigne’s 2004 autobiography, 'Football saved Paul from himself. He doesn't even like alcohol—he hates the taste. But when he's depressed, he wants to get obliterated.' In recent months, reports suggest Gascoigne has begun asking fans for £5 in exchange for selfies—a sign of deepening financial hardship. His only known source of income now appears tied to his celebrity status. Harry Redknapp, his friend and neighbor, offered him a coaching role with his QPR academy: 'I love Gazza. He’s got a heart of gold. But the only person who can help him now is himself.'

El seu cabell estava desgreñat, la seva pell era mancada i el seu cos visiblement malnutrit. Gascoigne, abans famós per la seva construcció atlètica, ara sembla una ombra del que va ser. Les seves cames són dolorosament fines, amb una petita ferida visible al seu turmell esquerre. Els seus braços, un cop potents prou per superar defensors, ara estan emaciat. Es preveu que sigui expulsat del seu pis en lloguer de 3 milions de lliures a Sandbanks el 13 de setembre, ja que el propietari ha decidit no renovar el contracte. Veïns han presentat múltiples queixes pel soroll provenint de la propietat, on Gascoigne viu sol. La seva germana, Lindsay, va publicar a Facebook: 'Aquesta malaltia és tan trágica, i no hi ha cura. Ha tornat a mostrar el seu costat més fosc. Us demano que ens deixeu sols per plorar i unir-nos com sempre per ajudar a salvar un gran home.' Les seves lluites daten del 1998, quan l'entrenador del Middlesbrough, Bryan Robson, el va enviar a rehabilitació després de trobar-lo inconscient després d'una beguda de 32 xiclets de whiski. Des d'aleshores, ha combatut l'alcoholisme, l'ús de drogues, TDAH, TOC, el síndrome de Tourette i trastorns alimentaris. Ha viscut a Poole durant els últims quatre anys i ha estat pacient al centre de rehabilitació The Providence Project. Tot i això, entre estades, la seva condició ha empeorat significativament. Amics i antics companys—com Gary Lineker, Chris Evans i Ronnie Irani—han finançat anteriorment tractaments a Arizona. Lineker va declarar al Festival de Televisió d'Edimburg: 'L'hem suportat durant anys. Però, en última instància, la responsabilitat per la recuperació ha de venir de Paul.' Segons Hunter Davies, coautor de la seva autobiografia de 2004, 'El futbol va salvar Paul de si mateix. Ni sequera li agrada l'alcohol—el detesta. Però quan està deprimit, vol emborratxar-se.' Els últims mesos, s'ha informat que Gascoigne ha començat a demanar 5 lliures als fans a canvi de fotos amb el mòbil—un senyal d'una creixent dificultat financera. La seva única font de ingressos coneguda ara sembla estar lligada al seu estatus de celebritat. Harry Redknapp, el seu amic i veí, li va oferir un paper d'entrenador a l'acadèmia del QPR: 'Estimo el Gazza. Té un cor d'or. Però la única persona que pot ajudar-lo ara és ell mateix.'

article_content: An Israeli soldier who was critically injured in fighting last month died on Sunday, the Israel Defense Forces announced in a tweet. The death of Sgt. Shacar Shalev, 20, came nearly a week after a new ceasefire between Israel and Hamas ended more than seven weeks of conflict. Shalev’s death brings the total number of Israeli fatalities in the conflict to 68 — 65 soldiers and two civilians. One foreign worker in Israel was also killed. The United Nations estimates that more than 2,100 Palestinians have been killed in the violence in Gaza, with at least 70% believed to be civilians. Israel, however, reports a higher proportion of militants among the deceased. The ceasefire, agreed upon on Tuesday by Israeli and Hamas officials, has no expiration date, unlike previous agreements. It does not address core long-term issues on either side. However, Israel has agreed to ease its blockade on Gaza, open border crossings for increased humanitarian aid, and extend the fishing limit off the coast to six nautical miles, according to a senior Egyptian government official. Both sides have agreed to return to Cairo for further negotiations, the official added.

article_content: By Lucy Crossley. PUBLISHED: 06:49 EST, 12 March 2014. | UPDATED: 10:02 EST, 12 March 2014. Keen walker: Sue Jones died after falling into a waterfall. Her husband Malcolm jumped in to try to save her, but the current was too strong. A retired doctor has described how he desperately tried to save his wife after she fell into a waterfall but lacked the strength to pull her free from the powerful current. Malcolm and Sue Jones had been walking with their dog near their home in the Lake District when she slipped and plunged into the fast-flowing water, becoming trapped face-down among large boulders. An inquest heard that Dr. Jones leapt into the waterfall, but the current was too strong and the water too deep for him to reach the mother of two. Mrs. Jones, 60, suffered fatal head injuries when she tumbled into the water at Force Forge, Satterthwaite, Cumbria, on January 11 this year, the inquest at Barrow Town Hall was told. 'We wanted to take the dog down a steep slope to a large pool so he could swim,' said 61-year-old Dr. Jones. 'After he went in for a while, we headed back up. The dog was dawdling, so Sue went ahead while I stayed about 20 yards behind. Then I heard a short scream—and she was gone.' Dr. Jones, who said the couple had walked along the stream 'many times,' told the hearing his wife became lodged face-down against the boulders. 'The current was so strong and the water so deep—I just couldn't reach her,' he said. The court heard Dr. Jones lost his glasses and sustained a scratch to his forehead during his attempt to reach his wife. The water eventually dislodged Mrs. Jones' body and carried her downstream to the pool. 'I swam to her, grabbed her, and pulled her to the edge. But by then I was so cold I didn’t have the strength to haul her onto the bank,' he said. Dr. Jones realized early on that his wife was unlikely to survive—she had been submerged face-down for too long. 'I turned her over. She wasn’t breathing and had no pulse,' he said. He positioned her body against the bank and went to seek help. Assistant coroner for South and East Cumbria, Mr. Alan Sharp, read a statement from Lee Warren, who spotted Dr. Jones by the roadside—covered in blood from his head injury and soaked to the skin. The statement said: 'He told me his wife had fallen, and I think she’s dead.' Mr. Warren rushed to the stream, pulled Mrs. Jones from the water, and administered CPR. Emergency services were called, and she was transported to the Royal Lancaster Infirmary, where she was pronounced dead hours later. A post-mortem examination revealed the cause of death was traumatic brain injury and a fractured skull caused by impact with a large, sharp object. Mr. Sharp recorded a verdict of accidental death. The couple, originally from Thame, Oxfordshire, had owned a holiday cottage in Satterthwaite for more than 12 years. They moved there permanently two years ago and spent their time renovating the old vicarage. Speaking after his wife’s death, Dr. Jones said: 'We’ve always traveled to the Lakes and always knew we’d eventually want to move here. This was the house my wife had always had her eye on—and when it came on the market, we seized the chance. It’s a beautiful place to live, and Sue loved everything about it.' 'Sue loved building friendships with the villagers. We felt so settled here—the community is small, and everyone welcomed us. Sue had so many good friends in the village.' 'She was desperate for grandchildren and thrilled to be helping out at the pub—she had so much fun. It gave us both a new lease on life.' The couple was later joined by their daughter Emma, 29, and her partner Simon Cole, who took over the village’s Eagles Head pub in November. 'We could only run a pub with family support—it was Satterthwaite or nothing,' said Ms. Jones. 'My mum was so happy to have us here. Everything was working out, and she had so many great ideas.' The family said housewife and enthusiastic cook Mrs. Jones was known for her 'famous chocolate brownies,' a favorite on the pub menu. 'Her priority was her family and friends,' said Ms. Jones. 'She did everything for everyone and could never do enough for us.' 'She spent so much time decorating the house—it was just perfect. She was the most amazing host and loved having us all together as a family.' Mrs. Jones’s son, pediatrician Dr. Andrew Jones, 32, who lives in south London with his wife Sonya, 31, said: 'She was very content and happy with what life had to offer right now. Emma and my mum were extremely close—so when Emma and Simon bought the pub, it was the best thing that could have happened. She was thrilled to help out. Everything was busy and thriving for them.' 'She was a gentle, loving person—elegant and beautiful inside and out. It’s because of Mum that we’re such a close family. At this terrible time, we’re determined to honor her legacy by sticking together.' 'She just wanted everyone to be happy. We’ve lost such a special person.'

Un metge jubilat ha descrit com va intentar desesperadament salvar la seva dona després que ella caigués en una cascada, però no va tenir la força per treure-la de la poderosa corrent. Malcolm i Sue Jones estaven caminant amb el seu gos prop de la seva casa als Llacs quan ella va reslliscar i va caure a l’aigua ràpida, quedant atrapada cara avall entre grans roques. Una investigació va escoltar que el Dr. Jones va saltar a la cascada, però la corrent era massa forta i l’aigua massa profunda perquè pogués arribar a la mare de dos fills. La Sra. Jones, de 60 anys, va patir lesions capilars mortals quan va caure a l’aigua a Force Forge, Satterthwaite, Cumbria, el 11 de gener d’aquest any, segons va informar l’investigació al Consistori de Barrow. 'Volem portar el gos per un pendent pronunciat fins a una gran piscina perquè pugui nedar,' va dir el Dr. Jones, de 61 anys. 'Després que ell va entrar a l’aigua un moment, vam tornar enrere. El gos anava molt lent, així que Sue va anar endavant mentre jo estava uns 20 metres darrere. Llavors he sentit un crit curt—i ella ja no hi era.' El Dr. Jones, que va dir que la parella havia caminat per aquest torrent 'moltes vegades', va explicar a l’audiència que la seva esposa va quedar atrapada cara avall contra les roques. 'La corrent era tan forta i l’aigua tant profunda—no puc arribar a ella,' va dir. El tribunal va saber que el Dr. Jones va perdre les ulleres i va patir un tall a la front durant el seu intent de rescatar la seva dona. L’aigua finalment va desplaçar el cos de la Sra. Jones i la va arrossegar riu avall fins a la piscina. 'He nadat fins a ella, l’he agafat i la he portat a la vora. Però llavors estava tan fred que no tenia força per a pujar-la a la riba,' va dir. El Dr. Jones va entendre de bon començament que la seva dona probablement no sobrevindria—havia estat boca avall durant massa temps. 'La vaig girar. No respirava i no tenia pols,' va dir. Va posar el cos de la seva dona contra la riba i va anar a buscar ajuda. El coroner adjunt del sud i l’est de Cumbria, el Sr. Alan Sharp, va llegir una declaració de Lee Warren, que va veure el Dr. Jones al costat de la carretera—cobert de sang pel seu feriment a la cap i empapat fins a l’os. La declaració deia: 'Em va dir que la seva dona havia caigut i crec que ja està morta.' El Sr. Warren va córrer cap al torrent, va treure la Sra. Jones de l’aigua i li va administrar RCP. Es van trucar els serveis d’urgència i la van transportar al Royal Lancaster Infirmary, on va ser declarada morta hores després. Un examen postmortem va revelar que la causa de la mort va ser una lesió traumàtica del cervell i un crani fracturat causats per l’impacte amb un objecte gran i afilat. El Sr. Sharp va registrar un veredicte de mort accidental. La parella, originària de Thame, Oxfordshire, havia tingut una casa de vacances a Satterthwaite durant més de 12 anys. Es van mudar permanentment allà fa dos anys i van passar el seu temps renovant l’antic vicariat. Parlant després de la mort de la seva dona, el Dr. Jones va dir: 'Sempre hem viatjat als Llacs i sempre vam saber que acabariem volent mudar-nos aquí. Aquesta era la casa que la meva dona havia tingut sempre a la mira—i quan va sortir al mercat, vam agafar l’oportunitat. És un lloc bellíssim per viure, i a la Sue li encantava tot d’aquí.' 'A la Sue li encantava fer amistats amb els veïns. Ens vam sentir molt instal·lats aquí—la comunitat és petita i tothom ens va acollir. La Sue tenia molts bons amics al poble.' 'Estava desitjosa de néts i emocionada d’ajudar a la taverna—se’n feia tanta diversió. Ens va donar a tots dos una nova oportunitat a la vida.' La parella va ser més tard acompanyada per la seva filla Emma, de 29 anys, i el seu pare Simon Cole, que van prendre el control de la taverna del poble, l’Eagles Head, a novembre. 'Només podíem gestionar una taverna amb el suport de la família—era Satterthwaite o res,' va dir la Sra. Jones. 'La meva mare estava tant contenta de tenir-nos aquí. Tot estava funcionant bé i tenia tantes idees genials.' La família va dir que la Sra. Jones, ama de casa i cuinera entusiasta, era coneguda pels seus 'coulis de xocolata famosos,' un favorit al menú de la taverna. 'La seva prioritat era la seva família i els seus amics,' va dir la Sra. Jones. 'Ho feia tot per tothom i mai no podia fer prou per nosaltres.' 'Va passar tant de temps decorant la casa—era perfecta. Era l’anfitriona més increïble i li encantava tenir-nos tots junts com a família.' El fill de la Sra. Jones, el metge pediatre Dr. Andrew Jones, de 32 anys, que viu a Londres Sud amb la seva dona Sonya, de 31 anys, va dir: 'Era molt contenta i feliç amb el que la vida li havia ofert ara mateix. Emma i la meva mare eren molt properes—per tant, quan Emma i Simon van comprar la taverna, va ser la millor cosa que podia passar. Va estar encantada d’ajudar. Tot estava molt ocupat i prosperant per ells.' 'Era una persona gentil i estimadora—elegant i bella per dins i per fora. És gràcies a la Mama que som una família tan unida. En aquest moment terrible, estem decidits a honrar el seu llegat mantenint-nos junts.' 'Només volia que tothom fos feliç. Hem perdut una persona tan especial.'

article_content: CNN — Welcome back to work, Congress. Hope you enjoyed your fourth full week off this year. Now find a way to work together to help get America back to work. Experts agree that little constructive action is likely from Congress until after the election. That’s why cynicism often passes for wisdom in Washington. But with economic headwinds from abroad dampening our recovery, there’s an obligation to act now. Fortunately, several bipartisan bills could jumpstart the U.S. economy—if given a fair chance. These aren’t partisan ideas—they’re practical ones. And unlike pork-barrel spending, they cost taxpayers relatively little. Here are three bipartisan proposals with real momentum that could pass this summer. Public-Private Infrastructure Bank: The bipartisan BUILD Act is a no-brainer—but it’s been stalled for no good reason. It would establish a public-private bank to fund critical infrastructure upgrades, boosting long-term resilience and competitiveness while creating jobs now. As Michael Likosky of NYU’s Center on Law & Public Finance notes: 'In a time of budgetary crisis, the American Infrastructure Bank leverages private capital sitting idle. Every other major country does this. The U.S. is an outlier.' John Hofmeister, former CEO of Shell Oil, adds: 'We’re poised for a new era of prosperity—if we can agree that our infrastructure needs rebuilding. It was designed for a different time and population.' President Obama has endorsed this bill as more feasible than his earlier proposal. 'Obama is the strongest advocate for public-private partnerships ever to hold office,' says Likosky. 'This is a rare Beltway-born idea embraced by governors and mayors across the aisle.' Start-Up 2.0 Act: Over 40% of Fortune 500 companies were founded by immigrants, and new businesses have created over 40 million jobs in the last 30 years. Yet, outdated visa rules force talented STEM graduates to leave the U.S. after earning degrees here. The Start-Up 2.0 Act—co-sponsored by Republican Sens. Marco Rubio and Jerry Moran, and Democratic Sens. Mark Warner and Chris Coons—would grant green cards to foreign Ph.D. and master’s graduates in STEM fields and lift per-country limits on skilled worker visas. It also includes tax incentives for startup investments and reduced taxes for early-stage businesses. Small Business Assistance: The Small Business Jobs and Tax Relief Act of 2012, backed by Senate Majority Leader Harry Reid and Sen. Chuck Schumer, is set for a vote this month. It offers a 10% tax credit for new hires or wage increases and allows full expensing of capital investments like machinery. Though a competing House bill proposes doubling the credit—and extending it to hedge funds—the core idea is sound and deserves bipartisan support. Small businesses employ more Americans than large corporations, yet they get far less attention. We must prioritize Main Street over Wall Street. These are modest, targeted measures—not grand reforms. Centrists understand the need to balance idealism with realism. Major tax reform or deficit deals won’t happen until after the election, and partisan gridlock won’t magically disappear then. Obstacles include lobbyists protecting industry loopholes, unions resisting skilled immigration reform, and extremists in both parties who fear giving the opposition a win. Republicans don’t want Obama to claim economic victories. Some Democrats worry bipartisan success might weaken their campaign narrative against a Republican House. 'The American people are held hostage to the selfish political interests of partisans on both sides,' says Hofmeister. There’s an old joke in Congress: Every bill is a jobs bill—because it’s your job on the line. These three bills are genuine win-wins. Every member of Congress should act now to prove they can govern—or face voter backlash. True leadership means serving the national interest, not special interests. Governing isn’t a zero-sum game. A rising tide lifts all boats—and a growing economy benefits everyone. After all, we’re all in the same boat.

Els experts coincideixen que és poc probable que es prenguin accions constructives al Congrés fins després de les eleccions. Per això, el cinisme sovint passa per sabiesa a Washington. Però amb vents econòmics des de l’estranger que atenuen la nostra recuperació, hi ha una obligació d’actuar ara. Afortunadament, diversos projectes bipartidistes podrien impulsar l’economia dels EUA si se’ls dóna una oportunitat justa. Aquests no són idees partidistes—són pràctiques. I a diferència dels projectes de gasta pública, costen relativament poc als contribuents. Aquí teniu tres propostes bipartidistes amb molt impulsi que podrien aprovar-se aquest estiu. Banc d’infraestructures públic-privat: El projecte bipartidista BUILD és una obvietat—però s’ha aturat sense raó vàlida. Crearia un banc públic-privat per finançar millores crítiques en infraestructura, augmentant la resiliència i competitivitat a llarg termini i creant feines ara. Com diu Michael Likosky del Centre de Dret i Finances Públiques de la NYU: 'En temps de crisi pressupostària, el Banc d’Infraestructura Americana aprofita el capital privat que està inactiu. Quasi tots els altres països grans ho fan. Els EUA són una excepció.' John Hofmeister, exdirector general de Shell Oil, afirma: 'Estem preparats per una nova era de prosperitat—si podem arribar a un acord que la nostra infraestructura necessita ser reconstruïda. Va ser dissenyada per una època i població diferents.' El president Obama ha donat suport a aquest projecte com a més factible que la seva proposta anterior. 'Obama és l'advocat més fort de les col·laboracions públic-privades mai haver ocupat càrrecs,' diu Likosky. 'Aquesta és una idea rara nascuda a Beltway, acceptada pels governadors i alcaldes de tots dos costats.' Llei Start-Up 2.0: Més del 40% de les empreses de la llista Fortune 500 van ser fundades per immigrants, i les noves empreses han creat més de 40 milions de feines en els últims 30 anys. Tanmateix, les normes de visat obsoletes forcen graduats en STEM a deixar els EUA després de rebre títols aquí. La Llei Start-Up 2.0—co-patrocinada pels senadors republicans Marco Rubio i Jerry Moran i pels senadors demòcrates Mark Warner i Chris Coons—otorgaria tarjetes verdes a graduats estrangers amb doctorat o màster en camps STEM i eliminaria els límits per país en visats de treballadors qualificats. També inclou incentius fiscais per inversions en empreses noves i reduccions d'impostos per a empreses en fase inicial. Assistència a petites empreses: La Llei de Treball i Alliberament Fiscal per a Pymes de 2012, respaldada pel líder majoritàri del Senat Harry Reid i el senador Chuck Schumer, es preveu que es voti aquest mes. Ofereix un crèdit fiscal del 10% per nous contractes o augmentos salarials i permet la deducció total d’inversions en capital com maquinària. Encara que un projecte competidor de la Cambra proposa duplicar el crèdit—i ampliar-lo a fons especulatius—la idea central és sòlida i mereix suport bipartidista. Les petites empreses empleen més americans que les grans corporacions, però reben molt menys atenció. Hem de prioritzar Main Street sobre Wall Street. Aquestes són mesures modestes i dirigides—no reformes grans. Els centrists entenen la necessitat d’equilibrar idealisme amb realisme. Reformes fiscales majors o acords sobre dèficit no passaran fins després de les eleccions, i la paralització partidista no desapareixerà mágicament després. Els obstacles inclouen pressionadors que protegeixen buits legislatius, sindicats que s’oposen a la reforma migratòria per a treballadors qualificats i extrems de tots dos partits que tenen por de donar victòries a l’oposició. Els republicans no volen que Obama aconsegueixi victòries econòmiques. Alguns demòcrates temen que el suport bipartidista debiliti la seva narrativa electoral contra la Cambra Republicana. 'El poble americà és hostatge dels interessos polítics egoistes dels partidaris de tots dos costats,' diu Hofmeister. Hi ha un antic chiste al Congrés: Tot projecte és un projecte de feina—perquè és el teu treball el que està en joc. Aquests tres projectes són guany-guany genuïns. Cada membre del Congrés ha d’actuar ara per demostrar que pot governar—o enfrentar-se a la reacció dels electors. El lideratge autèntic significa servir l’interès nacional, no els interessos especials. Governar no és un joc de suma zero. Una marea que puja eleva tots els vaixells—i una economia en creixement beneficia a tothom. Després de tot, som tots al mateix vaixell.

article_content: Oscar-winning actor Nicolas Cage was arrested in New Orleans’ French Quarter on Friday night following a drunken altercation, according to police. The incident began around 11:30 p.m. when Cage, in town to film a movie, argued with his wife, Alice Kim, on the 600 block of Dumaine Street. He insisted the residence they were standing in front of was their rental, but she disagreed. Witnesses reported that Cage grabbed her upper arm and pulled her toward the house. He then began striking nearby vehicles and attempted to enter a taxi. Police, summoned by bystanders, found him heavily intoxicated. After ordering him out of the cab, Cage reportedly yelled at officers, leading to his arrest. He was taken to Central Lock-Up and booked on charges of domestic abuse battery, disturbing the peace, and public drunkenness. A mugshot released by the Orleans Parish Sheriff shows an unshaven Cage with his eyes closed. His bond was set at $11,000, with a court date scheduled for May 31. Notably, the court waived the stay-away order, meaning Cage is permitted to be with his wife. Authorities confirmed there were no visible injuries on her arm. Cage was released from jail Saturday afternoon. He was bailed out by Duane Chapman, known as 'Dog the Bounty Hunter,' who stated he acted solely in his capacity as a bail bondsman—not as part of his reality TV persona. 'I do not believe the latter will be the case for Mr. Cage,' Chapman added, referring to Cage not fleeing court. CNN reached out to Cage’s legal team but received no response. Cage, 47, and Kim have a 5-year-old son. His previous marriages to Patricia Arquette and Lisa Marie Presley ended in divorce. An Academy Award winner for 'Leaving Las Vegas,' Cage has starred in dozens of films but has also faced well-publicized financial struggles, including tax liens and property foreclosures. In 2009, he sued his former accountant, Samuel Levin, alleging mismanagement that led to financial ruin. Levin countered that he had repeatedly warned Cage about his extravagant spending.

article_content: In a rare but legally justified move, psychiatrist Dr. Ruth Bagshaw broke patient confidentiality to alert police about Gareth Jordan, a 55-year-old man who confessed to having disturbing sexual fantasies involving children. Fearing he might act on these impulses, Dr. Bagshaw concluded her duty to protect potential victims outweighed her obligation to privacy. Her decision led to a police raid on Jordan’s home in Tylorstown, Rhondda, where investigators uncovered hundreds of indecent images of children, including 46 photos he’d taken of kids walking to a local Cardiff school. They also found children’s clothing and underwear he had purchased to fulfill his fantasies, along with a DVD featuring naked female participants from a naturist camp. Jordan, already on the sex offenders register for previous convictions related to child pornography, pleaded guilty to multiple charges including possession and creation of indecent material, and violating his existing prevention order. At Merthyr Tydfil Crown Court, Judge Richard Twomlow emphasized the deliberate nature of Jordan’s breach, sentencing him to 100 hours of community service, a £60 victim surcharge, and extending his restrictions under a new community order. The judge warned that any future violation would lead directly to prison. The General Medical Council later affirmed that while confidentiality is foundational in medicine, exceptions exist when there is a clear risk of serious harm — particularly to children — making disclosure not just permissible, but sometimes necessary in the public interest.

article_content: Researchers at Carnegie Mellon University have used Harry Potter to uncover how the brain processes magic — not the kind on the page, but the kind happening inside our minds as we read. In a groundbreaking study, they scanned the brains of eight participants as they read Chapter 9 of 'Harry Potter and the Sorcerer's Stone', focusing on Harry’s first flying lesson. To match the slow pace of fMRI scans — which capture brain activity every two seconds — the team presented one word every half second, grouping them into four-word segments. For each word, they coded 195 detailed linguistic features, including word length, part of speech, and semantic properties. Using a machine learning algorithm, researchers mapped how each cubic millimeter of the brain responded to these segments. Over time, the model learned to link specific linguistic features with precise brain regions: sentence parsing activated language centers, word meaning triggered semantic networks, and character interactions lit up areas tied to social cognition. Remarkably, the system could predict which of two unseen passages a participant was reading with 74% accuracy. 'We were skeptical this would work at all,' said Tom Mitchell of CMU. 'But it produced stunningly clear brain maps showing exactly where we think about characters, motion, and meaning.' Published in PLOS ONE, the study represents the first integrated computational model of natural reading. Unlike prior studies that examined single words or controlled stimuli, this model captures complex, real-world text processing in real time. Leila Wehbe noted that when characters flew on broomsticks, the brain activated the same regions used to perceive real human motion. When characters interacted socially, the brain engaged areas linked to understanding others’ intentions. Though the model remains imprecise, researchers believe it could one day help diagnose reading disorders like dyslexia, monitor stroke recovery, or guide foreign language instruction. As Mitchell explained: 'When you struggle to understand a sentence, you often can’t say why. But your brain knows — and now, we might be able to see it.' The researchers compare their model to a DNA fingerprint: even without knowing every detail of how it works, it provides a powerful roadmap for understanding how the brain constructs meaning during reading.

Per adaptar-se a la velocitat lenta de les escaneres fMRI — que capturen l'activitat cerebral cada dos segons — l'equip va presentar una paraula cada mig segon, agrupant-les en segments de quatre paraules. Per a cada paraula, van codificar 195 característiques lingüístiques detallades, incloent la longitud de la paraula, la seva classe gramatical i propietats semàntiques. Utilitzant un algorisme d'aprenentatge automàtic, els investigadors van mapejar com cada mil·límetre cúbic del cervell responia a aquests segments. Amb el temps, el model va aprendre a relacionar característiques lingüístiques específiques amb regions cerebrals precises: l'anàlisi de frases activava centres lingüístics, el significat de les paraules activava xarxes semàntiques, i les interaccions entre personatges il·luminaven àrees vinculades a la cognició social. Remarcablement, el sistema podia predir quin de dos passatges desconeguts estava llegint un participant amb un 74% d'exactitud. 'Érem escèptics que això funcionés', va dir Tom Mitchell de la CMU. 'Però va produir mapes cerebrals sorprenentment clars que mostren exactament on pensem sobre personatges, moviment i significat.' Publicat a PLOS ONE, l'estudi representa el primer model computacional integrat de la lectura natural. A diferència d'estudis anteriors que examinaven paraules úniques o estimuls controlats, aquest model captura el processament de textos complexes del món real en temps real. Leila Wehbe va observar que quan els personatges volaven en escobes, el cervell activava les mateixes regions utilitzades per percebre el moviment humà real. Quan els personatges interaccionaven socialment, el cervell enganxava àrees vinculades a entendre les intencions dels altres. Tot i que el model roman imprecís, els investigadors creuen que pot ajudar un dia a diagnosticar trastorns de la lectura com la dislexia, vigilar la recuperació després d'un ictus o guiar l'ensenyament d'idiomes estrangers. Com va explicar Mitchell: 'Quan tens dificultats per entendre una frase, sovint no pots dir per què. Però el teu cervell ho sap — i ara, potser podem veure-ho.' Els investigadors comparen el seu model amb una empremta de DNA: fins i tot sense conèixer cada detall del seu funcionament, ofereix una ruta poderosa per entendre com el cervell construeix significat durant la lectura.

article_content: Kevin Sutherland made history on the Champions Tour on Saturday by becoming the first player ever to shoot a sub-60 round — a spectacular 59 — propelling him to the top of the Dick's Sporting Goods Open leaderboard. What makes the feat even more extraordinary is that Sutherland, 50, nearly posted a 58. He bogeyed the final hole after his tee shot landed in the rough, costing him the chance at 14-under-par. The round began with an incredible streak: eight straight birdies to start, highlighted by an eagle on the par-five 5th hole. He turned in just 28 strokes. After birdies on the 10th and 11th, he added three more from the 15th onward. A par on the 18th would have sealed a 58 — but it wasn’t meant to be. Instead, Sutherland finished with a stunning 13-under 59, including 12 birdies and one bogey, moving him to 14-under overall — three shots ahead of his closest competitor. While six golfers have previously shot 59 on the PGA Tour, this marks the first time such a score has been recorded on the Champions Tour. The event is played on a par-72 course, making a 13-under 59 the lowest round in Champions Tour history.

El fet més extraordinari és que Sutherland, de 50 anys, va gairebé fer un 58. Va fer un bogey a l'últim forat després que el seu tee anés a l'herba alta, perdent l'oportunitat de fer 14-sota-el-par. La ronda va començar amb una seqüència increïble: vuit búrdits consecutius al principi, destacant un eagle al forat 5, par-cinc. Va arribar a la volta amb només 28 cops. Després de búrdits als forats 10 i 11, va afegir altres tres des del 15. Un par a l'últim forat hauria tancat un 58 — però no va ser per així. En canvi, Sutherland va acabar amb un sorprenent 59 sota-par 13, amb 12 búrdits i un bogey, situant-se a 14-sota-el-par en total — tres cops per davant del seu rival més proper. Encara que sis jugadors han fet abans un 59 al PGA Tour, aquesta és la primera vegada que aquesta puntuació s'ha assolit al Champions Tour. L'esdeveniment es juga en un camp de par-72, fent del 59 sota-par 13 la ronda més baixa de la història del Champions Tour.

article_content: The 2013 British Comedy Awards, hosted by Jonathan Ross, descended into chaos marked by excessive profanity, visibly intoxicated performers, and deeply offensive jokes — a far cry from the clever satire viewers anticipated. Broadcast live on Channel 4, the two-hour event featured Ross and Lee Mack reviving the 2008 Sachsgate scandal in a crude ventriloquist sketch, where Ross, masked as a dummy, responded to a mock apology with 'Oh f*** off.' Comedian Alan Carr told Nicole Scherzinger he wanted to 'f*** your brains out,' then kissed her on the lips, while Johnny Vegas, clearly drunk, ranted about past snubs: 'I haven't won f****** anything since nine years ago.' Technical failures led to Steve Coogan’s emotional acceptance speech for Outstanding Achievement being abruptly cut to air a repeat of Gogglebox. More than 50 formal complaints were submitted to Channel 4 and Ofcom, condemning the event as vulgar, unfunny, and inappropriate for prime-time television. Media watchdog Mediawatch-UK’s Vivienne Pattison criticized the reliance on swearing as a replacement for genuine humor, pointing out such language would be unacceptable in schools or workplaces. Although Channel 4 stated the show was promoted as adult content with clear warnings, many viewers felt the boundary between edgy and offensive had been recklessly crossed. Ross later tweeted that Channel 4 were 'f****** idiots' for cutting Coogan’s speech — a comment that only intensified public backlash.

Transmesos en directe per Channel 4, els dos hores de l'esdeveniment van incloure Ross i Lee Mack revivint l'escàndol de Sachsgate del 2008 en un esquetx brutal de ventròquil, on Ross, amb una màscara, va respondre a una disculpa simulada amb 'Oh f*** off.' Tot i que Channel 4 va afirmar que l'espectacle havia estat promocionat com a contingut per adults amb advertències clares, molts espectadors van considerar que s'havia creuat la línia entre l'audaç i l'ofensiu. Ross va publicar posteriorment un tuit en què deia que Channel 4 eren 'f****** idiots' per haver tallat el discurs de Coogan — una observació que va intensificar la reacció pública.

article_content: Microsoft co-founder Bill Gates and his wife, Melinda, have contributed $1 million to Initiative 594, a Washington state effort aiming to require background checks for every gun sale—including those at gun shows and between private individuals. The gift, quietly filed on Friday and revealed publicly on Monday, pushes the campaign’s total fundraising past $6 million. The initiative would close long-standing gaps in state law that currently allow unvetted transactions, though exceptions remain for family transfers and antique firearms. In a joint statement, the Gateses called I-594 a 'balanced and effective' step toward reducing gun violence in their home state. Their donation follows similar support from fellow Microsoft pioneer Paul Allen, who gave $500,000 earlier this month, and venture capitalist Nick Hanauer, whose latest $1 million contribution brings his total to nearly $1.4 million. Former Microsoft CEO Steve Ballmer and his wife, Connie, have also pitched in $580,000. On the other side, Initiative 591, which aims to block stricter rules beyond federal standards, has gathered just over $1 million. Campaign lead Zach Silk highlighted the grassroots momentum behind I-594, noting that nearly 350,000 residents signed petitions to get it on the ballot, and over 7,500 people from almost every county have donated. He credited the collective effort—especially from high-profile supporters—as vital to turning policy into action. Data from the FBI shows Washington recorded 106 gun-related homicides in 2012, a rise of 34 compared to the previous year, adding weight to the campaign’s call for reform.

La donació, presentada silenciosament el divendres i feta pública el dilluns, porta el total recaptat per la campanya més enllà dels 6 milions de dòlars. L'iniciativa pretén tancar les llacunes legals que actualment permeten transaccions sense verificació, encara que hi ha excepcions per a transferències familiars i armes antigues. En una declaració conjunta, els Gates van qualificar la I-594 com un pas 'equilibrat i efectiu' cap a reduir la violència amb armes al seu estat. La seva donació segueix el suport similar del també cofundador de Microsoft Paul Allen, que va donar 500.000 dòlars a principis d'aquest mes, i del capitalista de risc Nick Hanauer, la darrera contribució de 1 milió de dòlars del qual porta el seu total a gairebé 1,4 milions. L'exdirector general de Microsoft Steve Ballmer i la seva esposa, Connie, també han aportat 580.000 dòlars. Al costat oposat, la Iniciativa 591, que vol impedir normes més estrictes que l'estàndard nacional, ha recaptat només uns 1 milió de dòlars. El cap de campanya Zach Silk va destacar l'impuls ciutadà darrere de la I-594, assenyalant que gairebé 350.000 habitants van signar peticions per posar-la a votació, i més de 7.500 persones de gairebé tots els comtats han donat. Va atribuir l'esforç col·lectiu—especialment dels suports destacats—com vital per transformar la política en acció. Dades del FBI mostren que Washington va registrar 106 homicidis relacionats amb armes de foc el 2012, un augment de 34 respecte de l'any anterior, afegint pes a la crida de la campanya per a la reforma.

article_content: Dortmund, Barcelona, Atlético Madrid, and Lazio have confirmed their places in the last-16 stage of the Champions League. Borussia Dortmund advanced to the knockout stage with a 3-1 victory at AC Milan. Marco Reus opened the scoring from the penalty spot after Olivier Giroud had his own penalty saved. Samuel Chukwueze equalized before halftime, but goals from Jamie Bynoe-Gittens and substitute Karim Adeyemi secured the win for Dortmund. Barcelona came from behind to defeat Porto 2-1, reaching the knockout rounds for the first time in three seasons. Atlético Madrid beat Feyenoord 3-1, benefiting from two own goals, to seal their place in the last 16—a dramatic turnaround after failing to progress from the group stage last year. Their 11 points placed them one point ahead of Lazio, who defeated Celtic 2-0 earlier in the day. In Paris, Kylian Mbappé scored a 98th-minute penalty to earn Paris Saint-Germain a 1-1 draw with Newcastle United. The penalty was awarded after VAR reviewed contact between the ball and Newcastle’s Tino Livramento’s chest. Newcastle manager Eddie Howe criticized the decision, calling it incorrect and deeply frustrating. Manchester City overturned a 2-0 halftime deficit to beat RB Leipzig 3-2 at the Etihad Stadium. Phil Foden scored one goal and assisted two others, including the winner by substitute Julian Alvarez in the 87th minute. The victory extended City’s unbeaten home record in the Champions League to 29 games since September 2018. With one matchday remaining, AC Milan and Newcastle United sit two points below PSG, facing each other in the final round as PSG travel to Dortmund. City and Leipzig have both already qualified, with City topping Group G with 15 points—six clear of Leipzig.

article_content: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration is pushing for stricter rules on indoor tanning beds, citing alarming evidence that faulty equipment and poor safety practices are putting users—especially teenagers—at risk of severe burns and skin cancer. Dr. Jeffrey Shuren, who leads the FDA’s medical device division, clarified that the goal isn’t to hurt small businesses, but to close dangerous gaps in safety. Right now, tanning beds are treated like bandages—classified as low-risk devices with no federal oversight. The FDA wants to reclassify them as moderate-risk, meaning manufacturers must prove their machines deliver precise UV levels, have updated software, and fully function with safety locks and timers. According to Shuren, these aren’t new or extraordinary demands—they’re basic checks that too many companies either skip or do poorly. Meanwhile, the Indoor Tanning Association argues that its members already follow high standards and fears the new rules will add costly bureaucracy during tough economic times. But research tells a different story: a recent study in the American Journal of Preventive Medicine found that nearly all indoor tanners exceed recommended exposure times. Many salons also fail to post warnings or check IDs, letting minors tan without parental permission. Meg Watson, an epidemiologist with the CDC, says confusion reigns because rules have gone unenforced for years. ‘People hear mixed messages,’ she warns. ‘And teens are paying the price.’ Data from the CDC shows more than a third of high school senior girls have used tanning beds. The Skin Cancer Foundation stresses that using a tanning bed before age 35 raises the chance of melanoma—the deadliest skin cancer—by 75%. Dawn Holman, another CDC scientist, notes that the UV rays from these machines can be stronger than the midday summer sun. The FDA’s new proposal aims to reverse the sharp rise in skin cancer among young adults. Melanoma is now the second most common cancer for teens and young adults aged 15–29, and the top cancer for those 25–29. To raise awareness, the FDA plans to require clear warning labels on every tanning bed and printed materials specifically for under-18 users, stressing that repeated use dramatically increases cancer risk. The public has 90 days to respond to the proposal. If finalized, businesses will have one year to make the necessary changes.

article_content: Britain is enjoying a glorious stretch of sunny weather, with temperatures climbing to 22.4°C in Plymouth and families flooding parks, beaches, and fields across the country. In Earsdon, North Tyneside, three-year-old Sophie Walker strolled through golden rapeseed fields, using a ladybird-shaped umbrella as a parasol — a charming scene repeated nationwide. As the sun dipped behind Croyde Bay in North Devon, paddle boarders glided across the water beneath a breathtaking crimson-and-orange sky — a sight that seemed to confirm the old adage: 'Red sky at night, shepherd’s delight.' Despite a damp start in some areas, the southwest led the way in warmth and sunshine, with Brighton Beach slowly filling with sunbathers — including Sian Wilson and Ella King, who braved the heat in bikinis. Festivalgoers at Heaton Park in Manchester celebrated the Parklife Weekender under clear blue skies, while near Bamburgh Castle in Northumberland, four-year-old Kadie Lane played among wildflowers, later perching happily on her mother’s shoulders. While eastern coastal regions and parts of Scotland saw more cloud cover, and temperatures were expected to peak slightly lower — around 20–22°C — the overall pattern remained bright and dry. The Met Office forecasts a gradual shift beginning Tuesday, as a band of rain moves in from the west, bringing a more unsettled week ahead. However, forecaster David Jackson reassured the public: 'There should still be plenty of sunny weather to be enjoyed.' Though scattered showers may affect northern Scotland and Northern Ireland, they are expected to be light and brief, offering little disruption to the prevailing sunshine.

Despite the widening losses, Spinny’s gross revenue surged nearly 30-fold to ₹3,262 crore in FY23 from ₹109 crore in FY22—driven primarily by its cash-and-carry business model. Car sales accounted for 95% of total gross revenue, amounting to ₹3,105 crore. The remainder came from ancillary services, including commissions on sales and financial products. In 2021, Spinny secured $283 million in funding from new and existing investors, propelling its valuation to $1.8 billion and cementing its status as a unicorn. In August 2023, the company laid off nearly 300 employees as part of a restructuring effort that merged its Truebil and Spinny Max divisions into the main platform. Spinny stated that the move was prompted by rising demand for affordable, reliable vehicles as office workers returned post-pandemic. article_content: Over the past few decades, mountaintop removal coal mining has become more common in West Virginia. This method involves blasting away mountaintops and depositing the resulting debris into nearby valleys to access coal seams buried beneath. Although coal once supplied about 50% of U.S. electricity, as of 2023 it generates approximately 19%, according to the U.S. Energy Information Administration. Still, about one-third of West Virginia’s coal is mined this way. However, a CNN/ORC International poll found that 57% of respondents oppose mountaintop removal mining. Supporters, including miners and coal companies, argue these projects provide vital jobs. Opponents counter that the environmental damage and harm to local communities outweigh the economic benefits. In CNN’s documentary 'Battle for Blair Mountain: Working in America,' Soledad O’Brien explores both perspectives. For many in West Virginia, the issue feels like a difficult choice: stable employment or a healthy environment. What would you choose?

article_content: London, England (CNN) — The future of English Premier League club Portsmouth hung in the balance on Friday after it was forced into administration amid debts of approximately $90 million. The south coast team became the first Premier League club to enter administration since the league’s formation 18 years ago—a period marked by a financial boom fueled by lucrative television rights. 'At 10:20 a.m. today, Portsmouth Football Club was placed into administration following the filing of a notice of appointment at the High Court by the chargeholder, Portpin Limited,' the club stated on its website. Being placed into administration means an insolvent company is managed by a court-appointed administrator with the goal of avoiding liquidation. The administrator evaluates the company’s assets and negotiates with creditors. Managed by former Chelsea boss Avram Grant, Portsmouth is already at the bottom of the table and facing relegation. The club raised around $100 million through player sales before the current season in an effort to reduce its debt. It will now be docked nine additional points, effectively sealing its relegation to the English Football League Championship. Portsmouth has seen a series of owners this season, but efforts to find a fifth buyer collapsed on Tuesday when current owner Balram Chainrai confirmed the club would enter administration to avoid a government winding-up order. At a press conference Friday, administrator Andrew Andronikou confirmed Portsmouth’s debts were around $100 million but expressed confidence the club would not go bankrupt. He added that the Premier League had signaled it might allow Portsmouth to sell players outside the regular transfer window. 'There will be no fire sale,' Andronikou said. 'We will need to sell one or two players—that’s why we’re speaking with the Premier League. Restructuring begins today, and there will be significant cost-cutting across all levels. I will cut to the bone.' Andronikou also confirmed that Grant has pledged to remain at the club until the end of the season. CEO Peter Storrie called it 'an extremely sad day' but acknowledged that administration had kept the club alive and opened the door for fresh investment. He also confirmed his intention to step down once a new owner is found. Portsmouth’s financial collapse marks a dramatic fall from grace for a club that won the FA Cup in 2008—its first major trophy since capturing back-to-back English league titles in 1949 and 1950. Portsmouth is not alone in facing financial ruin due to on-field ambitions. Leeds United entered administration in 2007, three years after their Premier League relegation and six years after reaching the UEFA Champions League semifinals. Both Southampton and Leicester City also entered administration after dropping out of the top flight.

'A les 10:20 del matí d’avui, el Portsmouth Football Club ha entrat en administració després que el creditor garantidor, Portpin Limited, presentés una notificació d’assignació al Tribunal Superior', va declarar el club en el seu lloc web. Entrar en administració vol dir que una empresa insolvent és gestionada per un administrador nomenat pel tribunal amb l’objectiu d’evitar la liquidació. L’administrador avalua els actius de l’empresa i negocia amb els creditors. Dirigit per l’exentrenador del Chelsea Avram Grant, Portsmouth ja està al fons de la taula i en perill de descens. Portsmouth ha tingut una sèrie d’owners aquesta temporada, però els esforços per trobar un cinquè comprador van col·lapsar dimarts quan l’actual propietari Balram Chainrai va confirmar que el club entraria en administració per evitar una ordre de liquidació del govern britànic. En una conferència de premsa divendres, l’administrador Andrew Andronikou va confirmar que els deutes de Portsmouth eren d’uns 100 milions de dòlars, però va expressar confiança que el club no aniria a la bancarrota. Va afegir que la Premier League havia indicat que podria permetre a Portsmouth vendre jugadors fora de la finestra de transfers regular. 'No hi haurà cap venda massiva,' va dir Andronikou. 'Hem de vendre un o dos jugadors—per això estem parlant amb la Premier League. La reestructuració comença avui, i hi haurà recorts de costos significatius a tots els nivells. Arribaré fins a l’os.' Andronikou també va confirmar que Grant s’ha compromès a romandre al club fins al final de la temporada. El director general Peter Storrie va qualificar-ho com 'un dia extremadament trist', però va reconèixer que l’administració havia mantingut el club viu i obert la porta a una nova inversió. També va confirmar la seva intenció de dimitir quan es trobi un nou propietari. La caiguda financera de Portsmouth marca una caiguda dramàtica per a un club que va guanyar la Copa FA el 2008, el seu primer títol important des de capturar els títols de lliga anglesa consecutius el 1949 i el 1950. Portsmouth no és l’únic club que ha patit ruïna financera per ambitions al camp. Leeds United va entrar en administració el 2007, tres anys després del seu descens de la Premier League i sis anys després d’arribar a les semifinals de la Lliga de Campions de la UEFA. Tant Southampton com Leicester City també van entrar en administració després de baixar de la primera divisió.

article_content: Comedy has long unsettled those in power—and this week, we saw a troubling example in Egypt. Bassem Youssef, often called Egypt’s Jon Stewart, was charged with mocking President Mohamed Morsy and insulting Islam. If convicted, he faces fines and possible imprisonment. Before rushing to blame 'they hate us for our freedoms,' remember America’s own history. Comedian Lenny Bruce was arrested eight times in the early 1960s—not for swearing, but for ridiculing political figures and religion. In 1964, he was convicted under obscenity laws and sentenced to four months of hard labor. He died in 1966, still appealing his conviction, from a morphine overdose. Today, no U.S. comedian would face criminal charges for mocking politicians or religion. If they did, figures like Bill Maher might already be serving life sentences. While elected officials may dislike being lampooned, none claim satire threatens national security. In the Arab world, political satire is still emerging. When I performed stand-up across the Middle East, promoters warned us: avoid jokes about leaders, religion—including Islam, Christianity, and Judaism—and never use profanity or sexual humor. It felt absurd: what’s left? But surprisingly, there’s still plenty to joke about. Comedians everywhere adapt—U.S. corporate events also ban politics, sex, and religion. The irony? Corporations and autocrats enforce nearly identical rules. But change is happening. A few years ago, authorities demanded scripts for review. Now, that’s mostly gone. Some performers are testing limits with mild profanity or suggestive material. Youssef went further: he mocked Morsy by name, mimicked his appearance, and aired sketches on national TV. To us, it’s normal. In Egypt, it was revolutionary. Remember: Egypt was ruled for nearly 30 years by Hosni Mubarak, who crushed dissent. Youssef became the Arab world’s voice of fearless satire—and now he’s being punished for it. Democracy isn’t just about holding elections. It’s about protecting the right to laugh at power. Journalists, bloggers, critics—all must be free to challenge authority. Early signals from Morsy’s government are discouraging. After the U.S. Embassy tweeted support for Youssef, Egypt’s presidency condemned it as 'negative political propaganda.' Morsy must decide: Is Egypt moving toward true democracy—or simply replacing one oppressor with another? The world is watching.

article_content: My eight-year-old daughter Nancy walked into the kitchen, nose wrinkled. 'What’s that gross thing floating in the sink?' she asked. 'Just a silkworm cocoon,' I said casually — a response that left her utterly bewildered. Honestly? I didn’t blame her. At 46, I’ve tried nearly everything to slow down aging — but this might be the weirdest yet. I’m talking about using the very cocoons spun by silkworms to make silk. These tiny, white, egg-shaped casings, harvested across Asia and shipped to Europe, are being touted online as a miracle for skin. According to Naomi Moriyama, Japanese women have been using them for centuries, inspired by the soft hands of silk harvesters in ancient China and Japan. Though the idea of rubbing a moth’s birth chamber on my face made me shudder — silkworms are essentially white caterpillars — I decided to give it a shot. My skin was showing every one of my 46 years: dull, spotted, sun-damaged. I bought 30 cocoons online for under £4 each. They arrived wrapped in bubble wrap, no instructions included. A quick Amazon search told me to soak them in hot water, then gently massage them over my face. I did. And I was shocked: instead of dissolving into slime, the cocoon held together. Dr. Michael Prager, a cosmetic expert, reassured me: sericin, the sticky protein inside, contains 18 amino acids that lock in moisture and stimulate collagen. I scheduled a skin scan with dermatologist Dr. Sunil Chopra. My results weren’t great — lots of sun damage and acne scars. But I followed his advice: use the cocoon every other day for a month. For two weeks, I saw nothing. I thought it was nonsense. Then, around week three, my stubborn mouth spot began shrinking. My skin felt softer. By week four, my friend Laura stared at me and said, 'You look five years younger.' Dr. Chopra confirmed it: my skin texture had improved by 20%, UV damage and scarring reduced significantly, and my wrinkle depth softened — especially around my eyes and mouth. The Visia scan showed my skin now ranks better than 96% of women my age. Even the clinic nurse ordered some after seeing the results. Turns out, nature doesn’t need a fancy bottle to work — just time.
