article_content: In the wake of escalating violence, U.S. President George W. Bush sharply criticized Russia’s military actions in Georgia, saying they’ve severely harmed Moscow’s reputation globally. Speaking from the White House, Bush warned that Russia’s moves — including pushing troops into western Georgia and reportedly planning to bomb Tbilisi’s airport — risk destroying its relationships with the U.S. and Europe. He stressed that such actions go far beyond what Russia had claimed were its limited goals: restoring stability in South Ossetia after fighting broke out on August 6. Georgia’s government reported that Russian forces had moved beyond the breakaway regions of South Ossetia and Abkhazia, entering the town of Senaki — a claim Russia has not officially confirmed. Meanwhile, Russia insists its intervention is a defensive response to Georgian attacks on Russian peacekeepers and ethnic Ossetians, many of whom hold Russian passports. Moscow argues it’s protecting its citizens, not seizing territory. The conflict erupted last week after Georgia launched a military operation in South Ossetia, following artillery strikes that killed ten civilians. Russia responded swiftly, sending troops into both South Ossetia and Abkhazia. Tskhinvali, the capital of South Ossetia, was left in ruins after days of heavy fighting, with both sides accusing each other of targeting civilians — Russia claims over 2,000 dead in Tskhinvali alone. International pressure mounted for a ceasefire. The UN Security Council drafted a resolution calling for an immediate halt to hostilities, full troop withdrawals, and international mediation. But Russia, wielding its veto power as a permanent member, rejected the French-drafted plan, arguing it ignored Georgia’s ‘prior aggression.’ Despite the tensions, Georgia’s president, Mikheil Saakashvili, agreed to a ceasefire deal brokered by France and Finland. The U.S. has stepped in with humanitarian aid — distributing food, blankets, and tents — and helped evacuate nearly 170 American citizens. However, Washington made clear it has no plans for military intervention. NATO and EU envoys continue shuttle diplomacy, while Russia’s prime minister, Vladimir Putin, vowed to carry out its mission to its ‘logical conclusion.’ Georgia’s ambassador in Washington warned that his country faces existential threat, and Saakashvili accused Russia of trying to crush Georgia’s democratic future — a claim echoed by Western leaders who reaffirmed their support for Georgia’s sovereignty. Yet, the broader geopolitical context — including decades of Russian influence in the Caucasus and Georgia’s push toward NATO — remains underexplored in official statements.

article_content: Abu Qatada, a radical cleric once described as Osama bin Laden’s right-hand man in Europe, has received more than £515,778 in legal aid funding from the UK taxpayer, according to a written parliamentary answer from the Ministry of Justice. The amount does not include final claims still pending from his legal team, meaning the total will be higher. He recently moved into a £450,000 property in north London, rented at £1,400 per month through a letting agency. The property, located near a church, was leased without the landlord’s knowledge of his identity. She later expressed shock upon learning who her tenant was, stating she would never have agreed to rent to him if she had known. Qatada was released on strict bail conditions last month after spending over eight years in high-security custody, which has cost taxpayers approximately £850,000. The Home Office has spent £825,000 on legal efforts to deport him to Jordan, where he faces terrorism charges. His deportation remains blocked by the European Court of Human Rights, which ruled that he might not receive a fair trial due to concerns that evidence against him could have been obtained through torture. His current residence is under 24-hour surveillance by security personnel, costing £100,000 per week. Total public expenditure related to Qatada—including detention, legal fees, housing, and monitoring—is estimated at £3 million. Justice Secretary Chris Grayling and campaign group TaxPayers’ Alliance have criticized the spending as excessive and damaging to public confidence in the legal system. Grayling emphasized that legal aid is funded by taxpayers and must represent value for money. Meanwhile, a government-appointed Commission on a Bill of Rights, tasked with reviewing the Human Rights Act, is expected to release a report widely anticipated to be vague and inconclusive. Internal divisions among its members—some of whom support strengthening rights protections—have undermined efforts to achieve meaningful reform. Prime Minister David Cameron had initially promised to scrap the Human Rights Act but scaled back his plans after forming a coalition with the Liberal Democrats.

article_content: Microsoft's Surface tablet will cost between £399 and £559 ($499 to $699 in the US) when it goes on sale on October 26, the company announced today. The pricing places it directly in competition with the cheapest third-generation iPad. The Surface launches the same day as Windows 8 — Microsoft’s new desktop operating system — and three days after Apple is expected to unveil a more affordable iPad mini. This is Microsoft’s first entry into consumer hardware. Built on an NVIDIA chip designed by ARM Holdings, the Surface runs a streamlined version of Windows 8 that does not support traditional desktop applications. However, it includes touch-optimized versions of core Office programs — Word, PowerPoint, and Excel — along with integrated Xbox apps for music, video, and gaming. The device features dual cameras and a USB port but is Wi-Fi only; Microsoft has not indicated plans for a cellular model. Its release coincides with Amazon’s debut of its Fire tablet line in the UK. Experts warn the pricing strategy could pose challenges. Despite revealing the tablet last month, Microsoft waited until now to disclose pricing. 'It’s priced the same as the iPad 3, even though the Surface offers a higher specification — 32GB versus the iPad’s 16GB,' said Stuart Miles of gadget site Pocket Lint. 'But most consumers won’t notice that difference. They’ll simply see two tablets at the same price and likely choose the iPad — they’re unaware of the specs battle.' 'If you’ve used Windows Phone, the Surface feels familiar — but few people have. And people either love or hate Windows Phone.' Microsoft also debuted its first TV ad for the Surface during a prime-time slot on the U.S. version of Dancing With The Stars. The ad shows a diverse group of users — families, schoolchildren, dancers — performing choreographed routines using the Surface and its detachable keyboard cover. The campaign highlights the keyboard as a key differentiator from the iPad. Industry analysts suggest Microsoft may spend up to $400 million on advertising for the Surface and Windows 8 launch. Microsoft also revealed Xbox Music, a streaming service offering 30 million songs. A free, ad-supported tier and a premium £8.99 ($9.99) subscription will be available at launch. The paid plan is required to use Xbox Music on Xbox 360 consoles or Windows Phone devices — and an Xbox Live Gold membership is also needed for console access. Existing Xbox users — approximately 66 million globally — will receive a 30-day free trial starting immediately. Despite tight control over early access, testers who tried Windows 8 on Samsung tablets reported a steep learning curve. Unlike the iPad, which users of all ages can operate instinctively, Windows 8 was described as confusing and non-intuitive at first glance. Though polished and thoughtful once mastered, the challenge lies in convincing consumers to invest time learning it — especially when the iPad requires no training. The ad marks the beginning of what could be a massive marketing push for both products.

No obstant això, inclou versions optimitzades per toca dels programes principals d’Office —Word, PowerPoint i Excel— així com aplicacions integrades d’Xbox per a música, vídeo i jocs. El dispositiu disposa de dues càmeres i un port USB, però és només Wi-Fi; Microsoft no ha indicat plans per a un model amb connexió mòbil. El seu llançament coincideix amb l’estrena de la sèrie de tauletes Fire d’Amazon al Regne Unit. Els experts avisen que l’estratègia de preus pot plantejar reptes. Malgrat haver revelat la tauleta el mes passat, Microsoft va esperar fins ara per revelar els preus. 'Està al mateix preu que la iPad 3, encara que la Surface ofereix una especificació superior —32 GB en lloc dels 16 GB de la iPad—', va dir Stuart Miles del lloc de gadgets Pocket Lint. 'Però la majoria dels consumidors no notaran aquesta diferència. Simplement veuran dos tauletes al mateix preu i probablement triaran la iPad — no són conscients de la batalla d’especificacions.' 'Si has usat Windows Phone, la Surface es sent familiar — però pocs l’han fet. I les persones o les adoreu o les odien.' Microsoft també va estrenar el seu primer anunci de televisió per a la Surface durant un horari de màxima audiència de la versió nord-americana de Dancing With The Stars. L’anunci mostra un grup divers de usuaris — famílies, nens i nenes escolars, ballarins — realitzant rutines coreografiades utilitzant la Surface i la seva funda de teclat desmuntable. La campanya destaca el teclat com a diferenciador clau respecte a la iPad. Els analistes de la indústria suggerixen que Microsoft pot gastar fins a 400 milions de dòlars en publicitat per al llançament de la Surface i Windows 8. Microsoft també va revelar Xbox Music, un servei de streaming amb 30 milions de cançons. Una versió gratuïta amb publicitat i una subscripció premium de 8,99 lliures (9,99 dòlars) estaràn disponibles al llançament. Es requereix el pla pagat per utilitzar Xbox Music a consolas Xbox 360 o dispositius amb Windows Phone — i també es necessita un compte Xbox Live Gold per accedir-hi des de la consola. Els usuaris actuals d’Xbox —aproximadament 66 milions a nivell mundial— rebran una prova gratuïta de 30 dies que comença avui. Malgrat el control estricta sobre l’accés anticipat, els provadors que van provar Windows 8 en tauletes Samsung van informar d’una corba d’aprenentatge pronunciada. A diferència de la iPad, que els usuaris de qualsevol edat poden operar instintivament, Windows 8 es va descriure com confús i no intuïtiu a primera vista. Tot i que és refinat i ben pensat un cop s’hi acostuma, el repte consisteix en convèncer els consumidors que invertin temps en aprendre’l — especialment quan la iPad no requereix cap formació. L’anunci marca l’inici de lo que podria ser una gran campanya de promoció per a ambdós productes.

article_content: A tragic collision between a tourist tram and a freight train at Victoria Falls in Zimbabwe left one person dead and 19 others injured—many of them guests attending the wedding of Peter Holmes a Court and Alissa Everett. The tram, carrying 30 tourists and five crew members, was struck from behind as it paused at the main station, likely due to a railway switch error. Among the injured was Holmes a Court’s best man, Jason Gissing, who sustained fractures to his arm and leg and was flown to South Africa for emergency care. Holmes a Court himself suffered minor injuries, while his fiancée, award-winning photojournalist Alissa Everett, emerged unharmed. The deceased was identified as 44-year-old American William Poovey, whose wife, Kara, was treated for a broken jaw in South Africa. The couple’s wedding, originally planned in Botswana, was canceled—but they later married in a private ceremony. In lieu of traditional gifts, they asked guests to contribute to a charity Everett founded to support women and children in the Democratic Republic of Congo, with one new home to be named in memory of Poovey. Paul Holmes a Court, the groom’s younger brother, was aboard the tram with his two school-age children—one of whom also broke an arm. Witnesses described chaos: screams, people thrown from the vehicle, and the tram sliding hundreds of yards. Zimbabwe’s rail system, long neglected amid economic decline, has seen three serious accidents in just one week. Officials have not confirmed if legal action will follow. Holmes a Court, whose father grew up in Zimbabwe, has deep personal ties to the region. Everett, known for covering conflict zones across Africa and the Middle East, had previously photographed Holmes a Court during a trip to trace his father’s legacy. Before the crash, he had planned to join her on a return trip to the DRC, where she was violently attacked in 2012. 'I’m not going to let my bride out of my sight,' he wrote on their registry. Despite the trauma, the pair chose to move forward—together.

article_content: Rodrigo Duterte, the former president of the Philippines known for his inflammatory rhetoric—including threats to 'shoot women in the vagina' and 'kill corrupt journalists'—once operated with near-total impunity. But for the first time since leaving office last year, he may finally face legal consequences. According to government documents released Wednesday, a prosecutor in Metro Manila has issued a subpoena requiring Duterte to respond to allegations that he made a grave threat against opposition lawmaker France Castro. Under Philippine law, a grave threat can carry a prison sentence of up to six months; if combined with local cybercrime statutes, the penalty could extend to six years. Duterte was ordered to appear in person at the prosecutor’s office on December 4 and 11 to submit a counter-affidavit. The subpoena explicitly states that no motions to dismiss will be accepted. The alleged threat occurred during an October 10 episode of Duterte’s local TV show, where he advised his daughter, Sara Duterte-Carpio—the current vice president and education secretary—to target 'Communists' with confidential intelligence funds. In Tagalog, he said: 'But your first target there with your intelligence funds, are you, you France, you Communists that I want to kill.' The clip, later shared widely on social media before being removed, was interpreted by Rep. France Castro as a direct threat against her. She filed a formal complaint on October 24, citing fear and intimidation stemming from the remarks. Duterte-Carpio had previously requested additional intelligence funding to combat communist indoctrination in schools—a request she has since withdrawn. Antonio La Viña, Castro’s legal counsel, anticipates formal indictment. 'It doesn’t matter what the intent is—if he was joking or not—he can’t hide behind that excuse anymore. He’s no longer president,' La Viña told TIME. 'It created fear. He must be held accountable.' If prosecuted, this would mark the first criminal case ever brought against Duterte in the Philippines. His six-year presidency (2016–2022) remains deeply controversial, largely due to his brutal anti-drug campaign. Official figures record at least 6,000 deaths in police operations, but human rights organizations estimate the true toll exceeds tens of thousands, including many unexplained killings. Duterte’s 'shoot-to-kill' policy for suspected drug offenders has been widely condemned as enabling extrajudicial executions. Since 2021, the International Criminal Court has been investigating whether these actions constitute crimes against humanity.

Però per primera vegada després de deixar l'oficina l'any passat, pot finalment haver d'enfrontar-se a conseqüències legals. Segons documents governamentals publicats dimecres, un fiscal de Metro Manila ha emès una citació que exigeix a Duterte que respongui a les acusacions d'haver fet una amenaça greu contra la diputada d'oposició France Castro. Segons la llei filipina, una amenaça greu pot portar una pena de presó fins a sis mesos; si es combina amb estatuts locals de ciberdelinqüència, la pena pot arribar a sis anys. Duterte va ser ordenat d'aparèixer en persona a la oficina del fiscal el 4 i 11 de desembre per presentar una contradeclaració. La citació especifica explícitament que no es permetran mocions per desestimar el cas. El vídeo, més tard compartit àmpliament a les xarxes socials abans de ser eliminat, va ser interpretat per la diputada France Castro com una amenaça directa contra ella. Va presentar una denúncia formal el 24 d'octubre, citant por i intimidació derivades de les seves paraules. Duterte-Carpio havia sol·licitat anteriorment fons intel·ligents addicionals per combatre la doctrinació comunista a les escoles — una sol·licitud que ha retirat posteriorment. Antonio La Viña, conseller legal de Castro, espera una acusació formal. 'No importa quin sigui l'intent — si estava bromejant o no — no pot amagar-se darrere d'aquesta excusa més. Ja no és president,' va dir La Viña a TIME. 'Ha creat por. Ha de ser responsabilitzat.' Si és processat, aquest seria el primer cas penal mai presentat contra Duterte als Filipins. El seu mandat de sis anys (2016–2022) continua molt controvertit, principalment per la seva brutal campanya contra les drogues. Les xifres oficials registren almenys 6.000 morts en operacions policials, però les organitzacions de drets humans estimen que la veritable xifra supera les desenes de milers, incloent moltes morts sense explicació oficial. La política de 'disparar-per-matar' de Duterte per a sospitosos de tràfic de drogues ha estat àmpliament condemnada com a habilitadora d'execucions extrajudicials. Des del 2021, la Cort Penal Internacional està investigant si aquestes accions constitueixen crims contra la humanitat.

article_content: Sudan has requested an emergency meeting of Arab foreign ministers in anticipation of a possible indictment of President Omar al-Bashir by the International Criminal Court (ICC) for genocide and crimes against humanity in Darfur. According to reports, ICC Chief Prosecutor Luis Moreno-Ocampo is set to announce the filing of an arrest warrant—a move that would make al-Bashir the first sitting president ever charged with genocide by the ICC. The United Nations estimates that more than 2.5 million people have been displaced and approximately 300,000 have died since the conflict in Darfur began in 2003. Sudanese authorities, however, dispute these figures, claiming only 10,000 deaths and rejecting accusations of genocide. Sudan’s ambassador to the UN, Adbalmahmood Abdalhaleem Mohamad, described the potential indictment as a 'criminal move' that would destabilize the country and urged the international community to oppose it. He vowed Sudan would resist the action 'by all possible legal means.' Meanwhile, the Arab League, led by Secretary-General Amr Moussa, is coordinating with Arab foreign ministers to convene an emergency session. The ICC prosecutor has previously stated that Sudan’s 'whole state apparatus' was mobilized to plan, commit, and conceal atrocities in Darfur. The conflict erupted when rebels in Darfur rose up against the Khartoum government, accusing it of favoring Arab communities over African ones. In response, the government allegedly armed and coordinated with the janjaweed militia, which carried out systematic attacks—including killings, rape, and forced displacement—on civilian populations. Human rights organizations and the UN hold the janjaweed responsible for most atrocities, including the use of rape as a weapon of war. Two other Sudanese figures, former interior minister Ahmad Harun and militia leader Ali Kushayb, have already been indicted by the ICC for similar crimes. As the announcement looms, UN humanitarian coordinator John Holmes confirmed aid agencies are taking precautions to safeguard operations, emphasizing that humanitarian assistance must continue regardless of political developments. The ICC, established under a treaty ratified by 106 nations (but not Sudan), has jurisdiction to prosecute individuals for genocide, war crimes, and crimes against humanity. An arrest warrant would enable detention of al-Bashir if he travels to any member state.

article_content: Last month, 15-year-old Joshua Scott from Dothan, Alabama, picked up a worn brown teddy bear at the Second Chance Thrift Shop, thinking it would be a sweet gift for his younger sister. But when he got home and hugged the plush toy, he felt something unusual — a small, rigid object tucked inside. Curious, he carefully unzipped a hidden compartment along the bear’s back and discovered a tiny metal urn containing human ashes. Shocked and deeply moved, Joshua immediately told his mother, Samantha Hallford. Now, the family is on a heartfelt mission to find out who the ashes belong to. 'It could be a child’s most cherished possession,' Samantha told WSFA-TV. 'Or maybe it’s the last piece of a parent, a sibling, even a soldier — something someone held onto until the very end. We can’t just leave it sitting here.' The thrift store, which accepts around ten full carloads of donated items every day, has no way to trace who brought in the bear. No donation logs, no receipts, no names. The family has visited nearby funeral homes, posted online, and reached out to community groups, but so far, no leads. Still, they refuse to give up. For them, this isn’t just about returning an object — it’s about restoring dignity to someone’s memory.

Per a ells, això no és només tornar un objecte — és restaurar la dignitat del record de qualcú.

article_content: Stan Wawrinka kicked off his Australian Open title defense with a commanding performance, cruising past Turkey’s Marsel Ilhan 6-1, 6-4, 6-2 in just 89 minutes on Rod Laver Arena. The Swiss star, seeded fourth, dominated from the outset, wrapping up the opening set in under 20 minutes and never looking back. Despite the weight of being a reigning Grand Slam champion — a role that often brings added pressure — Wawrinka appeared relaxed and focused, letting his racket do the talking. His serve was a weapon, landing 82% of first serves, and he converted crucial break points with precision, sealing the match with an unreturnable ace. Ilhan, ranked 100th and never having advanced beyond the second round at a major, struggled to find rhythm against Wawrinka’s consistent aggression. After the match, Wawrinka reflected on the emotional lift from the crowd, saying, 'The first Grand Slam is never easy, but I’m happy with how I played today. I’m glad to be back on court — I could feel everyone behind me.' But he stayed grounded: 'It’s just one match. The real work starts now.' The 29-year-old enters the second round riding high after helping Switzerland win its first-ever Davis Cup last year and capturing the Chennai Open title two weeks ago. His next challenger will be either Spain’s Pablo Andujar or Romania’s Marius Copil, both set to clash on Thursday.

L'estrella suïssa, quart caps de sèrie, va dominar des del principi, guanyant el primer set en menys de 20 minuts i mai mirant enrere. Malgrat la pressió de ser campió defensor d'un Grand Slam — un rol que sovint porta més pressió — Wawrinka va semblar relaxat i concentrat, deixant que la seva raqueta parlessin per ell. article_content: CNN — I am probably neither the first nor the last critic to say this, but Michel Hazanavicius’ 'The Artist' is a flawless film. There is literally nothing wrong with it. I have not a single nit to pick, no minor flaw to point out, and no moment that annoyed me. It is pure magic from the first frame to the last. It proves that to be moving, engaging, enthralling, and fun, films need not rely on sex, violence, color, or even spoken dialogue. That’s not to say I don’t love many films with all those elements—but 'The Artist' distills cinema to something it so rarely achieves: pure joy in art. This is not art for art’s sake; it is art for enjoyment’s sake. It is not merely an 'important' film we must watch because it is great art (though it is both important and artistically brilliant)—it is a film everyone should see because it is joyous. Stunningly beautiful, it is a throwback to the very reasons people first flocked to cinemas: the chance to escape their lives and inhabit someone else’s for a while. The story draws on familiar plot elements from 'Singin’ in the Rain,' 'Citizen Kane,' 'A Star Is Born,' and classic Hollywood melodrama. George Valentin (Jean Dujardin), a matinee idol of the silent screen, stars in swashbuckling adventures alongside his loyal Jack Russell terrier, Uggie. He is adored by men and women alike—the archetype: men want to be him; women want to be with him. At the premiere of his latest hit, George meets Peppy Miller (Bérénice Bejo), an aspiring actress, in a charming encounter: she’s swept into the crowd of autograph seekers and ends up beside him. She playfully plants a kiss on his cheek—landing them both on the cover of Variety—and igniting the plot. It’s a classic 'boy meets girl' twist. While George revels in his success and Peppy chases her dreams, his wife, Doris (Penelope Ann Miller), grows jealous. Though the photo is innocent, her unease feels warranted. Peppy lands a minor role in George’s next film, and their mutual attraction deepens. She is wide-eyed and new to the industry; he, a seasoned star and charmer who has been here before. George’s world remains intact—until studio head Al Zimmer (John Goodman) embraces talkies. Convinced the public will stay loyal to silents, George refuses to adapt. His career declines just as Peppy’s ascends. The collapse of the silent era, his crumbling marriage, and the stock market crash plunge George into alcoholism and self-loathing. Only his dog and chauffeur, Clifton (James Cromwell), remain loyal. Bitter, he lashes out at Peppy—the living symbol of his obsolescence. 'The Artist' is not truly silent—it features a rich musical score and carefully placed sound effects. Hazanavicius’ use of sound is ingenious (I won’t spoil it). But for all practical purposes, it is silent. Actors still speak their lines—we simply don’t hear them. For audiences, however, the absence of dialogue transforms viewing: we notice body language, framing, composition, and how music drives emotion. Hazanavicius directs with a deft touch and delightful whimsy. The film is filled with classic Hollywood sight gags. Dujardin and Bejo deliver charismatic, nuanced performances. A brief pantomime scene between Bejo and one of George’s suits is worth the ticket alone—don’t blink when Uggie appears! The filmmakers took a bold gamble: a black-and-white, silent film with two largely unknown leads. But after Dujardin won Best Actor at Cannes and rave reviews poured in, it became clear they had a masterpiece. A heartfelt love letter to cinema, 'The Artist' is packed with Easter eggs for cinephiles. It is comedy, melodrama, and romance—but above all, it fulfills cinema’s highest promise: taking us on a journey through love, loss, heartbreak, and redemption. Rated PG-13 for mild peril, a single offensive gesture, and frequent smoking—if those bother you.
translated_content: CNN — Probablement ni el primer ni l’últim crític a dir-ho, però 'The Artist' de Michel Hazanavicius és una pel·lícula impecable. No hi ha res que es pugui criticar. No tinc cap petita qüestió per fer, cap defecte menor per assenyalar ni cap moment que m’hagi molestat. És màgia pura des del primer quadre fins al darrer. Demostra que per ser emotiva, atractiva, envolvent i divertida, una pel·lícula no necessita sexe, violència, color ni tan sols diàleg parlats. No vol dir que no m’agradi moltes pel·lícules amb tot això, però 'The Artist' redueix el cinema a alguna cosa que rarament aconsegueix: una alegría pura en l’art. Aquesta no és art per l’art; és art per la diversió. No és només una pel·lícula 'important' que hem de veure perquè és gran art (tot i que ho és), sinó una pel·lícula que tothom hauria de veure perquè és alegre. És increïblement bella. És un retorn als motius per als quals la gent va començar a anar al cinema: la possibilitat d’escapar de les seves vides i viure la vida d’una altra persona durant un temps. La història es basa en elements de 'Singin’ in the Rain,' 'Citizen Kane,' 'A Star Is Born' i el millor del melodrama hollywoodià. George Valentin (Jean Dujardin) és un ídol de pantalla silenciosa, que fa aventures d’acció amb el seu fidel terrier Jack Russell, Uggie. És adorat per homes i dones: els homes volen ser com ell; les dones volen estar amb ell. A l’estrena de la seva última pel·lícula, George coneix Peppy Miller (Bérénice Bejo), una actriu aspirant, en un encontre encantador: ella és arrossegada per la multitud de fans i acaba al costat d’ell. Ella li posa un petó a la galta—i així els dos apareixen a la portada de Variety—i posa en marxa la trama. És una variació clàssica del 'home coneix dona'. Mentre George gaudir de l’èxit i Peppy intenta aprofitar la seva fama immediata, la seva esposa, Doris (Penelope Ann Miller), bull de gelosia. Tot i que la foto és totalment innocenta, es sent que les seves por podrien no ser infundades. Peppy aconsegueix un paper secundari a la següent pel·lícula de George i l’atracció entre els dos comença a manifestar-se. Ella és una jove actriu novella; ell, un estel experimentat i seductor que ja ha passat per això abans. El món de George roman intacte... fins que el cap del studio, Al Zimmer (John Goodman), adopta els films sonors. Convencut que el futur és el so, George creu que el públic continuarà preferint els silents. La seva carrera comença a declinar, mentre la de Peppy puja. La fi de l’era silenciosa, la seva matrimonial en crisi i la caiguda de la borsa llancen George a un espiral d’alcoholisme i autoodi. Només el seu gos i el seu conductor, Clifton (James Cromwell), li romanen fidels. Amargat, es llença contra Peppy—el símbol viu del seu declivi. 'The Artist' no és realment silenciosa: té una banda sonora rica i efectes de so cuidadosament col·locats. L’ús del so de Hazanavicius és enginyós (no ho desvelaré). Però en tots els aspectes pràctics, és silenciosa. Els actors encara parlen les seves línies—nosaltres simplement no les escoltem. Però per a l’espectador, l’absència de diàleg transforma l’experiència: fixem la vista en el llenguatge corporal, la composició, l’ús dels objectes i com la música impulsa l’acció. Hazanavicius dirigeix amb un toc elegant i un gran sentit de l’humor. La pel·lícula està plena de gags visuals en la millor tradició hollywoodiana. Dujardin i Bejo ofereixen interpretacions carismàtiques i nuançades. Una breu escena de mímica entre Bejo i una de les samarretes de George val la entrada sola—no us perdeu el gos! Els creadors van prendre un gran risc: una pel·lícula en blanc i negre, silenciosa, amb dos protagonistes gairebé desconeguts als EUA. Però després que Dujardin guanyés el premi al millor actor a Canes i les crítiques comencessin a arribar, van saber que tenien un èxit. Una carta d’amor sincera al cinema, 'The Artist' conté molts homenatges i detalls per als aficionats. És comèdia, melodrama i romança, però sobretot compleix la promesa més alta del cinema: ens porta en un viatge a través de l’amor, la pèrdua, el cor trencat i la desesperació, i torna a l’amor. Classificada PG-13 per peril moderat, un gest ofensiu i fumar freqüent—si això et molesta.

article_content: A single mother in Sunderland was targeted by multiple men after a fake dating profile was created in her name. The profile, posted on Plenty of Fish, falsely claimed she was 'up for anything' and instructed men to meet her at Boots, where she works as a sales assistant. Lynn Gunning, 45, a mother of two including a 12-year-old son with autism, said she was 'beside herself' when men began arriving at her workplace expecting sexual encounters. She had no knowledge of the profile until one man showed it to her on his phone. 'All you need is a photo of someone,' she said, 'and anyone with a very sick and twisted mind could do what was done to me.' The ordeal left her terrified for her children’s safety. 'I was so scared they could follow me home,' she said. Her family was deeply concerned. After reporting the incident to Northumbria Police, the force contacted Plenty of Fish, which promptly removed the profile. However, authorities have yet to identify the person behind it. Gunning, who is also a student at Sunderland College, expressed outrage that the perpetrator remains at large. 'I want to have my story told so people understand how dangerous this can be. I hope this never happens to anyone else.'

article_content: In Fort Mill, South Carolina, Roy Tidwell runs Charity Services International, a small logistics firm that helps charities ship donated goods — from bottled water to medical supplies — across the country and abroad. He says his mission is simple: get essential items to those in need at minimal cost. 'I’m not making a fortune,' he says. 'I’m just helping move things that matter, often for pennies on the dollar.' But Tidwell’s business sits at the center of a growing controversy: how charities assign dollar values to non-cash donations. In 2009, the Disabled Veterans National Foundation used his services to send what it claimed was over $800,000 worth of clothing and gear to U.S. Vets in Arizona. Yet U.S. Vets told CNN they never requested the shipment and had no idea it was coming — and estimated the real value at a tiny fraction of that number. Similar issues arose last year when the same foundation shipped what it said was half a million dollars in supplies — including hand sanitizer and tote bags — to a VA facility in Arkansas. Officials there confirmed receiving the items but denied ever providing a valuation or even asking for them. The problems aren’t limited to the U.S. SPCA International, another of Tidwell’s clients, reported donating $816,000 in deworming and antibiotic medications to an elephant sanctuary in Nepal. But the customs paperwork showed a declared value of just $2,500. Tidwell defends such discrepancies, arguing that value should reflect the cost in the exporting country — not what similar goods cost locally. 'It’s not about what you can buy in Nepal,' he says. 'It’s about what the medicine cost in the U.S.' Yet critics say this reasoning masks manipulation. Daniel Borochoff of CharityWatch calls it a systemic problem. 'Many charities don’t even buy these items — they’re donated. Then they slap on inflated prices to make their program spending look better,' he explains. 'It’s like pretending a free t-shirt is worth $100 so you can say you spent 90% of your budget on missions instead of admin.' Even Operation Blessing International, run by Pat Robertson, stopped counting anti-parasite meds in their reports until clear industry standards emerge. Borochoff adds that nonprofit leaders sometimes coordinate to set fake benchmarks — calling them ‘industry standards’ — to justify inflated numbers. 'It’s a race to the top,' he says. 'If everyone else says their canned soup is worth $50, you feel pressured to do the same.' The IRS and Congress are now paying attention. With charities able to hide exactly what they’re sending and at what price, the public has little way to verify claims. Borochoff urges full transparency: 'Report what you paid. Not what you wish it was worth.' Until then, he says, skepticism isn’t just reasonable — it’s necessary.

Diu que la seva missió és senzilla: portar articles essencials a qui els necessita amb un cost mínim. 'No estic fent una fortuna,' diu. 'Només ajudo a moure coses que importen, sovint per uns centims del seu valor.' Però el negoci de Tidwell es troba al centre d’una creixent polèmica: com les organitzacions benèfiques assignen un valor monetari a les donacions en espècie. El 2009, la Disabled Veterans National Foundation va utilitzar els seus serveis per enviar el que va afirmar que eren més de 800.000 dòlars en roba i equipament a U.S. Vets a Arizona. Però U.S. Vets va dir a CNN que mai van sol·licitar l’enviament i no sabien que arribava — i van estimar que el valor real era una fracció molt petita d’aquesta xifra. Problemes similars van sorgir l’any passat quan la mateixa fundació va enviar el que va dir que eren mig milió de dòlars en subministraments — incloent desinfectant de mans i bosses — a una instal·lació de la VA a Little Rock, Arkansas. Les autoritats van confirmar que van rebre els articles, però van negar haver proporcionat mai una valoració o haver-los demanat. Els problemes no es limiten als EUA. Però els documents aduaners mostraven un valor declarat de només 2.500 dòlars. Tidwell defensa aquestes discrepàncies, argumentant que el valor ha de reflectir el cost al país d’exportació, no el preu local. 'No es tracta de què pots comprar al Nepal,' diu. 'Es tracta de quant va costar el medicament als EUA.' Però els crítics diuen que aquest raonament amaga manipulació. Daniel Borochoff de CharityWatch el qualifica de problema sistèmic. 'Moltes organitzacions ni tan sols compren aquests articles — els reben com a donació. Després, els posen preus inflats per fer que el seu gasto en programes sembli més alt,' explica. 'És com fingir que una samarreta gratuïta val 100 dòlars per dir que gastes un 90% del pressupost en missions en lloc d’administració.' Inclusivament Operation Blessing International, gestionada per Pat Robertson, va deixar de comptabilitzar els medicaments antiparasitaris en els seus informes fins que surtin normes clares de l’indústria. Borochoff afirma que alguns líders sense ànim de lucre coordinen per establir referències falses — anomenant-les 'normes de l’indústria' — per justificar preus inflats. 'És una carrera cap a dalt,' diu. 'Si tots diuen que la seva sopa enllaçada val 50 dòlars, et sents pressionat a fer el mateix.' L’IRS i el Congrés estan començant a prestar atenció. Amb les organitzacions benèfiques podent ocultar exactament què estan enviant i a quin preu, el públic no té manera de verificar les afirmacions. Borochoff exigeix transparència total: 'Informe el que va pagar. No el que desitja que valgui.' Fins llavors, diu, el pesimisme no només és raonable — és necessari.

article_content: Thirty-four years after his friend and songwriting partner John Lennon was fatally shot, Paul McCartney still recalls the overwhelming shock of that day. 'For days, I just couldn’t believe he was gone,' McCartney told UK talk-show host Jonathan Ross. 'It was just a huge shock.' Lennon was killed on December 8, 1980, outside his New York residence, The Dakota, by Mark David Chapman. He was 40 years old and had just released 'Double Fantasy,' an album with his wife, Yoko Ono, following a five-year absence from the public eye. At the time, McCartney faced criticism for his seemingly casual response — 'It's a drag, innit?' — when asked about the news. He now admits he was emotionally paralyzed. 'I was at home. It was early morning. The call came... it was just so horrific. I couldn’t take it in.' McCartney and Lennon had known each other since 1957, when they were teenagers. They saw themselves as brothers — a bond Lennon himself affirmed in his final interview: 'He’s like a brother. I love him. Families have their ups and downs, their quarrels. But at the end of the day, I’d do anything for him — and I think he’d do anything for me.' Despite a strained relationship after the Beatles’ 1970 breakup, the two had reconciled before Lennon’s death. 'I’m so glad,' McCartney said. 'It would have been the worst thing in the world if our great bond had turned sour and then he was taken. The fact that we got back together gave me some peace. We were good friends.' 'The story about the breakup? It’s true. But it’s not the main part. The main part was the affection.'

'Estava a casa. Era matí. Va arribar la trucada... va ser tan horripilant. No podia assimilar-ho.' McCartney i Lennon es coneixien des de 1957, quan eren adolescents. Es veien com germans — un vincle que Lennon va confirmar en la seva última entrevista: 'És com un germà. L'estimo molt. Les famílies tenen els seus alts i baixos, les seves discutides. Però al final del dia, faria qualsevol cosa per ell — i crec que ell faria qualsevol cosa per mi.' 'La història sobre la ruptura? És veritat. Però no és la part principal. La part principal era l’afecte.'

article_content: Confronted by police attempting to arrest him for allegedly selling illegal cigarettes, Eric Garner raised both hands and calmly told officers not to touch him. Seconds later, a video showed an officer behind him placing Garner — a 350-pound man — in a chokehold and pulling him to the sidewalk, rolling him onto his stomach. 'I can't breathe! I can't breathe!' Garner repeated, his voice muffled against the pavement. The video, recorded on Thursday, shows the Staten Island man lying motionless on the ground afterward. An asthmatic, Garner was later pronounced dead at a nearby hospital, according to CNN affiliate WCBS. Police stated he suffered a heart attack en route to the hospital. 'This is a terrible tragedy that occurred yesterday — one no family should ever endure,' said New York Mayor Bill de Blasio, calling the video 'very troubling.' According to WCBS, 43-year-old Garner, a father of six, had a prior arrest in May for selling untaxed cigarettes. Officer Daniel Pantaleo, seen in the video applying the chokehold, was placed on modified duty and stripped of his badge and firearm as the NYPD investigates. The chokehold is explicitly prohibited by NYPD policy. Two EMTs and two paramedics were suspended without pay, confirmed Erika Hellstrom, vice president of development at Richmond University Medical Center. Patrolmen's Benevolent Association President Patrick J. Lynch called Pantaleo’s reassignment 'a completely unwarranted, knee-jerk reaction for political reasons,' arguing it prejudiced the case and denied the officer the presumption of innocence. On Saturday, Garner’s family and friends joined Rev. Al Sharpton in Upper Manhattan to demand a full investigation. Garner’s wife was scheduled to speak but became too emotional, WCBS reported. New York photographer Joel Graham, who attended the two-hour demonstration, shared his images with CNN iReport. He said he captured them while walking with protesters traveling from New Brighton Church to the site of the incident. 'This crowd was made up of good, well-meaning people who believed peace was the only path forward — they were determined to keep things calm after Eric’s death,' Graham said. He added that he had known Garner personally: 'I’m an urban art photographer; I talk to everyone on the streets of NYC. I’d often chat with Eric near the Staten Island Ferry. I felt empathy for how he must have felt struggling to breathe, and deep sympathy for his family. This protest was heartfelt because everyone loved Eric.'

No puc respirar!', va repetir Garner, la seva veu amortida contra el paviment. El vídeo, registrat el dijous, mostra l'home de Staten Island inconscient al sòl després de l'esdeveniment. article_content: By James Nye. PUBLISHED: 02:00 EST, 23 December 2012. | UPDATED: 05:48 EST, 23 December 2012. The distraught police chief of Newtown spoke about the absolute 'carnage' he witnessed as one of the first responders inside Sandy Hook Elementary School. Police Chief Michael Kehoe said he was left speechless as he moved through the building, describing the shooting as 'devastating, absolutely devastating.' When he entered one classroom where shooter Adam Lanza had killed 14 first graders and their teacher, Kehoe said it was clear no one had survived. 'It was a very tragic scene on every level — you could see the carnage that was present,' Kehoe told CBS News about the massacre that claimed the lives of 20 children and six staff members at the hands of the 20-year-old gunman. 'It was devastating, absolutely devastating. I had no words. I felt anger toward the person who did this.' Kehoe revealed that Newtown police had to force entry through the back of the school, as the doors were secured. 'We broke out a window,' he said. 'If a room was locked, that meant the teachers had done their job — locking their doors and hiding their children from danger.' By the time Kehoe arrived, Lanza was already dead. But Kehoe said his dominant emotion was regret that he hadn’t arrived sooner to stop the killings. 'You feel a sense of guilt that you weren’t there quickly enough,' Kehoe said. 'But I also know our response stopped the threat — he could not proceed further.' Newtown Police Captain Joe Rios, stationed outside during the incident, recalled witnessing children emerging from the building. 'It was miraculous. I kept seeing children come out — and I kept hoping for more.' 'Walking inside, the crime scene was horrific — seeing adults and children dead in the classrooms. It was impossible to comprehend,' Rios said. Kehoe added that the previous year, he had visited the school to read a story to a kindergarten class — some of whom may have been among those killed. 'I may have read to some of these students. That hit me hard. I feel guilt — deep down, I believe our job is to keep kids safe. Schools should be places of learning.' The interview followed a nationwide moment of silence held on December 22, marking one week since Adam Lanza killed his mother and then attacked the school, killing 20 children and six adults before taking his own life. Connecticut Governor Dannel Malloy urged residents to observe a moment of silence at 9:30 a.m. to honor the victims. Governors in Maine, Illinois, Michigan, and other states echoed the call. Bells rang across the nation. President Barack Obama joined millions of Americans in observing the silence. At Washington National Cathedral, bells tolled 28 times during an interfaith memorial — 26 for the victims, two for Lanza and his mother. 'We have a moral obligation to stand with victims of gun violence and work to end it,' said Reverend Gary Hall, dean of the cathedral. 'Let us pray for the courage to act, so this murderous violence is never repeated.' The Nasdaq stock exchange paused operations briefly in remembrance, though trading resumed normally. On the morning of December 14, 2012, Adam Lanza, a 20-year-old man with a documented history of social withdrawal and mental health challenges, drove to the school armed with an assault rifle and opened fire, killing 20 children and six staff members. On the day of the article’s publication, the families of Emilie Parker, Ana Marquez-Greene, and Josephine Gay held the final funerals for the 26 victims.

article_content: Fox has officially greenlit a third season of 'The X Factor,' signaling the show’s continued momentum. He emphasized that the show’s core mission remains finding authentic, standout talent — a goal now entering its most thrilling phase: the live performances. With just days to go before the first live show, Cowell promised high-energy moments and unforgettable acts. So far this season, the program has drawn an average of 10.6 million viewers and a 3.9 rating in the key 18–49 demographic, placing it firmly among the top 15 primetime shows in those age groups. On Tuesday night, viewers will tune in at 9:30 p.m. to see how judges Cowell, Demi Lovato, L.A. Reid, and Britney Spears narrow the field to 16 finalists. Then, on November 1, those 16 acts will take the stage in a special two-and-a-half-hour live event hosted by Khloé Kardashian Odom and Mario Lopez.

article_content: For the first time in his life, 50-year-old Westley Grey is preparing to see his father on Christmas Day — not in person, but through a video call. Their reunion last October marked the end of a half-century separation, beginning when Westley and his twin brother David discovered their biological father, Westley Snr Moorehead, living in Texas. Their mother, Thomasina, had raised them alone after Westley Snr was deployed during the Cuban Missile Crisis in the early 1960s, leaving her pregnant with the twins and unable to reach him. Westley Snr, who joined the US Navy at 17, had no knowledge of his sons until David traveled across the Atlantic to find him. Westley, who lives with learning disabilities and receives long-term support from the Scottish charity Quarriers, helped fund the journey through community fundraisers. With assistance from two of his support workers, he joined David in Texas for an emotional first meeting. They also met their stepmother, Bernadine, who had dementia, and three other siblings. Six weeks later, Bernadine passed away. Now, as Westley Snr faces his first Christmas without her, the family will gather virtually — Westley in Scotland, David still in the US, and the step-siblings nearby. Westley calls the reunion 'the best year of my life' and says seeing his dad for the first time left him speechless. 'I just hugged him,' he says. Quarriers’ CEO described the story as one of the most moving in the charity’s 140-year history, praising the team’s dedication to helping Westley achieve his lifelong dream.

La seva mare, Thomasina, els havia criat sols després que Westley Snr fos destinat durant la crisi dels míssils de Cuba als inicis dels anys 60, deixant-la embarassada dels bessons i sense poder contactar amb ell. Westley Snr, que va ingressar a la Marina dels EUA als 17 anys, no tenia cap coneixement dels seus fills fins que David va travessar l'Atlàntic per trobar-lo. Westley, que viu amb discapacitats d'aprenentatge i rep suport a llarg termini de la caritat escocesa Quarriers, va ajudar a finançar el viatge a través de campanyes de recaptació de fons. Amb l'ajuda de dos dels seus treballadors de suport, es va unir a David a Texas per una emocionant primera trobada. També van conèixer la seva madrastra, Bernadine, que patia demència, i tres altres germans. Seixanta dies després, Bernadine va morir. Ara, mentre Westley Snr afronta el seu primer Nadal sense ella, la família es reunirà virtualment — Westley a Escòcia, David encara als EUA, i els germans adoptius a prop. Westley diu que la reunió ha estat 'l'any més bo de la meva vida' i que veure el seu pare per primera vegada el va deixar sense paraules. 'Només li he donat un gran abraç', diu. El director general de Quarriers va descriure aquesta història com una de les més emocionants dels 140 anys de la caritat, elogiant la dedicació de l'equip per ajudar Westley a assolir el seu somni de tota la vida.

article_content: Stockholm may not rival Parisian haute couture or Milanese glamour, but Sweden’s fashion scene is carving out a powerful global identity through its signature minimalist aesthetic. 'Sweden is the only country to have developed a uniquely recognizable fashion style,' says Yvan Rodic, a London-based fashion blogger and photographer. Rodic, along with fellow influencers like Susie Bubble and The Telegraph’s Hilary Alexander, visited Stockholm during Mercedes-Benz Fashion Week Stockholm to witness the unveiling of new collections from leading Swedish designers. Stockholm Fashion Week continues through February 12. Rodic credits the global appeal of Swedish fashion to its understated fabrics, restrained color palettes, and accessible price points — a refreshing contrast to what he describes as the 'expensive, serious, and pretentious' offerings from Paris and Milan. While H&M remains the most widely known Swedish export, other labels — including Cheap Monday, Tiger of Sweden, and Acne Studios — are gaining international traction. Acne denim has been worn by stars like Rihanna, Alexander Skarsgård, and Jared Leto. Meanwhile, Ed Westwick of 'Gossip Girl' has been spotted in J. Lindeberg. Even high-end designers are thriving: Mayla, founded by Marlene 'Mayla' Abraham, has sold dresses to premium retailers in Tokyo, San Francisco, and New York, before expanding across Scandinavia. Sweden’s textile exports reached SEK 10 billion ($1.5 billion) in 2010 — a 10% rise from 2009 — a remarkable feat given that overall national exports dropped 17% amid the global financial crisis, according to Sweden’s Minister for Trade, Ewa Björling. Björling, who is traveling to Shanghai this fall to promote Swedish fashion, believes exports could double by 2015 by tapping into emerging markets. Rodic attributes much of Sweden’s fashion success to its pioneering blogging culture. 'Sweden led the world in fashion blogging,' he says. 'For over a decade, people globally have turned to Swedish blogs for visual inspiration — even if they didn’t understand the language. These blogs taught them about the brands and how to build stylish wardrobes affordably.' He adds: 'It was the perfect fit for blogging — promoting individuality, authenticity, and accessibility — and turned Sweden into a fashion phenomenon.'

Rodic, juntament amb altres influenciadors com Susie Bubble i Hilary Alexander del Telegraph, va visitar Estocolm durant la Mercedes-Benz Fashion Week Stockholm per veure la presentació de les noves col·leccions dels dissenyadors suecs més importants. La Setmana de la Moda d'Estocolm continua fins al 12 de febrer. Rodic atribueix l'atractiu global de la moda sueca als teixits sobtats, les paletes de colors restringides i els preus accessibles — un contrast refrescant respecte als productes que ell descriu com a 'caros, seriosos i pretenciosos' de París i Milà. Mentre H&M roman la marca sueca més coneguda, altres etiquetes — com Cheap Monday, Tiger of Sweden i Acne Studios — estan guanyant presència internacional. Els jeans d'Acne han estat portats per estrelles com Rihanna, Alexander Skarsgård i Jared Leto. Mentre tant, Ed Westwick de 'Gossip Girl' ha estat vist amb J. Lindeberg. Inclusivament els dissenyadors de luxe estan prosperant: Mayla, fundada per Marlene 'Mayla' Abraham, ha venut vestits a botigues premium a Tokio, San Francisco i Nova York, abans d'expandir-se per l'Escandinàvia. Les exportacions textiles de Suècia van arribar a 10.000 milions de SEK (1.500 milions de dòlars) el 2010 — un augment del 10% respecte al 2009 — un fet notable donat que les exportacions nacionals totals van caure un 17% durant la crisi financera global, segons la ministra de Comerç de Suècia, Ewa Björling. Björling, que viatjarà a Xangai aquesta tardor per promocionar la moda sueca, creu que les exportacions podrien duplicar-se cap al 2015 si s'apunten als mercats emergents. Rodic atribueix gran part del èxit de la moda sueca a la seva cultura pionera del blogging. 'Suècia va liderar el món en blogging de moda,' diu. 'Durant més d'una dècada, gent de tot el món ha recorregut als blogs suecs per inspiració visual — fins i tot si no entenien la llengua. Aquests blogs els van ensenyar sobre les marques i com construir armaris elegants sense gastar una fortuna.' Afegeix: 'Va ser la combinació perfecta per al blogging — promocionant la individualitat, l'autenticitat i l'accessibilitat — i va convertir Suècia en un fenomen de moda.'

article_content: Washington (CNN) — The current large-scale U.S.-South Korean naval exercise off the west coast of Korea serves multiple purposes. Following last week’s North Korean attack on a South Korean island, the primary goal is to send a clear message to Pyongyang: Washington and Seoul possess both the capability and the will to respond with overwhelming force to any further acts of aggression. A secondary objective is to strengthen U.S.-ROK (Republic of Korea) coordination in joint military responses and to bolster anti-submarine capabilities — capabilities that were critically lacking last March when North Korea sank the South Korean naval vessel ROKS Cheonan in international waters. Given that past North Korean provocations have rarely resulted in serious consequences, it may be difficult to convince Pyongyang that 'this time we’re serious.' Although South Korea responded with artillery fire after last week’s shelling, the response was poorly executed and caused minimal damage. What is needed is a credible threat of a harsh retaliatory response — one that deters future attacks without provoking North Korean escalation or triggering a preemptive war based on fears of an imminent U.S.-led invasion. Despite declaring an 'ultra-emergency wartime situation,' the North Korean regime is not suicidal; it is unlikely to take actions that would inevitably lead to its own destruction. Yet its long-standing belief that it can act with impunity has been reinforced by years of muted responses — from South Korea’s limited reaction after the Cheonan sinking, to the absence of meaningful punishment following its violations of agreements not to test intercontinental ballistic missiles or nuclear weapons. Even past acts of aggression — such as assassination attempts against South Korean presidents and the bombing of a civilian Korean airliner — yielded little lasting consequence for North Korea. Fear of reigniting the Korean War has historically deterred stronger U.S.-ROK retaliation. This time, however, Washington and Seoul appear determined not only to demonstrate their resolve to respond proportionally if necessary, but also to strengthen existing UN-backed sanctions targeting the DPRK’s illicit activities and elite networks. Another dimension of these exercises — which include the aircraft carrier USS George Washington and its strike group — is to signal to China that, despite its vocal objections, the United States asserts its right to operate freely in international waters in defense of its national interests. The intent is not to provoke China; Washington prefers cooperation over confrontation. But for years, U.S. appeals to China to curb North Korea’s behavior have fallen on deaf ears. Instead, China’s tolerance has enabled Pyongyang’s defiance — contributing to stalled nuclear talks, the Cheonan sinking, and now a deliberate attack on a South Korean island that killed both civilians and military personnel. Thus, the U.S. message to Beijing is: 'If you cannot help bring North Korea to halt its provocations, we will take actions that, while not directed at you, will cause you discomfort.' Should this push China to exert greater pressure on Pyongyang, that outcome would be welcomed. Earlier this year, China loudly opposed any U.S. naval exercises in the Yellow Sea — particularly the deployment of an aircraft carrier. But given these constraints, the United States had to assert its freedom of navigation rights. The timing — coinciding with a planned Chinese state visit to Washington — was not ideal, but it was dictated by Pyongyang’s actions. Some observers argue that engagement alone can change North Korea’s behavior. The United States is willing to engage — including through serious negotiations. But it refuses to ignore Pyongyang’s aggressive military actions or its blatant violations of international pledges and UN resolutions on denuclearization. Nor will the U.S. accept the DPRK as a de facto nuclear weapons state by negotiating without first seeing concrete evidence of North Korea’s commitment to abandon its nuclear program — even if doubts remain about implementation. If North Korea takes meaningful steps to reduce tensions with the South and demonstrates sincere intent to denuclearize, prospects for reviving the six-party talks will improve. Until then, the United States will continue to stand firmly behind its South Korean ally in countering Pyongyang’s threats.

article_content: A second teenage girl has died following a devastating hit-and-run in northern Georgia. Juliana Ferrell, 16, was pronounced dead on Friday at approximately 2 p.m. She was injured earlier in the week alongside two other girls when a locksmith, chasing a 23-year-old man who refused to pay for a car lockout service, lost control of his vehicle. Mother Jane Ferrell told reporters she believed her daughter would not survive her injuries. Juliana passed away Friday. The incident occurred on Sunday night in Kennesaw, Georgia, after Tansu Kanlica, 27, pursued Garrett Anderson, 23, who had refused to pay $175 for unlocking his car. Anderson fled the scene before payment. Reina As-Salaam, 15, was pronounced dead at the scene. A third girl, Monica Epps, 16, was hospitalized with multiple broken bones but is expected to recover. Police immediately issued a first-degree vehicular homicide warrant for Kanlica upon learning of Ferrell’s death. Kanlica, who worked for a locksmith service, was called to unlock Anderson’s vehicle. After completing the service, Anderson drove off without paying. Kanlica followed in his silver 2004 Nissan van on Barrett Lakes Boulevard, approaching Shiloah Valley Drive just before 8 p.m. Reports state Anderson made a sudden stop, causing Kanlica’s van to lose control, leave the roadway, and strike the three girls walking to a nearby movie theater. article_content: In 2008, the Environment Agency drafted a plan to intentionally allow more frequent flooding across the Somerset Levels — not as an accident, but as a strategic decision to restore wetland habitats. Documents from the agency reveal that protecting species like water voles, greater water parsnips, and silver diving beetles was prioritized over maintaining traditional flood defenses for homes and farms. Critics say this policy ignored decades of human settlement and infrastructure, especially as river dredging, once routine, was abandoned. Since the last dredging in 2003, the rivers’ ability to carry water has dropped by nearly half, turning once-drainable fields into permanent marshes. When floods hit again in late 2013, residents were stunned to hear agency leaders call the situation a 'success story' — pointing to the fact that 1.3 million other properties were spared. But locals, especially in villages like Moorland, felt mocked. Their pumps sat idle, choked by silt, and promises of dredging had gone unfulfilled. Meanwhile, in the north of the Levels, the Huntspill Drain — a man-made channel kept clear — continues to effectively divert floodwaters, proving that proper maintenance works. The agency’s logic, laid out in its Parrett Catchment Flood Management Plan, was grounded in EU environmental rules requiring protection of habitats shaped by centuries of human land use. Yet the unintended consequence? Even the wildlife they aimed to save — like the elusive water vole — vanished as their habitats drowned under persistent water. Farmers and residents now argue the policy wasn’t just misguided — it was a slow-motion abandonment of communities under the guise of ecology. Prime Minister David Cameron called the floods 'biblical,' but locals insist they weren’t inevitable. Had the rivers been maintained, water levels could have dropped within days between storms. Instead, what was meant to be ecological restoration became a catastrophe for both people and nature.

Els documents de l'agència revelen que protegir espècies com les vises d'aigua, les pastanagues d'aigua majors i els escarabats platejats de buceig es va prioritzar sobre el manteniment de les defenses contra inundacions tradicionals per a cases i granjes. Els crítics diuen que aquesta política va ignorar desenes d'anys d'assentament humà i infraestructura, especialment quan la draga dels rius, abans rutinària, va ser abandonada. Des de l'última draga el 2003, la capacitat dels rius per transportar aigua ha caigut gairebé a la meitat, convertint camps abans drainables en marismes permanents. Quan les inundacions van tornar a arribar a finals de 2013, els veïns van quedar estupefactes d'escoltar els líders de l'agència anomenar la situació una 'història d'èxit' — assenyalant que 1,3 milions d'altres propietats van ser salvades. Però els veïns, especialment en pobles com Moorland, van sentir-se burlats. Les seves bombes estaven inactives, obstruïdes per fang, i les promeses de draga no s'havien complert. Mentre tant, al nord dels Nivells, el Canal Huntspill — un canal artifici mantingut net — continua desviant eficaçment les aigües d'inundació, provant que el manteniment adequat funciona. La lògica de l'agència, exposada en el seu Pla de Gestió d'inundacions de la Conca del Parrett, es basava en normatives ambientals de la UE que requereixen protegir hàbitats formats durant segles per l'ús humà de la terra. Tanmateix, la conseqüència no intencionada? Fins i tot la vida silvestre que volien salvar — com l'elusive vis d'aigua — va desaparèixer mentre els seus hàbitats es van enfonsar sota aigües persistents. Si els rius haguessin estat mantenits, els nivells d'aigua haurien pogut baixar en dies entre tempestes. En lloc d'això, el que estava previst com a restauració ecològica es va convertir en una catàstrofe tant per a les persones com per a la natura.

article_content: On September 11, 2001, Melbourne, Australia, evacuated its own World Trade Center — a modest building on the banks of the Yarra River, barely 10,000 miles from New York. Once a casino, it had briefly housed a Madam Tussauds waxwork exhibition. If you drilled a hole straight through the Earth from Ground Zero, you’d emerge not far from there. Australia, after all, is famously remote. A flight to Sydney takes 15 hours from Los Angeles, 21 from London, 14 from Johannesburg, and 10 from Tokyo. There’s rarely a reason to stop in Australia unless you’re heading to Antarctica. This isolation defines Australia. It allowed Aboriginal cultures to thrive undisturbed for 40,000 years, nurtured unique wildlife found nowhere else, and made it the perfect site for Britain’s 1788 penal colony — a place to exile those unwanted by the empire. It’s a land you go to escape the world. And yet, on Monday, the world turned to Sydney, where a man with a gun took hostages in a cafe, claiming to act for the Islamic State. Reports describe him as Man Haron Monis — a self-proclaimed cleric with a history of hostility toward Australia’s military role in Afghanistan. He was likely a dangerous loner, not part of an organized terror cell. Still, by the end of the siege, two innocent people were dead. This wasn’t Australia’s first encounter with terrorism. On 9/11, when terrorists struck New York, Melbourne evacuated its WTC — not because it was a target, but because the horror felt too real. That day, every fear seemed possible. 'We are all Americans,' Australians declared — though, technically, it was already September 12 there. The tragedy, once distant, became personal. But as the 'War on Terror' shifted to Iraq and American flags flew on global screens, it became clear: 9/11 was an American story. Australia sent troops to Afghanistan and Iraq — out of loyalty — but remained an observer, watching from afar. In 2002, 88 Australians died in the Bali bombings. Bali is just six hours from Sydney. Yet even then, it felt 'elsewhere.' Later, police raids across Australian cities uncovered alleged terror plots. Officials warned: extremists were growing within our borders. Australia lives a charmed life. Streets are safe. Weather is perfect. People are kind. The ocean, they say, keeps danger out — or at least delays it. We grumble about expensive cars or delayed Netflix releases, but that distance has preserved our way of life amid relentless globalization. For over a decade, we’ve had space to debate freedom versus security — without the pressure of a recent national trauma. If this Sydney gunman had ranted about taxes or car prices, we’d call him a disturbed individual — not a terrorist. But the truth is deeper: Australia’s oceans are shrinking. Technology now connects a man in Bexley North to extremists halfway across the globe more intimately than to his next-door neighbor. Toxic ideologies travel faster than ships ever did. Whether labeled a siege or terrorism, this attack was something that used to happen 'Over There.' Now, it’s here. It wasn’t surprising. It came quieter than it might have. Today, life resumes. But the charm is fading. We are no longer so far away.

Abans havia estat un casino i breument va acollir una exposició de cera de Madam Tussauds. Si es fes un forat recte a través del centre de la Terra des de Ground Zero, es sortiria no molt lluny d'allà. Austràlia, després de tot, és famosa per la seva remotesa. Un vol a Sydney triga 15 hores des de Los Angeles, 21 des de Londres, 14 des de Joanesburg i 10 des de Tokio. Rarament hi ha raó per aturar-se a Austràlia si no s'hi va cap a l'Antàrtida. Aquesta aïllament defineix Austràlia. Va permetre que les cultures aborígens floreixin sense pertorbacions durant 40.000 anys, va alimentar fauna i flora úniques al món i va fer que fos el lloc perfecte per a la colònia penal britànica de 1788: un lloc per exiliar els indesitjables de l'imperi. És un lloc al qual vas per escapar del món. I tot i això, el dilluns el món va mirar cap a Sydney, on un home amb una arma va prendre ostatges en un cafè, afirmant actuar en nom de l'Estat Islàmic. Les informacions descriuen el seu autor com a Man Haron Monis, un clèric autoproclamat amb un historial d'hostilitat cap al paper militar d'Austràlia a l'Afganistan. Probablement era un solitari perillós, no part d'una cel·la terrorista organitzada. Tot i això, al final del setge, dos innocents havien mort. Aquesta no va ser la primera vegada que Austràlia es trobava davant el terrorisme. El 11-S, quan els terroristes van atacar Nova York, Melbourne va evacuar el seu WTC — no perquè fos un objectiu, sinó perquè l'horror semblava massa real. Aquell dia, tota por semblava possible. 'Som tots americans', van declarar els australians — encara que, tècnicament, ja era el 12 de setembre allà. La tragèdia, abans distància, es va fer personal. Però quan la 'Guerra contra el Terror' es va convertir en la Guerra contra l'Iraq i les banderes americanes van ondejar a les pantalles globals, va quedar clar: el 11-S va ser una història americana. Austràlia va enviar tropes a l'Afghanistan i a l'Iraq — per lealtat — però va romandre com a observadora, mirant des de lluny. El 2002, 88 australians van morir en els atacs bombes de Bali. Bali està a només sis hores de Sydney. Encara així, semblava 'un altre lloc'. Més endavant, raids policials a ciutats australianes van descobrir suposats plans terrorífics. Les autoritats van advertir: els extremitats estaven creixent dins les nostres fronteres. Austràlia viu una vida encantada. Les carreres són segures. El temps és perfecte. La gent és amable. L'oceà, diuen, manté el perill fora — o almenys el retarda. Ens queixem del preu dels cotxes o de què les sèries de Netflix arribin tard, però aquesta distància ha preservat la nostra manera de vida davant la globalització implacable. Durant més d'una dècada, hem tingut espai per debatre la llibertat contra la seguretat — sense la pressió d'una recent traumàtica nacional. Si aquest home de Sydney hagués cridat sobre impostos o el preu dels cotxes, l'anomenaríem un individu pertorbat — no un terrorista. Però la veritat és més profunda: els oceans d'Austràlia estan reduint-se. La tecnologia ara connecta un home de Bexley North amb extremists a mig món més íntimament que amb el veí de la porta de al costat. Les idees tòxiques viatgen més ràpid que qualsevol vaixell. Sigui que l'anomenem setge o terrorisme, aquest atac era alguna cosa que solia passar 'Allà Fora'. Ara és aquí. No va ser inesperat. Va arribar més tranquil·lament del que podria haver estat. Avui, la vida continua. Però el encant està desapareixent. Ja no som tant lluny.

article_content: Almost four months after 14-year-old Avonte Oquendo vanished from his school in Long Island City, his family continues a relentless search for the nonverbal autistic teen. He slipped out through an unlocked security door during lunch on October 4, 2013, and has not been seen since. Due to his condition, Avonte requires constant supervision and cannot communicate verbally, making his disappearance especially alarming. In the absence of official federal action, Avonte’s family has turned to community efforts: organizing search parties, posting flyers across subway stations and local businesses, and offering a $95,000 reward for information. Several unconfirmed sightings of boys resembling Avonte have briefly lifted spirits — but hope remains unfulfilled. On January 5, the family shared an emotional plea on their Facebook page, 'Missing Avonte Oquendo,' asking for FBI assistance. They explained that despite repeated requests, federal authorities declined to lead the investigation because New York Police Department records classify Avonte as a missing person — not a kidnapping or federal crime victim. 'We can’t force them to act,' the post read. 'But we keep asking, and we keep praying.' Avonte’s older brother, Danny Oquendo Jr., relocated from Florida to New York to lead the search full-time. His social media presence has grown rapidly, helping spread Avonte’s image worldwide — including translations into Chinese and Portuguese. Thousands have joined the campaign, sharing posts and amplifying awareness. Meanwhile, investigations revealed serious lapses at Riverview School: staff didn’t notify Avonte’s mother or police for over an hour after he left. Administrators couldn’t access surveillance footage because they lacked passwords, and no lockdown was initiated. Initially, school officials mistakenly believed Avonte had stayed inside. The Department of Education is reviewing these failures. In October, former NYPD Commissioner Ray Kelly stirred controversy by saying it was ‘unlikely’ Avonte would be found alive. He later apologized. But for the Oquendo family, every day without answers is another wound.

Es va escapar per una porta de seguretat oberta durant el dinar del 4 d’octubre de 2013 i no s’ha tornat a veure des d’aleshores. Degut a la seva condició, Avonte necessita supervisió constant i no pot comunicar-se verbalment, cosa que fa que la seva desaparició sigui especialment alarmant. En absència d’acció federal oficial, la família d’Avonte ha recorregut a esforços comunitaris: organitzant grups de cerca, col·locant fullets a les estacions del metro i a comerços locals, i oferint una recompensa de 95.000 dòlars per informació. S’han produït diverses avistaments no confirmats de nens que li recorden, que han aixecat breument les esperances — però la esperança encara no s’ha complert. Però per a la família Oquendo, cada dia sense respostes és una altra ferida.

article_content: Kolo Touré, Liverpool’s experienced defender, doesn’t buy the hype around Chelsea’s unbeaten start — not yet, anyway. While the Blues sit comfortably atop the Premier League with a four-point lead, Touré insists that matching Arsenal’s legendary 2003–04 campaign isn’t about talent alone. It’s about grit. 'You can have the best squad in the world,' he says, 'but if you crack under pressure, it all falls apart.' With only ten games played, Touré reminds everyone that seasons are marathons, not sprints. He’s seen it before — as a key member of the Invincibles himself — and knows how quickly momentum can shift. Even a single slip, like Steven Gerrard’s infamous moment last April, can change everything. That night, Chelsea’s disciplined counter-attacking style crushed Liverpool’s title dreams, and the memory still stings. Now, with Liverpool eager for revenge and Chelsea arriving as favorites, Touré expects fireworks. 'Both teams attack. Both teams want to win. This won’t be a cagey affair — it’ll be electric.' He points out that Chelsea, with stars like Diego Costa and Cesc Fàbregas firing, can’t afford to park the bus anymore. They’ve got too much firepower to play defensively. And Touré? He’s not just talking. After a standout performance in Liverpool’s 1-0 Champions League loss to Real Madrid — where he shut down Karim Benzema for long stretches — he’s pushed himself into contention to start ahead of summer signing Dejan Lovren. Manager Brendan Rodgers noticed his composure, even in defeat, and isn’t taking anyone’s place for granted. For Touré, this isn’t just another match. It’s personal. 'Last year, they took our title away. Now we get our shot. I can’t wait.' And if Liverpool pull off the upset? It might just be the moment that turns their season around.

És qüestió de coratge. 'Pots tenir el millor equip del món,' diu, 'però si et trencs sota pressió, ho perds tot.' Amb només deu partits jugats, Touré recorda a tothom que les temporades són maratons, no esprints. Ho ha vist abans — com a membre clau dels Invencibles — i sap com pot canviar ràpidament la marea. Inclus un sol error, com el famós moment de Steven Gerrard l'abril passat, pot canviar-ho tot. article_content: Unhealthy foods and sugary drinks should be taxed to encourage healthier eating and alleviate Britain’s obesity crisis, according to Dr Mike Rayner, a leading public health academic at Oxford University. Dr Rayner told the BBC that one in four British adults is obese or overweight, and the NHS spends more than £5 billion annually treating obesity-related illnesses. He proposed a 12p tax on sugary drinks, estimating it could prevent up to 2,000 premature deaths each year by prompting consumers to choose healthier alternatives. Rayner compared the proposal to existing taxes on tobacco and alcohol, noting their proven success in reducing consumption and saving lives. He criticized the UK’s current VAT system, which taxes some healthier items like smoothies but exempts high-calorie junk foods such as chips and doughnuts. Rayner advocated for a comprehensive tax on all unhealthy foods — regardless of whether they’re served hot or cold, bought from a shop or takeaway — including butter, biscuits, and pastries. He cited Denmark’s former 'fat tax' on saturated fats as a model worth emulating. While the UK government introduced a controversial 'pasty tax' on hot takeaway meals in March 2012, Rayner called the overall system 'very muddled'. In 2004, then-Prime Minister Tony Blair rejected similar proposals, warning against turning Britain into a 'nanny state'. Some MPs argue education and improved food labeling are more practical solutions. Steve Webb, then pensions minister, urged manufacturers to reduce unhealthy ingredients and said any tax should focus on public health — not revenue generation.

El doctor Rayner va dir a la BBC que una de cada quatre persones adultes britàniques és obesa o amb sobrepès, i que el NHS gasta més de 5.000 milions de lliures esterlines anualment en tractar malalties relacionades amb l'obesitat. Va proposar un impost de 12 peniques sobre les begudes sucses, estimant que podria prevenir fins a 2.000 morts prematures cada any en animar els consumidors a triar alternatives més saludables. Rayner va comparar la proposta amb impostos existents sobre el tabac i l'alcohol, assenyalant el seu èxit comprovat per reduir el consum i salvar vides. Rayner va defensar un impost integral sobre tots els aliments no saludables —sigui quina sigui la seva temperatura o procedència— incloent mantega, galetes i pastissos. Va citar l'antic 'impost de greix' de Dinamarca sobre les greixos saturats com un model digne d'emular. Tot i que el govern britànic va introduir un controvertit 'impost de la pastisseria' sobre els aliments de llevada calents el març de 2012, Rayner va qualificar el sistema global de 'molt confús'. El 2004, l'aleshores primer ministre Tony Blair va rebutjar propostes similars, advertint contra convertir el Regne Unit en un 'estat tutelar'. Alguns membres del Parlament argumenten que l'educació i una millor etiquetatge alimentari són solucions més pràctiques. Steve Webb, alors ministre de pensions, va instar els fabricants a reduir els ingredients poc saludables i va dir que qualsevol impost hauria de centrar-se en la salut pública, no en la generació d'ingressos.
